ProfileMetadata.comment: This package contains the state instruction schedule profile.
ProfileMetadata.label: StateInstructionScheduleProfile

String.description: A string consisting of a sequence of characters. The character encoding is UTF-8. The string length is unspecified and unlimited.

IdentifiedObject.description.description: The description is a free human readable text describing or naming the object. It may be non unique and may not correlate to a naming hierarchy.

IdentifiedObject.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

IdentifiedObject.name.description: The name is any free human readable and possibly non unique text naming the object.

ACEmulationControlFunctionSchedule.ACEmu.description: The control function that has this schedule.

BaseTimeSeries.actionMethod.description: Action method used to create the value. This is used for identification in the case where there is multiple time series for the same validity period and kind.

TimeSeriesInterpolationKind.linear.description: Linear interpolation is applied for values between two time points.

TimeSeriesInterpolationKind.next.description: The value between two time points is set to next value.

TimeSeriesInterpolationKind.previous.description: The value between two time points is set to previous value.

BaseTimeSeries.interpolationKind.description: Kind of interpolation done between time point.

BaseTimeSeriesKind.actual.description: Time series is actual data. The values represent measured or calculated values that represent the actual behaviour.

BaseTimeSeriesKind.forecast.description: Time series is forecast data. The values represent the result of scientific predictions based on historical time stamped data.

BaseTimeSeriesKind.hindcast.description: Time series is hindcast data. The value represent probable past (historic) condition given by calculation done using actual values. For instance, determine the among of wind based on the energy produced by wind. However, hindcast is typical the result of a simulated forecasts for historical periods.

BaseTimeSeriesKind.schedule.description: Time series is schedule data. The values represent the result of a committed and plan forecast data that has been through a quality control and could incur penalty when not followed.

ACEmulationControlFunctionTimePoint.description: AC emulation control function value for a given point in time.

ACEmulationControlFunctionTimePoint.ACEm.description: The schedule that has this time point.

DateTime.description: Date and time as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss", which conforms with ISO 8601. UTC time zone is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sssZ". A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss-hh:mm". The second component (shown here as "ss.sss") could have any number of digits in its fractional part to allow any kind of precision beyond seconds.

ACEmulationControlFunctionTimePoint.atTi.description: The time the data is valid for.

Float.description: A floating point number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

ACEmulationControlFunctionTimePoint.gain.description: Control system gain in AC transmission emulation control measured in MW/deg. It plays the role of an admittance of the equivalent AC transmission line that the control is emulating the higher is the gain the higher is the active power transfer at steady state.

ActivePower.description: Product of RMS value of the voltage and the RMS value of the in-phase component of the current.

ACEmulationControlFunctionTimePoint.refe.description: Existing active power setpoint used to calculate the active power setpoint of the AC emulation control.

ACEmulationControlFunctionTimePoint.time.description:
Control system time constant in AC transmission emulation control. It affects the time needed to 
reach a new steady state equilibrium point after a network perturbation extremely important to guarantee N-1 relief related to an interconnection. The higher is time constant the slower is the DC system dynamic.

ActivePowerControlFunctionSchedule.Activ.description: The control function that has this schedule.

ActivePowerControlFunctionTimePoint.description: Active power control function value for a given point in time.

ActivePowerControlFunctionTimePoint.Acti.description: The schedule that has this time point.

ActivePowerControlFunctionTimePoint.atTi.description: The time the data is valid for.

ActivePowerControlFunctionTimePoint.targ.description: Target value for the active power that the control function is calculating to achieve by adjusting the operational setting to the controlled equipment.

AreaReserveResourceRegularSchedule.description: Regular schedule for area reserve resource .

AreaReserveResourceRegularSchedule.AreaR.description: The resource that has a schedule.

BaseRegularIntervalSchedule.HourPattern.description: HourPattern that has base regular interval schedule.

BaseRegularIntervalSchedule.Season.description: Season associated with a base regular interval schedule.

DayOfWeekKind.bridgeDay.description: A day that is a gap between two distinguished days e.g holiday and weekend that leads to an abnormal scheduling behavior. e.g. if Ascension day falls on a Thursday, then Friday would be a bridge day due to the schedule will not have a normal Friday consumption and production.

DayOfWeekKind.friday.description: Friday as the day of the week.

DayOfWeekKind.monday.description: Monday as the day of the week.

DayOfWeekKind.publicHoliday.description: Public holiday is an officially designated day when most workplaces and schools are closed.

DayOfWeekKind.saturday.description: Saturday as the day of the week.

DayOfWeekKind.sunday.description: Sunday as the day of the week.

DayOfWeekKind.thursday.description: Thursday as the day of the week.

DayOfWeekKind.tuesday.description: Tuesday as the day of the week.

DayOfWeekKind.wednesday.description: Wednesday as the day of the week.

DayOfWeekKind.weekday.description: Day of the week other than Sunday or Saturday.

DayOfWeekKind.weekend.description: Day of the week which is Sunday or Saturday.

BaseRegularIntervalSchedule.dayOfWeek.description: Day of the week for which the schedule is valid for.

BaseRegularIntervalSchedule.intervalEndT.description: Interval end time for which the schedule is valid for.

BaseRegularIntervalSchedule.intervalStar.description: Interval start time for which the schedule is valid for.

AreaReserveResourceSchedule.AreaReserveR.description: The resource that has a schedule.

AreaReserveResourceTimePoint.description: Area reserve resource for a given point in time.

AreaReserveResourceTimePoint.AreaReserve.description: The schedule that has a time point.

AreaReserveResourceTimePoint.activatedP.description: Amount of active power currently activated for the reserve product.

AreaReserveResourceTimePoint.allocatedP.description: Amount of active power capability allocated from the associated resource to the area for the given reserve product.

AreaReserveResourceTimePoint.atTime.description: The time the data is valid for.

AreaReserveResourceTimePoint.availableP.description: Amount of active power currently available for provision of the reserve product.

AreaReserveResourceTimePoint.contractedP.description: Amount of active power contracted for the reserve product.

Boolean.description: A type with the value space "true" and "false".

AreaReserveResourceTimePoint.enabled.description: Identifies if the unit is enabled to accept a dispatch instruction. If true, the unit is enabled to accept a dispatch instruction. If false, the unit has the capability, but it is not enabled to receive a dispatch instruction.

BalancingReserveKind.aFRR.description: Automatic Frequency Restoration Reserve (aFRR). Automatically activated balancing reserve used to restore system frequency and scheduled interchanges under automatic generation control (AGC).

BalancingReserveKind.fcr.description: Frequency Containment Reserve (FCR). Automatically activated reserve that provides immediate frequency containment following small frequency deviations or disturbances.

BalancingReserveKind.mFRR.description: Manual Frequency Restoration Reserve (mFRR). Manually activated balancing reserve used to restore system balance following activation by the system operator.

AreaReserveResourceTimePoint.kind.description: Type of reserve product represented by the allocation.

Integer.description: An integer number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

AreaReserveResourceTimePoint.priority.description: Relative priority for activation or selection within an area or aggregated reserve structure.

MarketRegulationDirectionKind.down.description: Regulation activation that decreases the system’s net power injection — achieved either by decreasing generation or increasing consumption. Used for down-regulation bids or activations.

MarketRegulationDirectionKind.stable.description: No activation or neutral position; used for capacity or reserve states that maintain stability without a directional effect (e.g., system in balanced or standby mode).

MarketRegulationDirectionKind.up.description: Regulation activation that increases the system’s net power injection — achieved either by increasing generation or decreasing consumption. Used for up-regulation bids or activations.

MarketRegulationDirectionKind.upAndDown.description: Product or capacity symmetrical for both up- and down-regulation; the same magnitude applies in both directions. Common for bidirectional balancing services (e.g., symmetrical aFRR capacity).

AssessedElementRegularSchedule.AssessedE.description: Assessed Element that has regular schedules.

AssessedElementRegularTimePoint.description: Assessed element instruction value at a given point in time.

AssessedElementRegularTimePoint.Assessed.description: Assessed element regular schedule which has assessed element regular time points.

PerCent.description: Percentage on a defined base.   For example, specify as 100 to indicate at the defined base.

AssessedElementRegularTimePoint.appointe.description:
The percentage (appointed to a region) of the remaining margin obtained in the grid model to reach its current limit. The maximum percentage shall by default be 10% of the remaining margin.
It is only used when an assessed element is considered conservative for a region.
The allowed value range is [0,100].

AssessedElementRegularTimePoint.enabled.description: It identifies if the assessed element is enabled. True means enabled, False means disabled.

AssessedElementRegularTimePoint.maxFlow.description: Maximum flow on an a conducting equipment or a collection of conducting equipment forming a power transfer corridor. For assessed elements that is becomes critical due to contingency, this value represents the maximum flow with remedial action taken into consideration.

AssessedElementRegularTimePoint.positive.description:
A margin defined only for scanned AssessedElement (If AssessedElement.ScannedForRegion is present) in order to represent the influence of available remedial action which is not cross-border relevant remedial action.
The margin is modifying the limits used for the assessment whatever the limit it is (e.g. PATL, TATL).This symbolizes a remedial action that can be applied internally by the System Operator. It will be resolved by the System Operator and not by the optimization of remedial actions. The attribute shall be a positive value.
The allowed value range is [0,100].

AssessedElementRegularTimePoint.scannedT.description:
Threshold percentage that a scanned element can be overloaded, on a given element, on top of any overload prior to optimisation (default= 5%). e.g. Initial loading of the element is 110%, with a 5% scanned threshold margin, the new maximum is 115% of the limit (e.g. PATL, TATL, etc).
The allowed value range is [0,100].

AssessedElementSchedule.AssessedElement.description: Assessed element which has an assessed element schedule.

AssessedElementTimePoint.description: Assessed element instruction value at a given point in time.

AssessedElementTimePoint.AssessedElement.description: The assessed element schedule that has this time point.

AssessedElementTimePoint.appointedMargin.description:
The percentage (appointed to a region) of the remaining margin obtained in the grid model to reach its current limit. The maximum percentage shall by default be 10% of the remaining margin.
It is only used when an assessed element is considered conservative for a region.
The allowed value range is [0,100].

AssessedElementTimePoint.atTime.description: The time the data is valid for.

AssessedElementTimePoint.coordinatedVali.description: A positive value expressed in MW, calculated and provided by the coordinated capacity calculator (CCC) for the reduction of Remaining Available Margin (RAM) in order to ensure grid security.

A text description provided by the coordinated capacity calculator (CCC) for justifying the reduction of Remaining Available Margin (RAM) by means of Coordinated Validation Adjustment (CVA). This justification is not intended for any application processing purpose, it should only be used for reporting.

AssessedElementTimePoint.criticalElement.description: Justification indicating the kind of critical element contingency. This justification is not intended for any application processing purpose, it should only be used for reporting.

AssessedElementTimePoint.enabled.description: It identifies if the assessed element is enabled. True means enabled, False means disabled.

SecuredExclusionReasonKind.capacityCalcu.description: The network element that is going to be assessed is excluded for being secured by the capacity calculation region.

SecuredExclusionReasonKind.nonNativeCapa.description: The network element that is going to be assessed is excluded for being secured for the native capacity calculation region since it would be secured for a non native capacity calculation region.

SecuredExclusionReasonKind.systemOperato.description: The network element that is going to be assessed is excluded for being secured by the system operator.

AssessedElementTimePoint.exclusionReason.description: Reason for not associating this assessed element with a secured region.

AssessedElementTimePoint.individualValid.description: A positive value expressed in MW, calculated and provided by System Operators from their individual validation process for the reduction of Remaining Available Margin in order to ensure grid security.

A text description provided by System Operators for justifying the reduction of Remaining Available Margin (RAM) by means of Individual Validation Adjustment (IVA). This justification is not intended for any application processing purpose, it should only be used for reporting.

A positive value expressed in MW, calculated by the coordinated capacity calculator (CCC) based on the provided Individual Validation Adjustment (IVA) by System Operators in order to show the actual reduction of Remaining Available Margin (RAM). Individual Validation Adjustment Share is a positive non-zero value. It is equal or less than the Individual Validation Adjustment value.

AssessedElementTimePoint.maxFlow.description: Maximum flow on an a conducting equipment or a collection of conducting equipment forming a power transfer corridor. For assessed elements that is becomes critical due to contingency, this value represents the maximum flow with remedial action taken into consideration.

AssessedElementTimePoint.positiveVirtual.description:
A margin defined only for scanned AssessedElement (If AssessedElement.ScannedForRegion is present) in order to represent the influence of available remedial action which is not cross-border relevant remedial action.
The margin is modifying the limits used for the assessment whatever the limit it is (e.g. PATL, TATL).This symbolizes a remedial action that can be applied internally by the System Operator. It will be resolved by the System Operator and not by the optimization of remedial actions. The attribute shall be a positive value.
The allowed value range is [0,100].

AssessedElementTimePoint.scannedThreshol.description:
Threshold percentage that a scanned element can be overloaded, on a given element, on top of any overload prior to optimisation (default= 5%). e.g. Initial loading of the element is 110%, with a 5% scanned threshold margin, the new maximum is 115% of the limit (e.g. PATL, TATL, etc).
The allowed value range is [0,100].

AssessedElementTimePoint.targetRemaining.description: Justification indicating the target remaining available margin. This justification is not intended for any application processing purpose, it should only be used for reporting.

AvailabilityTimePoint.description: Availability instruction value at a given point in time.

AvailabilityTimePoint.GenericAvailabilit.description: The availability schedule which belongs to the availability timepoint.

AvailabilityTimePoint.atTime.description: The time the data is valid for.

AvailabilityTimePoint.available.description: It identifies if the element is available. True means available, False means unavailable.

BaseCaseCurrentLimitSchedule.description: The schedule for a base case current limit.

BaseCaseCurrentLimitSchedule.BaseCaseCur.description: Base case current limit which has base case current limit schedule.

BaseCaseCurrentLimitTimePoint.description: Base case current limit at a given point in time.

BaseCaseCurrentLimitTimePoint.BaseCaseCu.description: Base case current limit schedule that has time point.

BaseCaseCurrentLimitTimePoint.atTime.description: The time the data is valid for.

CurrentFlow.description: Electrical current with sign convention: positive flow is out of the conducting equipment into the connectivity node. Can be both AC and DC.

BaseCaseCurrentLimitTimePoint.value.description: Value of current limit. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.ClimateZone.description: The climate zone that has regular schedule.

Decimal.description: Decimal is the base-10 notational system for representing real numbers.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.avalancheDang.description:
An index representing the avalanche danger for the corresponding time interval.
Note: The applicable avalanche danger methodology and classification are identified through the associated data provenance. The CIM model does not prescribe a particular avalanche danger scale. Where the index represents categorical danger levels, the numerical values shall not be assumed to form a linear scale.
Example: Using the European Avalanche Danger Scale: "1" (Low), "2" (Moderate), "3" (Considerable), "4" (High), "5" (Very high).

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.cloudCover.description: The proportion of the sky covered by cloud for the corresponding time interval.

Temperature.description: Value of temperature in degrees Celsius.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.dewPointTempA.description: The dew-point temperature at 2 metres above ground level for the corresponding time interval.

Irradiance.description:
Power carried by electromagnetic radiation incident on a surface per unit area.

Note: Intended for solar irradiance values such as global, direct and diffuse solar irradiance.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.diffuseSolarI.description: The diffuse solar irradiance for the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.directSolarIr.description: The direct solar irradiance for the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.droughtCode.description:
The Drought Code for the corresponding time interval.
Note: The Drought Code is a component of the Canadian Fire Weather Index System representing the moisture condition of deep, compact organic fuel layers. It is particularly useful for representing the cumulative effect of prolonged dry conditions and seasonal drought on wildfire potential. Higher values indicate drier conditions. The attribute is used when the applicable wildfire methodology provides a Drought Code.
Example: Values such as "15", "300" and "600" represent progressively drier conditions in the Drought Code scale. No universal low, moderate or high classification is implied by these example values; interpretation is provided by the applicable methodology and provenance.

Length.description: Unit of length. It shall be a positive value or zero.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.evaporation.description:
The evaporation and evapotranspiration during the corresponding time interval, expressed as an equivalent depth of water.
Note: The sign convention, where relevant, is defined by the applicable data specification.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.fireWeatherIn.description:
A fire-weather index indicating the meteorological conditions relevant to wildfire danger for the corresponding time interval.
Note: The applicable fire-weather index methodology and classification are identified through the associated data provenance. The CIM model does not prescribe a specific wildfire classification. The Canadian Fire Weather Index (FWI) System, as used by European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS), is one example. In this system, the index combines fuel-moisture and fire-behaviour components derived from temperature, relative humidity, wind speed and precipitation. Higher values indicate conditions increasingly favourable to intense wildfire.
Example: Using the EFFIS classification: "5.0" (Very low), "10.0" (Low), "15.0" (Moderate), "37.77" (High), "40.01" (Very high), "55.55" (Extreme).

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.freezingPreci.description: The number of days with freezing precipitation within the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.frostDays.description: The number of frost days within the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.globalSolarIr.description:
The global solar irradiance for the corresponding time interval.
Note: Global solar irradiance represents the total direct and diffuse solar power incident per unit area on the applicable reference surface. It may be used as an environmental input for applications such as photovoltaic production and thermal rating of overhead conductors. The orientation of the reference surface is defined by the applicable dataset or provenance information.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.hailDays.description: The number of days on which hail occurs within the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.heatwaveDays.description: The number of days occurring as part of a heatwave within the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.hotDays.description: The number of days meeting the applicable hot-day criterion within the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.hydroInflow.description:
The energy equivalent of natural hydro inflow associated with hydro resources in the ClimateZone during the corresponding time interval.
Note: The value represents inflow energy for the interval. For example, a weekly TimePoint may contain the natural hydro inflow energy for that week.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.icingDays.description: The number of days meeting the applicable icing criterion within the corresponding time interval.

CountPerArea.description:
Number of discrete occurrences or events per unit area.

Note: Intended for spatial event densities such as lightning density. A new UnitSymbol countPerm2 is required if this quantity is represented as a CIMDatatype with an explicit unit.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.lightningDens.description: The number of lightning events per unit area occurring during the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.maxTempAt2m.description:
The maximum air temperature at 2 metres above ground level during the corresponding time interval.
Note: This time series is intended for datasets providing maximum temperature directly.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.minTempAt2m.description:
The minimum air temperature at 2 metres above ground level during the corresponding time interval.
Note: This time series is intended for datasets providing minimum temperature directly, for example daily minimum temperature. It is not required when the minimum can appropriately be derived from tempAt2m.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.populationWei.description:
The population-weighted air temperature at 2 metres above ground level for the corresponding time interval.
Note: The value is derived by spatially weighting the air temperature within the represented area by the population distribution. It may be used for modelling temperature-dependent energy consumption, including heating and cooling demand. The population dataset and weighting method are identified through the applicable provenance information.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.potentialEvap.description: The potential evaporation during the corresponding time interval, expressed as an equivalent depth of water.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.precipitation.description:
The total precipitation received during the corresponding time interval.
Note: The value represents accumulated precipitation expressed as an equivalent depth of water.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.rainfall.description:
The amount of liquid precipitation received during the corresponding time interval.
Note: The value represents accumulated rainfall expressed as an equivalent depth of water.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.relativeHumid.description: The relative humidity at 2 metres above ground level for the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.runoff.description: The runoff during the corresponding time interval, expressed as an equivalent depth of water over the area.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.seaCurrentDir.description:
The direction of the sea-water current for the corresponding time interval.
Note: Current direction normally identifies the direction towards which the water is moving, unlike meteorological wind direction, which identifies the direction from which the wind originates.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.seaCurrentSpe.description:
The speed of the sea-water current for the corresponding time interval.
Note: The applicable depth or vertical reference is defined by the source dataset or provenance information.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.seaIceConcent.description:
The proportion of the sea surface covered by sea ice for the corresponding time interval.
Note: Sea-ice concentration provides the time-dependent information needed to determine sea-ice presence and extent. It replaces a simple integer seaIce value, which cannot distinguish between partial and complete ice coverage.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.seaIceThickne.description: The sea-ice thickness for the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.seaSurfaceTem.description: The sea-surface temperature for the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.significantWa.description: The significant wave height for the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.snowWater.description:
The amount of water stored in the snowpack at the corresponding time, expressed as an equivalent depth of liquid water.
Example: January = 180 mm, March = 430 mm, May = 160 mm, June = 0 mm.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.snowfall.description: The solid precipitation received during the corresponding time interval, expressed as its equivalent amount of liquid water.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.snowmelt.description: The amount of water released by melting snow during the corresponding time interval, expressed as an equivalent depth of liquid water.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.sunshineDurat.description: The duration of sunshine during the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.surfacePressu.description:
The atmospheric pressure at the surface for the corresponding time interval.
Note: Surface pressure may be relevant when determining air density for wind-energy calculations.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.tempAt2m.description: The air temperature at 2 metres above ground level for the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.thunderDays.description: The number of days on which thunder is observed within the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneRegularSchedule.tropicalNight.description: The number of nights meeting the applicable tropical-night criterion within the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.avalancheDangerInde.description:
An index representing the avalanche danger for the corresponding time interval.
Note: The applicable avalanche danger methodology and classification are identified through the associated data provenance. The CIM model does not prescribe a particular avalanche danger scale. Where the index represents categorical danger levels, the numerical values shall not be assumed to form a linear scale.
Example: Using the European Avalanche Danger Scale: "1" (Low), "2" (Moderate), "3" (Considerable), "4" (High), "5" (Very high).

ClimateZoneTimePoint.dewPointTempAt2m.description: The dew-point temperature at 2 metres above ground level for the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.directSolarIrradian.description: The direct solar irradiance for the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.droughtCode.description:
The Drought Code for the corresponding time interval.
Note: The Drought Code is a component of the Canadian Fire Weather Index System representing the moisture condition of deep, compact organic fuel layers. It is particularly useful for representing the cumulative effect of prolonged dry conditions and seasonal drought on wildfire potential. Higher values indicate drier conditions. The attribute is used when the applicable wildfire methodology provides a Drought Code.
Example: Values such as "15", "300" and "600" represent progressively drier conditions in the Drought Code scale. No universal low, moderate or high classification is implied by these example values; interpretation is provided by the applicable methodology and provenance.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.evaporation.description:
The evaporation and evapotranspiration during the corresponding time interval, expressed as an equivalent depth of water.
Note: The sign convention, where relevant, is defined by the applicable data specification.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.fireWeatherIndex.description:
A fire-weather index indicating the meteorological conditions relevant to wildfire danger for the corresponding time interval.
Note: The applicable fire-weather index methodology and classification are identified through the associated data provenance. The CIM model does not prescribe a specific wildfire classification. The Canadian Fire Weather Index (FWI) System, as used by European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS), is one example. In this system, the index combines fuel-moisture and fire-behaviour components derived from temperature, relative humidity, wind speed and precipitation. Higher values indicate conditions increasingly favourable to intense wildfire.
Example: Using the EFFIS classification: "5.0" (Very low), "10.0" (Low), "15.0" (Moderate), "37.77" (High), "40.01" (Very high), "55.55" (Extreme).

ClimateZoneTimePoint.freezingPrecipitati.description: The number of days with freezing precipitation within the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.frostDays.description: The number of frost days within the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.globalSolarIrradian.description:
The global solar irradiance for the corresponding time interval.
Note: Global solar irradiance represents the total direct and diffuse solar power incident per unit area on the applicable reference surface. It may be used as an environmental input for applications such as photovoltaic production and thermal rating of overhead conductors. The orientation of the reference surface is defined by the applicable dataset or provenance information.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.hailDays.description: The number of days on which hail occurs within the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.heatwaveDays.description: The number of days occurring as part of a heatwave within the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.hotDays.description: The number of days meeting the applicable hot-day criterion within the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.hydroInflow.description:

ClimateZoneTimePoint.icingDays.description: The number of days meeting the applicable icing criterion within the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.lightningDensity.description: The number of lightning events per unit area occurring during the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.maxTempAt2m.description:

Note: This time series is intended for datasets providing maximum temperature directly.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.minTempAt2m.description:
The minimum air temperature at 2 metres above ground level during the corresponding time interval.
Note: This time series is intended for datasets providing minimum temperature directly, for example daily minimum temperature. It is not required when the minimum can appropriately be derived from tempAt2m.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.populationWeightedT.description:
The population-weighted air temperature at 2 metres above ground level for the corresponding time interval.
Note: The value is derived by spatially weighting the air temperature within the represented area by the population distribution. It may be used for modelling temperature-dependent energy consumption, including heating and cooling demand. The population dataset and weighting method are identified through the applicable provenance information.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.potentialEvaporatio.description: The potential evaporation during the corresponding time interval, expressed as an equivalent depth of water.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.precipitation.description:

Note: The value represents accumulated precipitation expressed as an equivalent depth of water.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.rainfall.description:

Note: The value represents accumulated rainfall expressed as an equivalent depth of water.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.relativeHumidityAt2.description: The relative humidity at 2 metres above ground level for the corresponding time interval.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.runoff.description: The runoff during the corresponding time interval, expressed as an equivalent depth of water over the area.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.seaCurrentDirection.description:

ClimateZoneTimePoint.seaCurrentSpeed.description:

Note: The applicable depth or vertical reference is defined by the source dataset or provenance information.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.seaIceConcentration.description:

Example: January = 180 mm, March = 430 mm, May = 160 mm, June = 0 mm.

ClimateZoneTimePoint.surfacePressure.description:

EnergyResourceGroupCapacityRegularSchedu.description: The energy resource group capacity that has a regular schedule.

The ratio (in percent) between the effective available capacity and the installed capacity over a defined time interval. For weather-dependent resources, the value reflects climate-driven availability as derived from meteorological or hydrological conditions.

The weather or condition-dependent active power capacity that is realistically available for operation at a given time. This value reflects reductions due to climatic, hydrological, or operational constraints.

The relative weighting used to allocate an aggregate capacity requirement to this energy resource group on a time-series basis. 

Note: The values provide context-specific top-down capacity allocation weightings and may override normalCapacityAllocationFactor. Each value applies to the corresponding time interval represented by the time-series context. The factors are relative weights and are not required to represent percentages or to sum to 1. The allocation algorithm may normalize or otherwise adjust the applicable factors according to availability, existing capacity and other modelling constraints.

The nominal installed active power capacity of the energy type, independent of weather or operating conditions. This is the maximum technical power rating under standard design assumptions and optimum operation condition.

The effective active power capacity for the resource at the specified time, after considering all applied deratings, outages, operational limits, or weather influences. This value represents the usable capacity that can be delivered or consumed, effective capacity.
Participation factor for the power group in relation to scheduling area. Must be a positive value.

GridStateAlterationTimePoint.participati.description:
Participation factor describing the entity part of the active power provided by a collection of entities (e.g. an active power forecast to a collection of entities is divided to each of the member entity according to the participation factor). Must be a positive value.
In the case of a sharing strategy, the distribution is following entities value (V) equals aggregated value (T) divided by sum of participation factors (PF), i.e. V=T/sum(PF). 
In the case of priority strategy, the item with the lowest number gets allocated energy first.
e.g. If 0 this grid alteration does not participate. The sum of all participation factors for all grid state alterations associated with same remedial action shall be equal to 100%.

PowerBidDependency.description:
A peer temporal dependency that defines temporal or operational constraints between two power bid schedules.
Note: The dependency constrains activation or deactivation of the dependent power bid schedule relative to activation or deactivation of the dependee power bid schedule. Lag constraints are evaluated from the latest applicable activation or deactivation of the dependee. A subsequent state change of the dependee supersedes the previous reference transition if the corresponding transition of the dependent has not yet occurred.
Example:
- startToStartLag = 15M, startToStartLagKind = exact: the dependent bid is activated exactly 15 minutes after activation of the dependee bid, provided the dependee has not subsequently changed state.
- finishToStartLag = 30M, finishToStartLagKind = minimum: the dependent bid may be activated no earlier than 30 minutes after deactivation of the dependee bid.
- finishToFinishLag = 15M, finishToFinishLagKind = maximum: the dependent bid shall be deactivated no later than 15 minutes after deactivation of the dependee bid.

DependencyConstraintKind.exclusive.description: The dependee and dependent shall not both be active or effective at the same time.

DependencyConstraintKind.inclusive.description: The dependent shall only be active or effective while the dependee is active or effective.

DependencyConstraintKind.restrictive.description:
The dependee constrains the dependent without requiring the dependent to become active or effective.
Note: A restrictive dependency defines temporal or operational constraints on the behaviour of the dependent while leaving its activation or operation optional.

PeerTemporalDependency.constraintKind.description:
The kind of temporal or operational constraint defined between the dependee and the dependent.
Note: Certain dependency constraint kinds may require or prohibit the use of temporal constraint attributes, depending on the semantics of the specialization.

Duration.description: Duration as "PnYnMnDTnHnMnS" which conforms to ISO 8601, where nY expresses a number of years, nM a number of months, nD a number of days. The letter T separates the date expression from the time expression and, after it, nH identifies a number of hours, nM a number of minutes and nS a number of seconds. The number of seconds could be expressed as a decimal number, but all other numbers are integers.

PeerTemporalDependency.finishToFinishLag.description: The duration constraining the next finish or deactivation of the dependent relative to the latest applicable finish or deactivation of the dependee.

ReferenceValueKind.exact.description: The referenced value is to be met exactly.

ReferenceValueKind.maximum.description: The referenced value establishes a upper bound.

ReferenceValueKind.minimum.description: The referenced value establishes a lower bound.

PeerTemporalDependency.finishToFinishLag.description:
Specifies whether finishToFinishLag is an exact, minimum, or maximum temporal constraint.
Note: This attribute shall be specified when finishToFinishLag is provided.
Example: finishToFinishLag = 2D1H30M is interpreted together with finishToFinishLagKind:
- exact: the dependent finishes exactly 2 days, 1 hour and 30 minutes after the latest applicable finish of the dependee.
- minimum: the dependent may finish no earlier than 2 days, 1 hour and 30 minutes after the latest applicable finish of the dependee.
- maximum: the dependent shall finish no later than 2 days, 1 hour and 30 minutes after the latest applicable finish of the dependee.
In all cases, the dependee finish remains applicable only while the dependee remains in the state resulting from that finish. If the dependee subsequently changes state before the dependent finishes, the applicability of the previous finish is re-evaluated.

PeerTemporalDependency.finishToStartLag.description: The duration constraining the next start or activation of the dependent relative to the latest applicable finish or deactivation of the dependee.

PeerTemporalDependency.finishToStartLagK.description:
Specifies whether finishToStartLag is an exact, minimum, or maximum temporal constraint.
Note: This attribute shall be specified when finishToStartLag is provided.
Example: finishToStartLag = 20M is interpreted together with finishToStartLagKind:
- exact: the dependent starts exactly 20 minutes after the latest applicable finish of the dependee.
- minimum: the dependent may start no earlier than 20 minutes after the latest applicable finish of the dependee.
- maximum: the dependent shall start no later than 20 minutes after the latest applicable finish of the dependee.
In all cases, the dependee finish remains applicable only while the dependee remains in the state resulting from that finish. If the dependee subsequently changes state before the dependent starts, the constraint is evaluated from the next applicable finish of the dependee.

PeerTemporalDependency.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

PeerTemporalDependency.overlap.description: The duration constraining the period for which the dependee and dependent are simultaneously active or effective.

PeerTemporalDependency.overlapKind.description:
Specifies whether overlap is an exact, minimum, or maximum duration of simultaneous activity or effectiveness.
Note: This attribute shall be specified when overlap is provided.
Example: overlap = 1H28M45S is interpreted together with overlapKind:
- exact: the dependee and dependent are simultaneously active or effective for exactly 1 hour, 28 minutes, and 45 seconds.
- minimum: the dependee and dependent shall be simultaneously active or effective for at least 1 hour, 28 minutes, and 45 seconds.
- maximum: the dependee and dependent shall be simultaneously active or effective for no more than 1 hour, 28 minutes, and 45 seconds.
Unlike the lag attributes, overlap constrains the duration of a simultaneous state rather than the temporal separation between two state transitions.

PeerTemporalDependency.startToStartLag.description: The duration constraining the next start or activation of the dependent relative to the latest applicable start or activation of the dependee.

PeerTemporalDependency.startToStartLagKi.description:
Specifies whether startToStartLag is an exact, minimum, or maximum temporal constraint.
Note: This attribute shall be specified when startToStartLag is provided.
Example: startToStartLag = 2H is interpreted together with startToStartLagKind:
- exact: the dependent starts exactly 2 hours after the latest applicable start of the dependee.
- minimum: the dependent may start no earlier than 2 hours after the latest applicable start of the dependee.
- maximum: the dependent shall start no later than 2 hours after the latest applicable start of the dependee.
In all cases, the dependee start remains applicable only while the dependee remains in the state resulting from that start. If the dependee subsequently changes state before the dependent starts, the constraint is evaluated from the next applicable start of the dependee.

Dataset.description: A collection of data, published or curated by a single source, and available for access or download in one or more representations.

URI.description: Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) or URI Reference as defined by [RFC 3986], including amendments from [RFC 6874] for IPv6 zone identifiers. The value may be absolute or relative and can include an optional fragment identifier. This datatype is used to indicate that the value fulfills the role of a URI or URI Reference, providing a consistent format for referencing abstract or physical resources.

accessRights.description:
Information about who access the resource or an indication of its security status. Access Rights may include information regarding access or restrictions based on privacy, security, or other policies.
[CIM context:
Reference to the confidentiality level that shall be applied when handling this model.].

accrualPeriodicity.description:
The frequency with which items are added to a collection.
[CIM context:
Reference to the time frame.].

conformsTo.description:
An established standard to which the described resource conforms.
[CIM context:
An IRI describing the profile that governs this model. It uniquely identifies the profile and its version. Multiple instances of the property describe all standards or specifications to which the model and the document representing this model conform to.
A document would normally conform to profile definitions, the constraints that relate to the profile and/or the set of business specific constrains. A reference to a machine- readable constraints or specification indicates that the document was tested against these constraints and it conforms to them.].

LangString.description: Datatype that conforms to rdf:langString, representing a textual value with an associated language tag, following BCP 47 language conventions (e.g., en, fr-CA, no-NB).

description.description:
A free-text account of the resource.
Description may include but is not limited to: an abstract, a table of contents, a graphical representation, or a free-text account of the resource.

hasPart.description: The dataset which is part of another dataset.

UUID.description: Datatype representing a unique identifier in the form of a universally unique identifier (UUID). The value must conform to the UUID format as defined in RFC 4122, allowing for globally unique identification of entities.

identifier.description:
A unique identifier of the resource being described or cataloged.
The identifier might be used as part of the IRI of the resource, but still having it represented explicitly is useful.
The identifier is a text string which is assigned to the resource to provide an unambiguous reference within a particular context.
[CIM context:
A unique identifier of the model which is serialised in the document where the header is located. The identifier is persistent for a given version of the model and shall change when the model changes.
If a model is serialized as complete (full) model or as difference model exchange the identifier shall be the same. The identifier shall not be used as an identifier of the document which can be different for a given version of a model.].

issued.description:
Date of formal issuance of the resource.
Recommended practice is to describe the date, date/time, or period of time as recommended for the property Date, of which this is a subproperty.
[CIM context:
Reference to the date that the complete data set was made valid/available.].

license.description:
A legal document giving official permission to do something with the resource. Recommended practice is to identify the license document with a URI. If this is not possible or feasible, a literal value that identifies the license may be provided.
[CIM context:
Reference to the license under which the data is made available. If no license holder is defined, then the original data provider holds the license.].

publisher.description:
An entity responsible for making the resource available.
[CIM context: 
The agent that is publishing the dataset on the given platform.]

references.description:
A related resource that is referenced, cited, or otherwise pointed to by the described resource[.
[CIM context: 
The referenced resource that is being complemented in this dataset, e.g. SSH is referencing EQ.]

replaces.description:
A related resource that is supplanted, displaced, or superseded by the described resource
[CIM context: 
The referenced dataset is being replaced by this dataset.]

requires.description: A related resource that is required by the described resource to support its function, delivery, or coherence.

rights.description: A statement that concerns all rights not addressed with dct:license or dct:accessRights, such as copyright statements.

rightsHolder.description:
Information about rights held in and over the resource.
Typically, rights information includes a statement about various property rights associated with the resource, including intellectual property rights. Recommended practice is to refer to a rights statement with a URI. If this is not possible or feasible, a literal value (name, label, or short text) may be provided.

source.description:
A related resource from which the described resource is derived.
This property is intended to be used with non-literal values. The described resource may be derived from the related resource in whole or in part. Best practice is to identify the related resource by means of a URI or a string conforming to a formal identification system.

spatial.description:
The geographical area covered by the dataset.
[CIM context: 
The responsibility area that multiple model can describe, also referred to frame.].

title.description: A name given to the resource.

type.description: The nature or genre of the resource. Recommended practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as the DCMI Type Vocabulary [DCMI-TYPE]. To describe the file format, physical medium, or dimensions of the resource, use the property Format.

versionNotes.description: A description of changes between this version and the previous version of the resource.

DateTimeStamp.description: Position of an instant, expressed using xsd:dateTimeStamp, in which the time-zone field is mandatory.

endDate.description:

[CIM context:
The end date and time of the validity period of the model that it is serialized in the document where the header is located. It is only used in relation to the startDate property which indicates the beginning of the validity period of the model.].

inSeries.description: A dataset series of which the dataset is part.

isVersionOf.description:
This resource has a more specific, versioned resource. This property is intended for relating a non-versioned or abstract resource to several versioned resources, e.g., snapshots.

The notion of version used by this property is limited to versions resulting from revisions occurring to a resource as part of its life-cycle. Therefore, its semantics is more specific than its super-property dcterms:hasVersion, which makes use of a broader notion of version, including editions and adaptations.

keyword.description:
A keyword or tag describing a resource.
[CIM context:
The intended content type of the model, usually the profile keyword. Used to identify what profiles and content is expected in the document, e.g., Equipment, Boundary, SSH, AE, etc. The same keyword is used for different versions of same profile. It can be also used to identify different content based on the same profile.
For instance, as the equipment profile can be used for both boundary data and equipment not related to boundary, the keyword is different to indicate that boundary data is exchanged. In order to avoid ambiguity the property is not exchanged in cases where the document contains multiple profiles referenced by dcterms:conformsTo.].

nextVersion.description: The next version for the resource.

previousVersion.description:
The previous version of a resource in a lineage.
This property is meant to be used to specify a version chain, consisting of snapshots of a resource.

The notion of version used by this property is limited to versions resulting from revisions occurring to a resource as part of its life-cycle. One of the typical cases here is representing the history of the versions of a dataset that have been released over time.

startDate.description:
This property contains the start of the period.
[CIM context:
The date and time that this model represents, i.e. for which the model is (or was) valid. It indicates the beginning of the validity period. It is indicating either an instant (in cases where the model is only valid for a point in time) or the start time of a period. If not provided the model is considered valid for any time stamp. The format is an extended format according to the ISO 8601-2005. European exchanges shall refer to UTC.].

applicationSoftware.description:

alternativeVersionOf.description:

This property is intended for relating a versioned resource to a non-versioned or abstract resource at the same time express that multiple versions exist.
dcatcim:alternativeVersionOf is a specialisation of dcat:isVersionOf with the restriction that the resource shall have a preferred version (dcatcim:preferredVersion) so that the preferred dataset can be used when there is no need to access all alternative versions.

Integer.description: An integer number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

AvailabilitySchedule.priority.description: Value 0 means ignore priority. 1 means the highest priority, 2 is the second highest priority.

CountertradeScheduleAction.description: Countertrade schedule action is an action to rearrange power schedules based on a Generation and Load Shift Key (GLSK) strategy.

PowerScheduleAction.PowerSchedule.description: Power schedule which contains the power schedule action.

EventSchedule.RemedialActionSchedule.description: Remedial action schedule is the event that is validity for the given time series.

DateTime.description: Date and time as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss", which conforms with ISO 8601. UTC time zone is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sssZ". A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss-hh:mm". The second component (shown here as "ss.sss") could have any number of digits in its fractional part to allow any kind of precision beyond seconds.

EventTimePoint.isActive.description: True, if the event is occurring (Active) at this time point. Otherwise false.

GenericValueTimePoint.description: Generic value for a given point in time.

GenericValueTimePoint.atTime.description: The time the data is valid for.

In case of boolean 1.0 equals true and 0.0 equals false. In case of integer the 0 should be included as a decimal, e.g. 2.0.

GridStateIntensitySchedule.description: Defines the intensity applied for a given grid state alteration. It is primarily used in exchanges related to the remedial action schedule. The value provided by the schedule replaces the value of the attribute to which the schedule refers to.

GenericValueSchedule.RemedialActionSched.description: Remedial action schedule which has generic value schedules.

GridStateIntensitySchedule.GridStateAlte.description: The grid state alteration which has intensity.

PowerSchedule.description: Time series represent irregular power, active and reactive, values at given points in time.

PowerSchedule.currency.description: Currency the energy price is given in.

PowerTimePoint.description: Time series represent irregular values at given points in time.

PowerTimePoint.PowerSchedule.description: Time series the time point values belongs to.

ActivePower.description: Product of RMS value of the voltage and the RMS value of the in-phase component of the current.

PowerTimePoint.activatedP.description: Active power activated as part of redispatch. Negative number means that the value is scheduling down. Positive number means that the value is scheduling up.

PowerTimePoint.activatedPrice.description: Price for the activated active power per unit e.g. per MW.

PowerTimePoint.atTime.description: The time the data is valid for.

PowerTimePoint.p.description: Active power injection. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node or area.

PowerTimePoint.price.description: Price for the scheduled active power per unit of active power. e.g. per MW.

ReactivePower.description: Product of RMS value of the voltage and the RMS value of the quadrature component of the current.

PowerTimePoint.q.description: Reactive power injection. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node or area.

ProposingRemedialActionScheduleShare.description: Proposing entity (System Operator) with a proper cost share for a given remedial action schedule.

ProposingRemedialActionScheduleShare.Pro.description: Proposing entity making the proposing remedial action schedule share.

ProposingRemedialActionScheduleShare.Rem.description: Remedial action schedule proposed by the proposing entity.

ProposingRemedialActionScheduleShare.cos.description: Sharing factor of the cost of the remedial action as a  fraction of the total cost, i.e. system operator's cost = cost x (costSharingFactor / sum of all costSharingFactor).

ProposingRemedialActionScheduleShare.mRI.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

RedispatchScheduleAction.description: Redispatch schedule action is an action to rearrange power schedules for a scheduled resource to obtain a feasible and secure operational state of the power electricity system.

RemedialActionCost.description: Remedial action cost is the total cost itemised cost by category and type for the remedial action.

RemedialActionCost.RemedialActionSchedul.description: Remedial action schedule for which this remedial action cost relates to.

RemedialActionCost.costAllocationTime.description: Cost allocation time is the time the cost shall be allocated.

CostSettledKind.final.description: Final cost. For instance, the cost is not expected to be changed on a later stage.

RemedialActionCost.kind.description: Remedial action cost category related to the confirmation of the cost in regards to changes.

RemedialActionCost.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

RemedialActionCost.operationalCost.description: Operational cost is the total cost directly related to operate the unit according to the remedial action, e.g. fuel cost.

RemedialActionCost.opportunityCost.description: Opportunity cost is the total cost of potential earning that is missed due to performing the remedial action.

RemedialActionCost.otherCost.description: Other cost is the total cost that cannot be directly allocated to any of the other items.

RemedialActionCost.processingFee.description: Processing fee is the total cost for processing the remedial action.

RemedialActionCost.savedFuelCost.description: Saved fuel cost is the total saving due to not consuming the expected fuel as part of the remedial action.

RemedialActionCost.shutdownCost.description: Shutdown cost is the total cost for shutting down a unit as part of the remedial action.

RemedialActionCost.startupCost.description: Start-up cost is the total cost for activating the remedial action, e.g. if a generator needs to be started before it can perform the remedial action.

RemedialActionSchedule.description: A schedule for a determined remedial action.

RemedialActionSchedule.AssignedRegion.description: The assigned region for this remedial action schedule.

RemedialActionSchedule.Contingency.description: The contingency for a curative remedial action schedule.

RemedialActionSchedule.ProposingEntity.description: The security coordinator that is proposing this remedial action schedule.

RemedialActionSchedule.RemedialAction.description: The remedial action that has a remedial action schedule associated.

RemedialActionScheduleStatusKind.agreeme.description: The agreement is validated for the remedial action schedule.

RemedialActionScheduleStatusKind.impleme.description: An ordered remedial action is implemented.

RemedialActionScheduleStatusKind.rejecti.description: The rejection is validated for the remedial action schedule.

RemedialActionSchedule.statusKind.description: Indicates the status kind for the remedial action schedule.

RemedialActionSchedule.statusReason.description: Description of reasoning for the status. For instance, in case of rejected remedial action, the reason for this rejection is described here.

RemedialActionSchedule.totalCostCurrency.description: The currency of the total cost.

RemedialActionScheduleDependency.description: Remedial action schedule dependency is making two remedial action schedules depending on each other.

RemedialActionScheduleDependency.Propose.description: Proposed remedial action schedule that has dependency.

RemedialActionScheduleDependency.Remedia.description: Remedial action schedule group which has remedial action schedule dependency.

RemedialActionScheduleDependency.Replace.description: Remedial action schedule that is replaced by dependent remedial action schedule.

RemedialActionScheduleDependencyKind.exc.description: Remedial action schedules are exclusive depending on each other. e.g. Only one of the remedial action schedules can be selected at the same time.

RemedialActionScheduleDependencyKind.inc.description: Remedial action schedules are inclusive depending on each other. e.g. Both remedial action schedules need to be picked if one of them is needed.

RemedialActionScheduleDependencyKind.non.description: Remedial action schedules are not depending on each other. However, the two remedial action schedules should be evaluated together.

RemedialActionScheduleDependency.kind.description: Type of dependency between two remedial action schedules.

RemedialActionScheduleDependency.mRID.description:

For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

RemedialActionScheduleGroup.description: Remedial action schedule group collects two or more remedial action schedules together. The remedial action schedule group needs to be set up for the same remedial action or proposing alternative remedial action by including a reference to another remedial action.

RemedialActionScheduleResponse.description: The response on the remedial action schedule by a given system operator.

RemedialActionScheduleResponse.RemedialA.description: A remedial action schedule for which a remedial action schedule response is reported.

RemedialActionScheduleResponse.Respondin.description: An entity for which a remedial action schedule response is reported.

RemedialActionScheduleResponseKind.accep.description: The acceptance of remedial action schedule is concluded and accepted.

RemedialActionScheduleResponseKind.refus.description: The acceptance of the remedial action schedule is concluded and refused.

RemedialActionScheduleResponseKind.timeo.description: The acceptance of the remedial action schedule was not completed due to timeout.

RemedialActionScheduleResponseKind.waiti.description: The acceptance of the remedial action schedule is waiting (in progress).

RemedialActionScheduleResponse.kind.description: The kind of the remedial action response.

RemedialActionScheduleResponse.rejection.description: An additional type of rejection reason. It is used only when rejectionReasonKind equals RejectionReasonKind.other.

RejectionReasonKind.madeAlternative.description: The rejection is due to a proposal of an alternative remedial action.

RejectionReasonKind.noTimeToImplement.description: The rejection is due to lack of time to realise the proposed remedial action.

RejectionReasonKind.notAvailable.description: The rejection is due to unavailability of the object.

RejectionReasonKind.other.description: The rejection is due to other more complex reason or the details are unknown.

RejectionReasonKind.securityLimit.description: The rejection is due to security limit violation.

RemedialActionScheduleResponse.rejection.description: The kind of the remedial action rejection reason.

RemedialActionSchemeSchedule.description: The schedule for a remedial action scheme.

RemedialActionSchemeSchedule.SchemeRemed.description: Remedial action scheme which has remedial action scheme schedules.

SchemeRemedialAction.description: Scheme remedial action is remedial action that involves a scheme that can include conditional logic and stages of grid alteration. The primary remedial action is the arming of these schemes, that will then perform curative remedial action when the condition is met. System Integrity Protection Scheme (SIPS) and Special Protection Scheme (SPS) are example of this.

Dataset.description: A collection of data, published or curated by a single source, and available for access or download in one or more representations.

URI.description: Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) or URI Reference as defined by [RFC 3986], including amendments from [RFC 6874] for IPv6 zone identifiers. The value may be absolute or relative and can include an optional fragment identifier. This datatype is used to indicate that the value fulfills the role of a URI or URI Reference, providing a consistent format for referencing abstract or physical resources.

accessRights.description:
Information about who access the resource or an indication of its security status. Access Rights may include information regarding access or restrictions based on privacy, security, or other policies.
[CIM context:
Reference to the confidentiality level that shall be applied when handling this model.].

accrualPeriodicity.description:
The frequency with which items are added to a collection.
[CIM context:
Reference to the time frame.].

conformsTo.description:
An established standard to which the described resource conforms.
[CIM context:
An IRI describing the profile that governs this model. It uniquely identifies the profile and its version. Multiple instances of the property describe all standards or specifications to which the model and the document representing this model conform to.
A document would normally conform to profile definitions, the constraints that relate to the profile and/or the set of business specific constrains. A reference to a machine- readable constraints or specification indicates that the document was tested against these constraints and it conforms to them.].

LangString.description: Datatype that conforms to rdf:langString, representing a textual value with an associated language tag, following BCP 47 language conventions (e.g., en, fr-CA, no-NB).

description.description:
A free-text account of the resource.
Description may include but is not limited to: an abstract, a table of contents, a graphical representation, or a free-text account of the resource.

hasPart.description: The dataset which is part of another dataset.

UUID.description: Datatype representing a unique identifier in the form of a universally unique identifier (UUID). The value must conform to the UUID format as defined in RFC 4122, allowing for globally unique identification of entities.

identifier.description:
A unique identifier of the resource being described or cataloged.
The identifier might be used as part of the IRI of the resource, but still having it represented explicitly is useful.
The identifier is a text string which is assigned to the resource to provide an unambiguous reference within a particular context.
[CIM context:
A unique identifier of the model which is serialised in the document where the header is located. The identifier is persistent for a given version of the model and shall change when the model changes.
If a model is serialized as complete (full) model or as difference model exchange the identifier shall be the same. The identifier shall not be used as an identifier of the document which can be different for a given version of a model.].

issued.description:
Date of formal issuance of the resource.
Recommended practice is to describe the date, date/time, or period of time as recommended for the property Date, of which this is a subproperty.
[CIM context:
Reference to the date that the complete data set was made valid/available.].

license.description:
A legal document giving official permission to do something with the resource. Recommended practice is to identify the license document with a URI. If this is not possible or feasible, a literal value that identifies the license may be provided.
[CIM context:
Reference to the license under which the data is made available. If no license holder is defined, then the original data provider holds the license.].

publisher.description:
An entity responsible for making the resource available.
[CIM context: 
The agent that is publishing the dataset on the given platform.]

references.description:
A related resource that is referenced, cited, or otherwise pointed to by the described resource[.
[CIM context: 
The referenced resource that is being complemented in this dataset, e.g. SSH is referencing EQ.]

replaces.description:
A related resource that is supplanted, displaced, or superseded by the described resource
[CIM context: 
The referenced dataset is being replaced by this dataset.]

requires.description: A related resource that is required by the described resource to support its function, delivery, or coherence.

rights.description: A statement that concerns all rights not addressed with dct:license or dct:accessRights, such as copyright statements.

rightsHolder.description:
Information about rights held in and over the resource.
Typically, rights information includes a statement about various property rights associated with the resource, including intellectual property rights. Recommended practice is to refer to a rights statement with a URI. If this is not possible or feasible, a literal value (name, label, or short text) may be provided.

source.description:
A related resource from which the described resource is derived.
This property is intended to be used with non-literal values. The described resource may be derived from the related resource in whole or in part. Best practice is to identify the related resource by means of a URI or a string conforming to a formal identification system.

spatial.description:
The geographical area covered by the dataset.
[CIM context: 
The responsibility area that multiple model can describe, also referred to frame.].

title.description: A name given to the resource.

type.description: The nature or genre of the resource. Recommended practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as the DCMI Type Vocabulary [DCMI-TYPE]. To describe the file format, physical medium, or dimensions of the resource, use the property Format.

versionNotes.description: A description of changes between this version and the previous version of the resource.

DateTimeStamp.description: Position of an instant, expressed using xsd:dateTimeStamp, in which the time-zone field is mandatory.

endDate.description:
This property contains the end of the period.
[CIM context:
The end date and time of the validity period of the model that it is serialized in the document where the header is located. It is only used in relation to the startDate property which indicates the beginning of the validity period of the model.].

inSeries.description: A dataset series of which the dataset is part.

isVersionOf.description:
This resource has a more specific, versioned resource. This property is intended for relating a non-versioned or abstract resource to several versioned resources, e.g., snapshots.

The notion of version used by this property is limited to versions resulting from revisions occurring to a resource as part of its life-cycle. Therefore, its semantics is more specific than its super-property dcterms:hasVersion, which makes use of a broader notion of version, including editions and adaptations.

keyword.description:
A keyword or tag describing a resource.
[CIM context:
The intended content type of the model, usually the profile keyword. Used to identify what profiles and content is expected in the document, e.g., Equipment, Boundary, SSH, AE, etc. The same keyword is used for different versions of same profile. It can be also used to identify different content based on the same profile.
For instance, as the equipment profile can be used for both boundary data and equipment not related to boundary, the keyword is different to indicate that boundary data is exchanged. In order to avoid ambiguity the property is not exchanged in cases where the document contains multiple profiles referenced by dcterms:conformsTo.].

nextVersion.description: The next version for the resource.

previousVersion.description:
The previous version of a resource in a lineage.
This property is meant to be used to specify a version chain, consisting of snapshots of a resource.

The notion of version used by this property is limited to versions resulting from revisions occurring to a resource as part of its life-cycle. One of the typical cases here is representing the history of the versions of a dataset that have been released over time.

startDate.description:
This property contains the start of the period.
[CIM context:
The date and time that this model represents, i.e. for which the model is (or was) valid. It indicates the beginning of the validity period. It is indicating either an instant (in cases where the model is only valid for a point in time) or the start time of a period. If not provided the model is considered valid for any time stamp. The format is an extended format according to the ISO 8601-2005. European exchanges shall refer to UTC.].

Duration.description: Duration as "PnYnMnDTnHnMnS" which conforms to ISO 8601, where nY expresses a number of years, nM a number of months, nD a number of days. The letter T separates the date expression from the time expression and, after it, nH identifies a number of hours, nM a number of minutes and nS a number of seconds. The number of seconds could be expressed as a decimal number, but all other numbers are integers.

temporalResolution.description:
Minimum time period resolvable in a dataset.
[CIM context: 
Describes the Market Time Unit (MTU), e.g. hourly, 15 min., etc.]

Version.description: Datatype representing a version identifier that follows Semantic Versioning (SemVer 2.0.0) principles: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+BUILD]. The version consists of a sequence of numbers and optional alphanumeric identifiers that indicate changes in a system, model, or software over time.

version.description: The version indicator (name or identifier) of a resource.

generatedAtTime.description:
Generation is the completion of production of a new entity by an activity. This entity did not exist before generation and becomes available for usage after this generation.
[CIM context:
The date and time when the model was serialized in the document where the header is located. The format is an extended format according to the ISO 8601-2005. European exchanges shall refer to UTC.].
