Generation is the completion of production of a new entity by an activity. This entity did not exist before generation and becomes available for usage after this generation.
[CIM context:
Reference to an activity or the exact business nature (process, configuration) which produced or uses the model.].

applicationSoftware.description:
Identifies the application software which generated this instance file. The application software term is defined in ISO/IEC/IEEE 24765:2017. The application software can be identified either:
- as a string which contains information on the software name and version, e.g. <tool_name>-<major_version>.<minor_version>.<patch>, or
- as a reference to a software identification tag as defined by ISO/IEC 19770-2:2015 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 24765:2017.

processType.description: The exact business nature. Reference to Business Process configurations.

usedSettings.description: Reference to a set of parameters describing used settings (e.g. power flow settings, process settings, etc.) applied to the model prior its serialisation.

alternativeVersionOf.description:
This resource is an alternative version of a non-versioned or abstract resource.
This property is intended for relating a versioned resource to a non-versioned or abstract resource at the same time express that multiple versions exist.
dcatcim:alternativeVersionOf is a specialisation of dcat:isVersionOf with the restriction that the resource shall have a preferred version (dcatcim:preferredVersion) so that the preferred dataset can be used when there is no need to access all alternative versions.

preferredVersion.description:
The preferred version of a resource in a lineage of alternative versions.
This property is used to specify a specific version to be the preference in a chain of alternatives, consisting of snapshots of a resource.

DifferenceSet.description: A dataset that is represented by statement that describe the difference previous version by using forwardDifference Statement for item that is added and reverseDifference Statement for items that are removed. Items that are updated is described in both the forwardDifference and reversalDifference statements.

Statements.description: One or more facts in the form of an RDF triples that forms a cohesive description of change to a dataset.

forwardDifference.description: Statement that describes facts that has been added from previous version of the dataset.

reverseDifference.description: Statement that describes facts that has been removed from previous version of the dataset.

Statement.description: rdf:Statement is an instance of rdfs:Class. It is intended to represent the class of RDF statements. An RDF statement is the statement made by a token of an RDF triple. The subject of an RDF statement is the instance of rdfs:Resource identified by the subject of the triple. The predicate of an RDF statement is the instance of rdf:Property identified by the predicate of the triple. The object of an RDF statement is the instance of rdfs:Resource identified by the object of the triple. rdf:Statement is in the domain of the properties rdf:predicate, rdf:subject and rdf:object. Different individual rdf:Statement instances may have the same values for their rdf:predicate, rdf:subject and rdf:object properties.

StringIRI.description:
An IRI (Internationalized Resource Identifier) within an RDF graph is a Unicode string that conforms to the syntax defined in RFC 3987.
The primitive is serialized as literal without language support.
IRIs in the RDF abstract syntax must be absolute, and may contain a fragment identifier.
IRI equality: Two IRIs are equal if and only if they are equivalent under Simple String Comparison according to section 5.1 of [RFC3987]. Further normalization must not be performed when comparing IRIs for equality.
IRIs are a generalization of URIs [RFC3986] that permits a wider range of Unicode characters. Every absolute URI and URL is an IRI, but not every IRI is an URI. When IRIs are used in operations that are only defined for URIs, they must first be converted according to the mapping defined in section 3.1 of [RFC3987]. A notable example is retrieval over the HTTP protocol. The mapping involves UTF-8 encoding of non-ASCII characters, %-encoding of octets not allowed in URIs, and Punycode-encoding of domain names.

The primitive is serialized as literal without language support.

Resource.keyword.description: A keyword or tag describing a resource.

Resource.version.description: The version indicator (name or identifier) of a resource.

PowerSystemProject.description: Knowledge data for the power system project that describe the status and the planned implementation of the changes into the as-built model.

PowerSystemProject.AvailabilitySchedule.description: The availability schedule associated with this power system project.

PowerSystemProject.DependentOnProject.description: Grouping of projects that are depending on each other. A project can only be linked to one dependent project.

PowerSystemProject.DifferenceModel.description: The difference model describing this power system project.

PowerSystemProject.PriorityProject.description: The project that has an alternative project.

PowerSystemProject.ProjectGroup.description: Power system project group to which this project belongs.

PowerSystemProject.ShadowProject.description: A shadowing project that includes the same change set, but different timeline.

PowerSystemProject.cancelled.description: From this date the project is in cancelled state. No further development will be done to the project or associated change set in this state.

PowerSystemProject.commissioned.description: From this date the project is in commissioned state. Any conducting equipment in the change set can be energized from this day. No further changes will be done to the change set.

PowerSystemProject.committed.description: From this date the project is in committed state. The change set will from this day be part of the as-build model.

PowerSystemProject.inBuild.description: From this day the project is in build state. Alternative project have been evaluated. Any procurement has started and the change set is being updated to an as-build model.

PowerSystemProject.inPlan.description: From this date the project is in planning state. Study or procurement strategy has triggered the start of a project involving changes to one or more models. Alternative projects and change sets are evaluated.

Integer.description: An integer number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

PowerSystemProject.priority.description: Priority between competing project. Use 0 for do not care. Use 1 for highest priority. Use 2 as priority is less than 1 and so on.

PowerSystemProjectGroup.description: A container with project that are grouped together. Primarily used for navigation and to highlight the phases that an overall project can go though.

PowerSystemProjectGroup.description.description:
A free-text account of the resource.
Description may include but is not limited to: an abstract, a table of contents, a graphical representation, or a free-text account of the resource.

PowerSystemProjectGroup.identifier.description:
A unique identifier of the resource being described or cataloged.
The identifier might be used as part of the IRI of the resource, but still having it represented explicitly is useful.
The identifier is a text string which is assigned to the resource to provide an unambiguous reference within a particular context.

PowerSystemProjectGroup.title.description: A name given to the resource.

Dataset.description: A collection of data, published or curated by a single source, and available for access or download in one or more representations.

URI.description: Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) or URI Reference as defined by [RFC 3986], including amendments from [RFC 6874] for IPv6 zone identifiers. The value may be absolute or relative and can include an optional fragment identifier. This datatype is used to indicate that the value fulfills the role of a URI or URI Reference, providing a consistent format for referencing abstract or physical resources.

accessRights.description:
Information about who access the resource or an indication of its security status. Access Rights may include information regarding access or restrictions based on privacy, security, or other policies.
[CIM context:
Reference to the confidentiality level that shall be applied when handling this model.].

accrualPeriodicity.description:
The frequency with which items are added to a collection.
[CIM context:
Reference to the time frame.].

conformsTo.description:
An established standard to which the described resource conforms.
[CIM context:
An IRI describing the profile that governs this model. It uniquely identifies the profile and its version. Multiple instances of the property describe all standards or specifications to which the model and the document representing this model conform to.
A document would normally conform to profile definitions, the constraints that relate to the profile and/or the set of business specific constrains. A reference to a machine- readable constraints or specification indicates that the document was tested against these constraints and it conforms to them.].

LangString.description: Datatype that conforms to rdf:langString, representing a textual value with an associated language tag, following BCP 47 language conventions (e.g., en, fr-CA, no-NB).

description.description:
A free-text account of the resource.
Description may include but is not limited to: an abstract, a table of contents, a graphical representation, or a free-text account of the resource.

hasPart.description: The dataset which is part of another dataset.

UUID.description: Datatype representing a unique identifier in the form of a universally unique identifier (UUID). The value must conform to the UUID format as defined in RFC 4122, allowing for globally unique identification of entities.

identifier.description:
A unique identifier of the resource being described or cataloged.
The identifier might be used as part of the IRI of the resource, but still having it represented explicitly is useful.
The identifier is a text string which is assigned to the resource to provide an unambiguous reference within a particular context.
[CIM context:
A unique identifier of the model which is serialised in the document where the header is located. The identifier is persistent for a given version of the model and shall change when the model changes.
If a model is serialized as complete (full) model or as difference model exchange the identifier shall be the same. The identifier shall not be used as an identifier of the document which can be different for a given version of a model.].

issued.description:
Date of formal issuance of the resource.
Recommended practice is to describe the date, date/time, or period of time as recommended for the property Date, of which this is a subproperty.
[CIM context:
Reference to the date that the complete data set was made valid/available.].

license.description:
A legal document giving official permission to do something with the resource. Recommended practice is to identify the license document with a URI. If this is not possible or feasible, a literal value that identifies the license may be provided.
[CIM context:
Reference to the license under which the data is made available. If no license holder is defined, then the original data provider holds the license.].

publisher.description:
An entity responsible for making the resource available.
[CIM context: 
The agent that is publishing the dataset on the given platform.]

references.description:
A related resource that is referenced, cited, or otherwise pointed to by the described resource[.
[CIM context: 
The referenced resource that is being complemented in this dataset, e.g. SSH is referencing EQ.]

replaces.description:
A related resource that is supplanted, displaced, or superseded by the described resource
[CIM context: 
The referenced dataset is being replaced by this dataset.]

requires.description: A related resource that is required by the described resource to support its function, delivery, or coherence.

rights.description: A statement that concerns all rights not addressed with dct:license or dct:accessRights, such as copyright statements.

rightsHolder.description:
Information about rights held in and over the resource.
Typically, rights information includes a statement about various property rights associated with the resource, including intellectual property rights. Recommended practice is to refer to a rights statement with a URI. If this is not possible or feasible, a literal value (name, label, or short text) may be provided.

source.description:
A related resource from which the described resource is derived.
This property is intended to be used with non-literal values. The described resource may be derived from the related resource in whole or in part. Best practice is to identify the related resource by means of a URI or a string conforming to a formal identification system.

spatial.description:
The geographical area covered by the dataset.
[CIM context: 
The responsibility area that multiple model can describe, also referred to frame.].

title.description: A name given to the resource.

type.description: The nature or genre of the resource. Recommended practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as the DCMI Type Vocabulary [DCMI-TYPE]. To describe the file format, physical medium, or dimensions of the resource, use the property Format.

versionNotes.description: A description of changes between this version and the previous version of the resource.

DateTimeStamp.description: Position of an instant, expressed using xsd:dateTimeStamp, in which the time-zone field is mandatory.

endDate.description:
This property contains the end of the period.
[CIM context:
The end date and time of the validity period of the model that it is serialized in the document where the header is located. It is only used in relation to the startDate property which indicates the beginning of the validity period of the model.].

inSeries.description: A dataset series of which the dataset is part.

isVersionOf.description:
This resource has a more specific, versioned resource. This property is intended for relating a non-versioned or abstract resource to several versioned resources, e.g., snapshots.

The notion of version used by this property is limited to versions resulting from revisions occurring to a resource as part of its life-cycle. Therefore, its semantics is more specific than its super-property dcterms:hasVersion, which makes use of a broader notion of version, including editions and adaptations.

keyword.description:
A keyword or tag describing a resource.
[CIM context:
The intended content type of the model, usually the profile keyword. Used to identify what profiles and content is expected in the document, e.g., Equipment, Boundary, SSH, AE, etc. The same keyword is used for different versions of same profile. It can be also used to identify different content based on the same profile.
For instance, as the equipment profile can be used for both boundary data and equipment not related to boundary, the keyword is different to indicate that boundary data is exchanged. In order to avoid ambiguity the property is not exchanged in cases where the document contains multiple profiles referenced by dcterms:conformsTo.].

nextVersion.description: The next version for the resource.

previousVersion.description:
The previous version of a resource in a lineage.
This property is meant to be used to specify a version chain, consisting of snapshots of a resource.

The notion of version used by this property is limited to versions resulting from revisions occurring to a resource as part of its life-cycle. One of the typical cases here is representing the history of the versions of a dataset that have been released over time.

startDate.description:
This property contains the start of the period.
[CIM context:
The date and time that this model represents, i.e. for which the model is (or was) valid. It indicates the beginning of the validity period. It is indicating either an instant (in cases where the model is only valid for a point in time) or the start time of a period. If not provided the model is considered valid for any time stamp. The format is an extended format according to the ISO 8601-2005. European exchanges shall refer to UTC.].

Duration.description: Duration as "PnYnMnDTnHnMnS" which conforms to ISO 8601, where nY expresses a number of years, nM a number of months, nD a number of days. The letter T separates the date expression from the time expression and, after it, nH identifies a number of hours, nM a number of minutes and nS a number of seconds. The number of seconds could be expressed as a decimal number, but all other numbers are integers.

temporalResolution.description:
Minimum time period resolvable in a dataset.
[CIM context: 
Describes the Market Time Unit (MTU), e.g. hourly, 15 min., etc.]

Version.description: Datatype representing a version identifier that follows Semantic Versioning (SemVer 2.0.0) principles: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+BUILD]. The version consists of a sequence of numbers and optional alphanumeric identifiers that indicate changes in a system, model, or software over time.

version.description: The version indicator (name or identifier) of a resource.

generatedAtTime.description:
Generation is the completion of production of a new entity by an activity. This entity did not exist before generation and becomes available for usage after this generation.
[CIM context:
The date and time when the model was serialized in the document where the header is located. The format is an extended format according to the ISO 8601-2005. European exchanges shall refer to UTC.].

wasGeneratedBy.description:
Generation is the completion of production of a new entity by an activity. This entity did not exist before generation and becomes available for usage after this generation.
[CIM context:
Reference to an activity or the exact business nature (process, configuration) which produced or uses the model.].

applicationSoftware.description:
Identifies the application software which generated this instance file. The application software term is defined in ISO/IEC/IEEE 24765:2017. The application software can be identified either:
- as a string which contains information on the software name and version, e.g. <tool_name>-<major_version>.<minor_version>.<patch>, or
- as a reference to a software identification tag as defined by ISO/IEC 19770-2:2015 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 24765:2017.

processType.description: The exact business nature. Reference to Business Process configurations.

usedSettings.description: Reference to a set of parameters describing used settings (e.g. power flow settings, process settings, etc.) applied to the model prior its serialisation.

alternativeVersionOf.description:
This resource is an alternative version of a non-versioned or abstract resource.
This property is intended for relating a versioned resource to a non-versioned or abstract resource at the same time express that multiple versions exist.
dcatcim:alternativeVersionOf is a specialisation of dcat:isVersionOf with the restriction that the resource shall have a preferred version (dcatcim:preferredVersion) so that the preferred dataset can be used when there is no need to access all alternative versions.

preferredVersion.description:
The preferred version of a resource in a lineage of alternative versions.
This property is used to specify a specific version to be the preference in a chain of alternatives, consisting of snapshots of a resource.

DifferenceSet.description: A dataset that is represented by statement that describe the difference previous version by using forwardDifference Statement for item that is added and reverseDifference Statement for items that are removed. Items that are updated is described in both the forwardDifference and reversalDifference statements.

Statements.description: One or more facts in the form of an RDF triples that forms a cohesive description of change to a dataset.

forwardDifference.description: Statement that describes facts that has been added from previous version of the dataset.

reverseDifference.description: Statement that describes facts that has been removed from previous version of the dataset.

Statement.description: rdf:Statement is an instance of rdfs:Class. It is intended to represent the class of RDF statements. An RDF statement is the statement made by a token of an RDF triple. The subject of an RDF statement is the instance of rdfs:Resource identified by the subject of the triple. The predicate of an RDF statement is the instance of rdf:Property identified by the predicate of the triple. The object of an RDF statement is the instance of rdfs:Resource identified by the object of the triple. rdf:Statement is in the domain of the properties rdf:predicate, rdf:subject and rdf:object. Different individual rdf:Statement instances may have the same values for their rdf:predicate, rdf:subject and rdf:object properties.

statement.description: A name given to the resource.

ProfileMetadata.description: This vocabulary is describing the aseessed element profile.
ProfileMetadata.title: AssessedElement-AP-Voc-RDFS2020.rdf
ProfileMetadata.comment: This package contains datatypes used only in the RDFS header.
ProfileMetadata.label: DocAssessedElementProfile

AssessedElement.description:
Assessed element is a network element for which the electrical state is evaluated in the regional or cross-regional process and which value is expected to fulfil regional rules function of the operational security limits.
The measurements and limits are as defined in the steady state hypothesis.

String.description: A string consisting of a sequence of characters. The character encoding is UTF-8. The string length is unspecified and unlimited.

IdentifiedObject.description.description: The description is a free human readable text describing or naming the object. It may be non unique and may not correlate to a naming hierarchy.

IdentifiedObject.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

IdentifiedObject.name.description: The name is any free human readable and possibly non unique text naming the object.

AssessedElement.AssessedPowerTransferCor.description: The power transfer corridor that is designated as an assessed element.

AssessedElement.AssessedSystemOperator.description: A system operator that assesses the element.

AssessedElement.ConductingEquipment.description: The conducting equipment that is designated as an assessed element, i.e. the equipment that is assessed.

AssessedElement.DCTieCorridor.description: The DC tie corridor that is assessed.

AssessedElement.Line.description: The line that is designated as an assessed element, i.e. the equipment that is assessed.

AssessedElement.NativeRegion.description: The native region for an assessed element.

AssessedElement.OperationalLimit.description: The terminal limit that is being assessed against.

AssessedElement.OverlappingZone.description: The overlapping zone grouping the overlapping assessed elements.

AssessedElement.ScannedForRegion.description: This is the region in which this assessed element is scanned.

AssessedElement.SecuredForRegion.description: This is the region where the element is secured.

CriticalElementKind.critical.description: Network element is considered to be critical according to the methodology.

CriticalElementKind.criticalAndMonitored.description: Network element is considered to be Critical Network Element monitored under Contingency (CNEC).

CriticalElementKind.monitored.description: Network element is considered to be monitored under contingency.

CriticalElementKind.validation.description: Network element should be assessed according to the methodology.

AssessedElement.criticalElement.description: Indicates the type of the critical element.

SecuredExclusionReasonKind.capacityCalcu.description: The network element that is going to be assessed is excluded for being secured by the capacity calculation region.

SecuredExclusionReasonKind.nonNativeCapa.description: The network element that is going to be assessed is excluded for being secured for the native capacity calculation region since it would be secured for a non native capacity calculation region.

SecuredExclusionReasonKind.systemOperato.description: The network element that is going to be assessed is excluded for being secured by the system operator.

AssessedElement.exclusionReason.description: Reason for not associating this assessed element with a secured region.

PerCent.description: Percentage on a defined base.   For example, specify as 100 to indicate at the defined base.

AssessedElement.flowReliabilityMargin.description:
Percentage of the maximum flow (margin) reserved to anticipate forecasting errors.
The allowed value range is [0,100].

Boolean.description: A type with the value space "true" and "false".

AssessedElement.inBaseCase.description:
Indicates if the assessed element is scanned in the base case. In case of a base case overload, the assessed element is considered as a limiting element for the optimization process.
True means that the assessed element is scanned in the base case. False means it is not scanned in the base case.

AssessedElement.insideCapacityMargin.description:
Percentage of the maximum flow (margin) from coordinated capacity calculation, i.e. capacity available for cross-zonal trade within the considered coordination area.
The allowed value range is [0,100].

AssessedElement.isCombinableWithContinge.description: Defines if the AssessedElement is available to be combined with Contingency. If true,  this AssessedElement can be included in various combinations not defined in the data exchange in an explicit way. If false, this assessed element is not to be considered in any combination with remedial actions and contingencies except for the exclusive combination. If not provided, the default meaning is true, i.e. the assessed element is combinable.

AssessedElement.isCombinableWithRemedial.description: Defines if the AssessedElement is available to be combined with RemedialAction. If true,  this AssessedElement can be included in various combinations not defined in the data exchange in an explicit way. If false, this assessed element is not to be considered in any combination with remedial actions and contingencies except for the exclusive combination. If not provided, the default meaning is true, i.e. the assessed element is combinable.

AssessedElement.isCriticalForCapacityCal.description: Indicates whether the capacity calculation process is using the element or not.

AssessedElement.maxMarginAdjustment.description:
Maximum adjustment, relative to maximum flow allowed for exceeding the maximum flow of this assessed element.
The allowed value range is [0,100].

AssessedElement.normalAppointedMargin.description:
The normal percentage (appointed to a region) of the remaining margin obtained in the grid model to reach its current limit under normal operating conditions. The maximum percentage shall by default be 10% of the remaining margin.
It is only used when an assessed element is considered conservative for a region.
The allowed value range is [0,100].

ActivePower.description: Product of RMS value of the voltage and the RMS value of the in-phase component of the current.

AssessedElement.normalCoordinatedValidat.description: Normal positive value calculated and provided by the Coordinated Capacity Calculator (CCC) for the reduction of Remaining Available Margin (RAM) in order to ensure grid security.

Normal free text description provided by the coordinated capacity calculator (CCC) for justifying the reduction of Remaining Available Margin (RAM) by means of Coordinated Validation Adjustment (CVA). This justification is not intended for any application processing purpose, it should only be used for reporting.

AssessedElement.normalCriticalElementJus.description: Normal free text describing the justification of critical element categorization (e.g. the use of the kind). This justification is not intended for any application processing purpose, it should only be used for reporting.

AssessedElement.normalEnabled.description: If true, the assessed element shall be considered under normal operating conditions.

AssessedElement.normalIndividualValidati.description: Normal positive value calculated and provided by System Operators from their individual validation process for the reduction of Remaining Available Margin (RAM) in order to ensure grid security.

Normal free text description provided by System Operators for justifying the reduction of Remaining Available Margin (RAM) by means of Individual Validation Adjustment (IVA). This justification is not intended for any application processing purpose, it should only be used for reporting.

Normal positive value expressed calculated by the Coordinated Capacity Calculator (CCC) based on the provided Individual Validation Adjustment (IVA) by System Operators in order to show the actual reduction of Remaining Available Margin (RAM). Individual Validation Adjustment Share is a positive non-zero value. It is equal or less than the Individual Validation Adjustment value.

AssessedElement.normalMaxFlow.description: Maximum flow on a conducting equipment or a collection of conducting equipment forming a power transfer corridor under normal operating conditions. For assessed elements that become critical due to contingency, this value represents the maximum flow with remedial action taken into consideration.

AssessedElement.normalPositiveVirtualMar.description:
A positive margin that defines the overload allowed in a solution for the assessed element for a normal situation. The margin represents influences that can be solved by the System Operators using available remedial action which is not cross-border relevant remedial action.
All relevant operational limits (e.g. PATL, TATL, etc) are modified by this margin value. The attribute represents the increase. The allowed value range is [0,100].

AssessedElement.normalScannedThresholdMa.description:
Normal threshold percentage that a scanned element can be overloaded, on a given element, on top of any overload prior to optimisation (default= 5%). e.g. Initial loading of the element is 110%, with a 5% scanned threshold margin, the new maximum is 115% of the limit (e.g. PATL, TATL, etc).
The allowed value range is [0,100].

AssessedElement.normalTargetRemainingAva.description: Normal free text describing the justification for the target Remaining Available Margin (RAM). This justification is not intended for any application processing purpose, it should only be used for reporting.

AssessedElement.outsideCapacityMargin.description:
Percentage of the maximum flow (margin) capacity calculation, i.e. the capacity available for cross-zonal trade outside the considered coordination area. 
The allowed value range is [0,100].

AssessedElement.targetRemainingAvailable.description:
Target for the remaining available margin as a percentage of maximum flow.
The allowed value range is [0,100].

AssessedElementWithContingency.description: Combination of an assessed element and a contingency.

AssessedElementWithContingency.AssessedE.description: The assessed element defined for this contingency and assessed element combination.

AssessedElementWithContingency.Contingen.description: The contingency defined for this contingency and assessed element combination.

AssessedElementWithContingency.combinati.description: Defines the combination constraint of the AssessedElement and Contingency. If included, this assessed element is only assessed for this contingency. Else if excluded, this assessed element should not be assessed for this contingency. Considered shall not be used for this combination.

AssessedElementWithContingency.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

AssessedElementWithContingency.normalEna.description: If true, the assessed element with contingency is enabled, otherwise it is disabled under normal operating conditions.

AssessedElementWithRemedialAction.description: Combination of an assessed element and a remedial action

AssessedElementWithRemedialAction.Assess.description: The assessed element defined for this assessed element and remedial action combination.

AssessedElementWithRemedialAction.Remedi.description: The remedial action defined for this assessed element and remedial action combination.

AssessedElementWithRemedialAction.combin.description: Defines the combination constraint of the AssessedElement and Remedial Action. If included, this remedial action is only assessed for this assessed element. Else if excluded, this remedial action should not be used for this assessed element. Else if considered, this remedial action can be considered for this assessed element.

AssessedElementWithRemedialAction.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

AssessedElementWithRemedialAction.normal.description: If true, the assessed element with remedial action is enabled, otherwise it is disabled under normal operating conditions.

BaseCaseCurrentLimit.description: Operational limit on current applicable for base case.

OperationalLimit.OperationalLimitSet.description: The limit set to which the limit values belong.

CurrentFlow.description: Electrical current with sign convention: positive flow is out of the conducting equipment into the connectivity node. Can be both AC and DC.

BaseCaseCurrentLimit.normalValue.description: The normal value for limit on current flow. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero.

CrossBorderRelevance.description: Combination of an assessed element and one or more bidding zone border that are affected by the assessment.

CrossBorderRelevance.AssessedElement.description: Assessed element which is cross border relevant.

CrossBorderRelevance.BiddingZoneBorder.description: Bidding zone border relevant for this combination.

CrossBorderRelevance.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

CrossBorderRelevance.normalEnabled.description: If true, the cross border relevance shall be considered under normal operating conditions.

OperationalLimitSet.description: A set of limits associated with equipment.  Sets of limits might apply to a specific temperature, or season for example. A set of limits may contain different severities of limit levels that would apply to the same equipment. The set may contain limits of different types such as apparent power and current limits or high and low voltage limits  that are logically applied together as a set.

references.description:
A related resource that is referenced, cited, or otherwise pointed to by the described resource[.
[CIM context: 
The referenced resource that is being complemented in this dataset, e.g. SSH is referencing EQ.]

replaces.description:
A related resource that is supplanted, displaced, or superseded by the described resource
[CIM context: 
The referenced dataset is being replaced by this dataset.]

requires.description: A related resource that is required by the described resource to support its function, delivery, or coherence.

rights.description: A statement that concerns all rights not addressed with dct:license or dct:accessRights, such as copyright statements.

rightsHolder.description:
Information about rights held in and over the resource.
Typically, rights information includes a statement about various property rights associated with the resource, including intellectual property rights. Recommended practice is to refer to a rights statement with a URI. If this is not possible or feasible, a literal value (name, label, or short text) may be provided.

source.description:
A related resource from which the described resource is derived.
This property is intended to be used with non-literal values. The described resource may be derived from the related resource in whole or in part. Best practice is to identify the related resource by means of a URI or a string conforming to a formal identification system.

spatial.description:
The geographical area covered by the dataset.
[CIM context: 
The responsibility area that multiple model can describe, also referred to frame.].

title.description: A name given to the resource.

type.description: The nature or genre of the resource. Recommended practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as the DCMI Type Vocabulary [DCMI-TYPE]. To describe the file format, physical medium, or dimensions of the resource, use the property Format.

versionNotes.description: A description of changes between this version and the previous version of the resource.

DateTimeStamp.description: Position of an instant, expressed using xsd:dateTimeStamp, in which the time-zone field is mandatory.

endDate.description:
This property contains the end of the period.
[CIM context:
The end date and time of the validity period of the model that it is serialized in the document where the header is located. It is only used in relation to the startDate property which indicates the beginning of the validity period of the model.].

inSeries.description: A dataset series of which the dataset is part.

isVersionOf.description:
This resource has a more specific, versioned resource. This property is intended for relating a non-versioned or abstract resource to several versioned resources, e.g., snapshots.

The notion of version used by this property is limited to versions resulting from revisions occurring to a resource as part of its life-cycle. Therefore, its semantics is more specific than its super-property dcterms:hasVersion, which makes use of a broader notion of version, including editions and adaptations.

keyword.description:
A keyword or tag describing a resource.
[CIM context:
The intended content type of the model, usually the profile keyword. Used to identify what profiles and content is expected in the document, e.g., Equipment, Boundary, SSH, AE, etc. The same keyword is used for different versions of same profile. It can be also used to identify different content based on the same profile.
For instance, as the equipment profile can be used for both boundary data and equipment not related to boundary, the keyword is different to indicate that boundary data is exchanged. In order to avoid ambiguity the property is not exchanged in cases where the document contains multiple profiles referenced by dcterms:conformsTo.].

nextVersion.description: The next version for the resource.

previousVersion.description:
The previous version of a resource in a lineage.
This property is meant to be used to specify a version chain, consisting of snapshots of a resource.

The notion of version used by this property is limited to versions resulting from revisions occurring to a resource as part of its life-cycle. One of the typical cases here is representing the history of the versions of a dataset that have been released over time.

startDate.description:
This property contains the start of the period.
[CIM context:
The date and time that this model represents, i.e. for which the model is (or was) valid. It indicates the beginning of the validity period. It is indicating either an instant (in cases where the model is only valid for a point in time) or the start time of a period. If not provided the model is considered valid for any time stamp. The format is an extended format according to the ISO 8601-2005. European exchanges shall refer to UTC.].

Duration.description: Duration as "PnYnMnDTnHnMnS" which conforms to ISO 8601, where nY expresses a number of years, nM a number of months, nD a number of days. The letter T separates the date expression from the time expression and, after it, nH identifies a number of hours, nM a number of minutes and nS a number of seconds. The number of seconds could be expressed as a decimal number, but all other numbers are integers.

temporalResolution.description:
Minimum time period resolvable in a dataset.
[CIM context: 
Describes the Market Time Unit (MTU), e.g. hourly, 15 min., etc.]

Version.description: Datatype representing a version identifier that follows Semantic Versioning (SemVer 2.0.0) principles: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+BUILD]. The version consists of a sequence of numbers and optional alphanumeric identifiers that indicate changes in a system, model, or software over time.

version.description: The version indicator (name or identifier) of a resource.

generatedAtTime.description:
Generation is the completion of production of a new entity by an activity. This entity did not exist before generation and becomes available for usage after this generation.
[CIM context:
The date and time when the model was serialized in the document where the header is located. The format is an extended format according to the ISO 8601-2005. European exchanges shall refer to UTC.].

wasGeneratedBy.description:
Generation is the completion of production of a new entity by an activity. This entity did not exist before generation and becomes available for usage after this generation.
[CIM context:
Reference to an activity or the exact business nature (process, configuration) which produced or uses the model.].

applicationSoftware.description:
Identifies the application software which generated this instance file. The application software term is defined in ISO/IEC/IEEE 24765:2017. The application software can be identified either:
- as a string which contains information on the software name and version, e.g. <tool_name>-<major_version>.<minor_version>.<patch>, or
- as a reference to a software identification tag as defined by ISO/IEC 19770-2:2015 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 24765:2017.

processType.description: The exact business nature. Reference to Business Process configurations.

usedSettings.description: Reference to a set of parameters describing used settings (e.g. power flow settings, process settings, etc.) applied to the model prior its serialisation.

alternativeVersionOf.description:
This resource is an alternative version of a non-versioned or abstract resource.
This property is intended for relating a versioned resource to a non-versioned or abstract resource at the same time express that multiple versions exist.
dcatcim:alternativeVersionOf is a specialisation of dcat:isVersionOf with the restriction that the resource shall have a preferred version (dcatcim:preferredVersion) so that the preferred dataset can be used when there is no need to access all alternative versions.

preferredVersion.description:
The preferred version of a resource in a lineage of alternative versions.
This property is used to specify a specific version to be the preference in a chain of alternatives, consisting of snapshots of a resource.

DifferenceSet.description: A dataset that is represented by statement that describe the difference previous version by using forwardDifference Statement for item that is added and reverseDifference Statement for items that are removed. Items that are updated is described in both the forwardDifference and reversalDifference statements.

Statements.description: One or more facts in the form of an RDF triples that forms a cohesive description of change to a dataset.

forwardDifference.description: Statement that describes facts that has been added from previous version of the dataset.

reverseDifference.description: Statement that describes facts that has been removed from previous version of the dataset.

Statement.description: rdf:Statement is an instance of rdfs:Class. It is intended to represent the class of RDF statements. An RDF statement is the statement made by a token of an RDF triple. The subject of an RDF statement is the instance of rdfs:Resource identified by the subject of the triple. The predicate of an RDF statement is the instance of rdf:Property identified by the predicate of the triple. The object of an RDF statement is the instance of rdfs:Resource identified by the object of the triple. rdf:Statement is in the domain of the properties rdf:predicate, rdf:subject and rdf:object. Different individual rdf:Statement instances may have the same values for their rdf:predicate, rdf:subject and rdf:object properties.

statement.description: A name given to the resource.

ProfileMetadata.description: This vocabulary is describing the grid disturbance profile.
ProfileMetadata.title: GridDisturbance-AP-Voc-RDFS2020.rdf
ProfileMetadata.comment: This package contains the grid disturbance profile.
ProfileMetadata.label: GridDisturbanceProfile

String.description: A string consisting of a sequence of characters. The character encoding is UTF-8. The string length is unspecified and unlimited.

CoordinateSystem.crsUrn.description:
A Uniform Resource Name (URN) for the coordinate reference system (crs) used to define 'Location.PositionPoints'.
An example would be the European Petroleum Survey Group (EPSG) code for a coordinate reference system, defined in URN under the Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) namespace as: urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::XXXX, where XXXX is an EPSG code (a full list of codes can be found at the EPSG Registry web site http://www.epsg-registry.org/). To define the coordinate system as being WGS84 (latitude, longitude) using an EPSG OGC, this attribute would be urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::4236.
A profile should limit this code to a set of allowed URNs agreed to by all sending and receiving parties.

IdentifiedObject.description.description: The description is a free human readable text describing or naming the object. It may be non unique and may not correlate to a naming hierarchy.

IdentifiedObject.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

IdentifiedObject.name.description: The name is any free human readable and possibly non unique text naming the object.

Fault.description: Abnormal condition causing current flow through conducting equipment, such as caused by equipment failure or short circuits from objects not typically modelled (for example, a tree falling on a line).

PhaseConnectedFaultKind.lineOpen.description: The fault is when the conductor path is broken between two terminals. Additional coexisting faults may be required if the broken conductor also causes connections to grounds or other lines or phases.

PhaseConnectedFaultKind.lineToGround.description: The fault connects the indicated phases to ground. The line to line fault impedance is not used and assumed infinite. The full ground impedance is connected between each phase specified in the fault and ground, but not between the phases.

PhaseConnectedFaultKind.lineToLine.description: The fault connects the specified phases together without a connection to ground. The ground impedance of this fault is ignored. The line to line impedance is connected between each of the phases specified in the fault. For example three times for a three phase fault, one time for a two phase fault.  A single phase fault should not be specified.

PhaseConnectedFaultKind.lineToLineToGrou.description: The fault connects the indicated phases to ground and to each other. The line to line impedance is connected between each of the phases specified in the fault in a full mesh. For example three times for a three phase fault, one time for a two phase fault. A single phase fault should not be specified. The full ground impedance is connected between each phase specified in the fault and ground.

DateTime.description: Date and time as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss", which conforms with ISO 8601. UTC time zone is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sssZ". A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss-hh:mm". The second component (shown here as "ss.sss") could have any number of digits in its fractional part to allow any kind of precision beyond seconds.

Fault.occurredDateTime.description: The date and time at which the fault occurred.

PhaseCode.ABCN.description: Phases A, B, C, and N.

PhaseCode.XYN.description: Two unknown non-neutral phases plus neutral.

Fault.phases.description: The phases participating in the fault. The fault connections into these phases are further specified by the type of fault.

Fault.BaseVoltage.description: The base voltage of this fault.

Fault.GridDisturbance.description: A grid disturbance to contain all faults.

Fault.SystemOperator.description: The system operator in whose control area this fault occurred.

FaultCategoryKind.operational.description:
A fault due to a temporary human error.

Note 1: incorrect operation is considered a fault in a component, or in other words, the incorrect operation is attributed to the unit which has been operated incorrectly.

FaultCategoryKind.system.description:
A fault due to off-nominal parameters, exceeding of regulated norms and standards, or exceeding protection limits.

Note 1: Typical examples of system fault causes are high/low frequency, power oscillations, overload, overvoltage, undervoltage or high harmonic content in voltage or current. Common causes for system faults are significant changes in load or generation and switching of lines or transformers with following change of load flow.

FaultCategoryKind.technical.description: A fault due to a technical error.

Duration.description: Duration as "PnYnMnDTnHnMnS" which conforms to ISO 8601, where nY expresses a number of years, nM a number of months, nD a number of days. The letter T separates the date expression from the time expression and, after it, nH identifies a number of hours, nM a number of minutes and nS a number of seconds. The number of seconds could be expressed as a decimal number, but all other numbers are integers.

FaultKind.functional.description: The components main function failed to occur.

FaultKind.lineOpen.description: The fault is when the conductor path is broken between two terminals. Additional coexisting faults may be required if the broken conductor also causes connections to grounds or other lines or phases.

FaultKind.lineToGround.description: The fault connects the indicated phases to ground. The line to line fault impedance is not used and assumed infinite. The full ground impedance is connected between each phase specified in the fault and ground, but not between the phases.

FaultKind.lineToLine.description: The fault connects the specified phases together without a connection to ground. The ground impedance of this fault is ignored. The line to line impedance is connected between each of the phases specified in the fault. For example three times for a three phase fault, one time for a two phase fault.  A single phase fault should not be specified.

FaultKind.lineToLineToGround.description: The fault connects the indicated phases to ground and to each other. The line to line impedance is connected between each of the phases specified in the fault in a full mesh. For example three times for a three phase fault, one time for a two phase fault. A single phase fault should not be specified. The full ground impedance is connected between each phase specified in the fault and ground.

FaultKind.other.description: For example, geomagnetic currents, SSR, capacitor bank imbalances, bad contact, overheating.

FaultKind.undesiredFunction.description:
If the component's main function occurred correctly but had an undesired result, that is, the fault.
Is only stated if the component is a circuit breaker, disconnector or control system.

Fault.faultKind.description:
One fault can consist of several fault types. If a fault consists of several fault types, the most significant fault type is used.

In case of developing faults, that is in faults changing from one type to another, the final type is given.

Boolean.description: A type with the value space "true" and "false".

Fault.isDirectlyEarthed.description:
Whether the power system is directly earthed (true) or compensated (false). 
Usually optional for faults on units with reactive compensation with voltages lower than 100 kV.

Fault.isIntermittent.description:
The kind of occurrence of the fault. It is either intermittent (true) or non-intermittent (false).
An intermittent fault is a recurring fault in the same unit and in the same place and for the same reason which repeats itself before it becomes necessary to carry out any repairs or eliminate the cause [8].
A non-intermittent fault occurs only once.

Note 1: a fault which repeats itself after an inspection, which did not result in the fault being pinpointed or repaired, is not considered an intermittent fault. A fault like this is considered as the beginning of a grid disturbance every time the fault occurs.
Note 2: one example of an intermittent fault is galloping lines.
Note 3: when deciding whether a fault is intermittent or not, one should consider more of the cause, location and consequence of the fault and not on the time between the faults. An intermittent fault is counted as one fault. However, all individual caused outages are connected to this fault.
Note 4: there is no standard for the required timespan between intermittent faults. Some system operators use 2 hours.

Fault.isPermanent.description:
Whether the fault is a permanent (true) or a temporary (false) fault.
A permanent fault is a fault that will remain unless it is removed by some intervention.
Note 1 to entry: The “intervention” may be modification or maintenance.
Note 2: a permanent fault requires repair or adjustment before the unit is ready for operation. For example, the resetting of computers is considered as repair work and a switch in the wrong position is considered as a permanent fault. Signal acknowledgement is not considered as repair work. 
Note 3: the duration of the disconnection is irrelevant when determining if a fault is permanent or not.

A temporary fault is a fault where the unit or component is undamaged and is restored to service by switching operations without repair but possibly with on-site inspection.  
Note 1: a temporary fault does not require measures other than the reconnection of circuit breakers, replacement of fuses or signal acknowledgement.
Note 2: the duration of the disconnection is irrelevant when determining if a fault is temporary or not. If, for example, a fault results in long-term disconnection and (on-site) inspection cannot pinpoint its source, the fault is considered to be temporary as no repairs are carried out.

Fault.repairTime.description:
Time from when repair commences, including necessary troubleshooting, until the unit’s function(s) has (have) been resumed and the unit is ready for operation.

Note 1: repair time is registered only for permanent faults and does not include administrative delays (voluntary waiting time). However, any preparations necessary to carry out repairs, for example the collection or ordering of spare parts, waiting for spare parts or transport, are included in the repair time. 

Note 2: the repair time is zero if a fault is left unrepaired deliberately.

Note 3: this definition differs from the IEC 192-07-19 definition by also including the preparation time necessary to carry out the repairs mentioned in note 1.

Integer.description: An integer number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

Fault.sequenceNumber.description:
A chronological serial number indicating the order of the faults related to the grid disturbance. 

Primary faults have fault ID “1”, and secondary/latent faults have fault ID “2” or more.

FaultCause.Fault.description: The fault defined for this fault and cause combination.

FaultCause.FaultCauseType.description: The fault and cause combination to be simulated for this cause.

FaultCause.certaintyLevel.description:
The degree of certainty of which the cause of a fault is determined by a user. 
Note 1: the used certainty levels are low, medium and high. High certainty level is used when the cause of a fault is 100 % certain or when the cause is the most probable cause and potentially determined by an expert. Medium certainty level is used when the cause of the fault is very probable but there is not enough evidence to fully support the claim. Low certainty level is used when there is some idea of what the cause could be with the help of, for example, the fault details or expert knowledge. 
Note 2: the fault cause ‘unknown’ is used if no other fault cause can be chosen by any degree of certainty.

FaultCause.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

FaultCauseType.description: Type of cause of the fault.

FaultOutage.description: Association class for relating one fault and one outage.

FaultOutage.Fault.description: The fault defined for this combination of a fault and an outage.

FaultOutage.Outage.description: The outage defined for this combination of a fault and an outage.

FaultOutage.isMainFault.description: If true the fault outage is the main fault.

FaultOutage.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

GridDisturbance.description: Automatic, unintended, or manual undeferrable switching of breakers as a result of faults in the power grid.

Interruption.description: Disappearance of the supply voltage at a delivery point.

Interruption.InterruptedDeliveryEquipmen.description: The delivery point (equipment) that is affected by the interruption. It is an equipment, power transformer or busbar in the grid where electricity is exchanged.

Interruption.Outage.description: One outage may have multiple interruptions.

Interruption.energyNotDelivered.description: The estimated energy which would have been delivered through the delivery point if no interruption and no transmission restrictions had occurred.

Interruption.energyNotSupplied.description: The estimated energy which would have been supplied to end-users if no interruption and no transmission restrictions had occurred.

ActivePower.description: Product of RMS value of the voltage and the RMS value of the in-phase component of the current.

Interruption.interruptedPower.description: The estimated power that was delivered through the delivery point when the interruption occurred.

Interruption.startDateTime.description: The date and time at which the interruption occurred.

Location.description: The place, scene, or point of something where someone or something has been, is, and/or will be at a given moment in time. It can be defined with one or more position points (coordinates) in a given coordinate system.

Location.CoordinateSystem.description: Coordinate system used to describe position points of this location.

PositionPoint.description: Set of spatial coordinates that determine a point, defined in the coordinate system specified in 'Location.CoordinateSystem'. Use a single position point instance to describe a point-oriented location. Use a sequence of position points to describe a line-oriented object (physical location of non-point oriented objects like cables or lines), or area of an object (like a substation or a geographical zone - in this case, have first and last position point with the same values).

PositionPoint.Location.description: Location described by this position point.

UnplannedOutage.description:
Document describing the consequence of an unplanned outage in a part of the electrical network. For the purposes of this model, an unplanned outage refers to a state where energy is not delivered; such as, customers out of service, a street light is not served, etc.
A unplanned outage may be created upon:
- impacts the SAIDI calculation
- a breaker trip,
- a fault indicator status change,
- a meter event indicating customer outage,
- a reception of one or more customer trouble calls, or
- an operator command, reflecting information obtained from the field crew.
Outage restoration may be performed using a switching plan which complements the outage information with detailed switching activities, including the relationship to the crew and work.

Outage.Equipments.description: All equipments associated with this outage.

UnplannedOutage.reportedStartTime.description: The earliest start time of the Outage - as reported by some system or individual

AutoReclosingKind.automaticallyAfter2Sec.description:
If the automatic reclosing was successful in 2 seconds or more.

Also known as "successful high-speed reclosing".

AutoReclosingKind.automaticallyAfterLess.description:
If the automatic reclosing was successful in 2 seconds or less.

Also known as "successful high-speed reclosing".

AutoReclosingKind.manuallyAfterInspectio.description: If the reclosing was done manually after inspection of the component.

AutoReclosingKind.manuallyAfterRepair.description: If the reclosing was done manually after repair.

AutoReclosingKind.manuallyAfterRestructu.description: If the reclosing was done manually after restructuring of operations.

AutoReclosingKind.manuallyWithoutEitherI.description: If the reclosing was done manually without any inspections, repairs or restructurings of operations.

AutoReclosingKind.other.description: If the type of auto-reclosing is not unknown but does not fit the other categories, report it as other.

AutoReclosingKind.unknown.description: If the type of auto-reclosing is unknown.

UnplannedOutage.autoReclosingKind.description:
The type of autoreclosing that occurred with the trip.

If high-speed automatic reclosing is successful at one end of a line, but the line needs to be reclosed manually at the other end, choose manual reclosing.

In this document, high-speed automatic reclosing refers to automatic reclosing after less than 2 seconds.

UnplannedOutage.duration.description: The duration of the unplanned outage.

UnplannedOutage.startDateTime.description: The date and time at which the unplanned outage occurred.

SystemUnitKind.busbar.description: If the main function of the system unit is busbar.

SystemUnitKind.cable.description: If the main function of the system unit is cable.

SystemUnitKind.dcCable.description: If the main function of the system unit is DCCable.

SystemUnitKind.dcConverter.description: If the main function of the system unit is DCConverter.

SystemUnitKind.facts.description: If the main function of the system unit is FACTS.

SystemUnitKind.other.description: If it is of other kind.

SystemUnitKind.overheadLine.description: If the main function of the system unit is overhead line.

SystemUnitKind.powerTransformer.description: If the main function of the system unit is power transformer.

SystemUnitKind.reactor.description: If the main function of the system unit is reactor.

SystemUnitKind.seriesCapacitor.description: If the main function of the system unit is series capacitor.

SystemUnitKind.shuntCapacitor.description: If the main function of the system unit is shunt capacitor.

SystemUnitKind.svc.description: If the main function of the system unit is static var compensator (SVC).

UnplannedOutage.systemUnitKind.description:
The type of system unit of the component affected by the outage.

A system unit is defined as:

A group of components which are delimited by one or more circuit breakers.

Note 1: the system unit concept has been defined to simplify the calculation of availability. While a system unit is always delimited by circuit breakers, an individual component may not always be. A system unit may therefore contain more than one component. 

Note 2: the circuit breakers are not included in the system unit.

Note 3: a tripped element is synonymous to a tripped system unit.

Note 4: the type of a system unit is determined by its dominant component. The available system unit types are power transformer, overhead line, cable, reactor, busbar, series capacitor, shunt capacitor and SVC.

Note 5: when a system unit is no longer transporting or supplying electrical energy, the system unit is affected by an outage. The system unit is unavailable after the outage has occurred.

TripKind.automatic.description:
The trip that resulted in the outage was automatic.

In case of a fault in the reclosing automatics resulting in lack of reclosing, automatic should be chosen as an alternative.

TripKind.automaticWithUnsuccessfulAutoma.description:
The trip that resulted in an outage was correctly initiated but the automatic reclosing was unsuccessful.

In case of a fault in the reclosing automatics resulting in lack of reclosing, automatic should be chosen as an alternative.

TripKind.manual.description: The trip that resulted in the outage was manually cleared.

UnplannedOutage.tripKind.description:
Whether the type of the trip due to the outage was automatic, automatic with successful automatic reclosing or manual.

In case of a fault in the reclosing automatics resulting in lack of reclosing, automatic should be chosen as an alternative.

Equipment.description: The parts of a power system that are physical devices, electronic or mechanical.

Equipment.UnplannedOutage.description: The outage this tripped breaker is involved with.

Dataset.description: A collection of data, published or curated by a single source, and available for access or download in one or more representations.

URI.description: Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) or URI Reference as defined by [RFC 3986], including amendments from [RFC 6874] for IPv6 zone identifiers. The value may be absolute or relative and can include an optional fragment identifier. This datatype is used to indicate that the value fulfills the role of a URI or URI Reference, providing a consistent format for referencing abstract or physical resources.

accessRights.description:
Information about who access the resource or an indication of its security status. Access Rights may include information regarding access or restrictions based on privacy, security, or other policies.
[CIM context:
Reference to the confidentiality level that shall be applied when handling this model.].

accrualPeriodicity.description:
The frequency with which items are added to a collection.
[CIM context:
Reference to the time frame.].

conformsTo.description:
An established standard to which the described resource conforms.
[CIM context:
An IRI describing the profile that governs this model. It uniquely identifies the profile and its version. Multiple instances of the property describe all standards or specifications to which the model and the document representing this model conform to.
A document would normally conform to profile definitions, the constraints that relate to the profile and/or the set of business specific constrains. A reference to a machine- readable constraints or specification indicates that the document was tested against these constraints and it conforms to them.].

LangString.description: Datatype that conforms to rdf:langString, representing a textual value with an associated language tag, following BCP 47 language conventions (e.g., en, fr-CA, no-NB).

description.description:
A free-text account of the resource.
Description may include but is not limited to: an abstract, a table of contents, a graphical representation, or a free-text account of the resource.

hasPart.description: The dataset which is part of another dataset.

UUID.description: Datatype representing a unique identifier in the form of a universally unique identifier (UUID). The value must conform to the UUID format as defined in RFC 4122, allowing for globally unique identification of entities.

identifier.description:
A unique identifier of the resource being described or cataloged.
The identifier might be used as part of the IRI of the resource, but still having it represented explicitly is useful.
The identifier is a text string which is assigned to the resource to provide an unambiguous reference within a particular context.
[CIM context:
A unique identifier of the model which is serialised in the document where the header is located. The identifier is persistent for a given version of the model and shall change when the model changes.
If a model is serialized as complete (full) model or as difference model exchange the identifier shall be the same. The identifier shall not be used as an identifier of the document which can be different for a given version of a model.].

issued.description:
Date of formal issuance of the resource.
Recommended practice is to describe the date, date/time, or period of time as recommended for the property Date, of which this is a subproperty.
[CIM context:
Reference to the date that the complete data set was made valid/available.].

license.description:
A legal document giving official permission to do something with the resource. Recommended practice is to identify the license document with a URI. If this is not possible or feasible, a literal value that identifies the license may be provided.
[CIM context:
Reference to the license under which the data is made available. If no license holder is defined, then the original data provider holds the license.].

publisher.description:
An entity responsible for making the resource available.
[CIM context:

ContingencyEquipment.description: Equipment whose in service status is to change, such as a power transformer or AC line segment.

ContingencyElement.Contingency.description: A contingency element belongs to one contingency.

ContingencyEquipment.Equipment.description: The single piece of equipment to which to apply the contingency.

ContingencyEquipmentStatusKind.inService.description: The equipment is to be put into service.

ContingencyEquipmentStatusKind.outOfServ.description: The equipment is to be taken out of service.

ContingencyEquipment.contingentStatus.description: The status for the associated equipment when in the contingency state.   This status is independent of the case to which the contingency is originally applied, but defines the equipment status when the contingency is applied.

String.description: A string consisting of a sequence of characters. The character encoding is UTF-8. The string length is unspecified and unlimited.

IdentifiedObject.mRID.description:

For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

ExceptionalContingency.description: Exceptional contingency means the simultaneous occurrence of multiple contingencies with a common cause.

Contingency.EquipmentOperator.description: System operator that is operating the equipment that is being run a contingency on.

Boolean.description: A type with the value space "true" and "false".

Contingency.normalMustStudy.description: Specifies the requirement of study the contingency under normal operating conditions. True means the contingency must be study in a normal scenario. False means that the contingency does not need to be included in the scenario. This is the default value if mustStudy is missing.

PerCent.description: Percentage on a defined base.   For example, specify as 100 to indicate at the defined base.

Contingency.normalProbability.description:
Normal probability of the occurrence of the contingency based on normal operational condition. The value is used as the default if the probability is missing.
The allowed value range is [0,100].

ContingencyConditionKind.design.description: Permanent occurrence factor which is design condition.

ContingencyConditionKind.environmental.description: Temporary occurrence factor which is weather or environmental condition (e.g. storm).

ContingencyConditionKind.geographicalLoc.description: Permanent occurrence factor which is specific geographical location.

ContingencyConditionKind.malfunction.description: Temporary occurrence factor which is life time or generic malfunction affecting the risk of failure condition.

ContingencyConditionKind.operational.description: Temporary occurrence factor which is operational condition.

ExceptionalContingency.kind.description: Defines the kind of relevance and criteria of application of the exceptional contingency.

OrdinaryContingency.description: Ordinary contingency means the occurrence of a contingency of a single branch or injection.

OutOfRangeContingency.description: Out of range means the simultaneous occurrence of multiple contingencies without a common cause, or a loss of power generating modules with a total loss of generation capacity exceeding the reference incident.
