AvailabilityContainer.description: Availability container serves for associating an equipment container with an availability schedule. For instance, putting in or out of service all the equipment inside a Line or a Bay in combination with other availability functions with the same availability schedule.

String.description: A string consisting of a sequence of characters. The character encoding is UTF-8. The string length is unspecified and unlimited.

IdentifiedObject.description.description: The description is a free human readable text describing or naming the object. It may be non unique and may not correlate to a naming hierarchy.

IdentifiedObject.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

IdentifiedObject.name.description: The name is any free human readable and possibly non unique text naming the object.

AvailabilityContainer.EquipmentContainer.description: Equipment container that is affected by the availability given by this availability container.

AvailabilityPowerSystemFunction.Availabi.description: Grouping for all availability power system functions (controlled by all relevant system operators) that have the same availability schedule.
Availability schedule for this availability power system function.

AvailabilityFunctionKind.underTesting.description: Function is under testing and need to expect unscheduled availability.

AvailabilityPowerSystemFunction.kind.description: Kind of availability that affect the power system function.

AvailabilityEnabled.description: Availability enabled is enabling or disabling grid state alteration (e.g. tap position action) or assessed element that is related to the availability schedule. For instance, the cancellation of availability schedule can lead to changes in the  assessed element. This is done by enabling one assessment and disabling another.

AvailabilityEnabled.AssessedElement.description: Assessed element that is affected by the availability given by this availability enabling.

AvailabilityEnabled.GridStateAlteration.description: Grid state alteration that is affected by the availability given by this availability enabling.

Boolean.description: A type with the value space "true" and "false".

AvailabilityEnabled.enabled.description: Instruction to enable or disable alteration and assessment.

AvailabilityEquipment.description: Availability equipment serves for associating an equipment with an availability schedule. For instance, putting in or out of service an ACLineSegment in combination with other availability functions with the same availability schedule.

AvailabilityEquipment.Equipment.description: Equipment that is affected by the availability given by this availability equipment.

AvailabilityExceptionalLimit.description: Availability exceptional limit serves for associating an operational limit restriction with an availability schedule. For instance, enabling or disabling the current limit on ACLineSegment terminal in combination with other availability functions with the same availability schedule or de-rating due to fault.

AvailabilityExceptionalLimit.Operational.description: Operational limit that is constrained by this availability exceptional limit.

Float.description: A floating point number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

AvailabilityExceptionalLimit.value.description: Value for the referred operational limit.

AvailabilityGroup.description: Container to link relevant equipment that is affected by (un)availability schedule across availability coordinator (e.g. TSO-TSO, TSO-DSO or DSO-DSO).

AvailabilityRemedialActionScheme.description: Availability remedial action scheme serves for associating a remedial action scheme with an availability schedule. For instance, taking in or out of service a SIPS / SPS due to communication issue, in combination with other availability functions with the same availability schedule.

AvailabilityRemedialActionScheme.Remedia.description: Remedial action scheme that is affected by the availability given by this availability remedial action scheme.

AvailabilitySchedule.description: A given (un)availability schedule with a given status and cause that include multiple equipment that need to follow the same scheduling periods.

AvailabilitySchedule.ActualSchedule.description: Actual schedule that relates to this availability schedule; used for ex-post reporting and analysis (e.g., to compare planned vs. actual).

AvailabilitySchedule.AvailablityPlan.description: The AvailabilityPlan of which this AvailabilitySchedule is a component.

AvailabilitySchedule.DependentOnSchedule.description: (Un)availability schedule requested by one operator may require another operator to request their (un)availability schedule. This association is linking the schedules so that the dependency is clear.

AvailabilitySchedule.GridStateAlteration.description: The grid state alteration collection that has this availability schedule.

AvailabilitySchedule.PlannedSchedule.description: Planned schedule that relates to this availability schedule used for planning availability (e.g., to compare planned vs. actual).

AvailabilitySchedule.PrioritySchedule.description: Priority schedule. This is the schedule that has the highest priority and the only valid if not cancelled.

AvailabilitySchedule.RemedialAction.description: Remedial action that is cancelling this availability schedule.

DateTime.description: Date and time as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss", which conforms with ISO 8601. UTC time zone is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sssZ". A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss-hh:mm". The second component (shown here as "ss.sss") could have any number of digits in its fractional part to allow any kind of precision beyond seconds.

AvailabilitySchedule.cancelledDateTime.description: The date and time the (un)availability schedule were cancelled .

AvailabilitySchedule.causeDescription.description: A cause description for a cause kind. In case of CauseKind equals other, description or a reference of the cause of the (un)availability schedule.

AvailabilityScheduleCauseKind.commission.description: The cause is due to a commissioning.

AvailabilityScheduleCauseKind.decommissi.description: The cause is due to a decommissioning.

AvailabilityScheduleCauseKind.environmen.description: The cause is due to an environmental condition. This can lead to exceptional margin and limits.

AvailabilityScheduleCauseKind.functional.description: The cause is due to a functional control (in & out).

AvailabilityScheduleCauseKind.maintenanc.description: The cause is due to a maintenance.

AvailabilityScheduleCauseKind.other.description: The cause is of other kind.

AvailabilityScheduleCauseKind.refurbishm.description: The cause is due to a refurbishment, either upgrade or downgrade.

AvailabilityScheduleCauseKind.worksInPro.description: The cause is due to a works in proximity.

AvailabilitySchedule.causeKind.description: Kind of cause for the availability schedule.

Duration.description: Duration as "PnYnMnDTnHnMnS" which conforms to ISO 8601, where nY expresses a number of years, nM a number of months, nD a number of days. The letter T separates the date expression from the time expression and, after it, nH identifies a number of hours, nM a number of minutes and nS a number of seconds. The number of seconds could be expressed as a decimal number, but all other numbers are integers.

AvailabilitySchedule.daytimeRestitutionD.description: The time required to take the out-of-service equipment back into service during daytime. This includes the start-up time for generating units.

AvailabilitySchedule.eveningRestitutionD.description: The time required to take the out-of-service equipment back into service after office hours. This includes the start-up time for generating units.

AvailabilitySchedule.isCancelled.description: Defines the cancelling of the availability schedule. True means that is cancelling, False means that it is not cancelling.

AvailabilitySchedule.maxRestitutionDurat.description: The maximum time required to take the out-of-service equipment back into service. This includes the start-up time for generating units.

Integer.description: An integer number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

AvailabilitySchedule.priority.description: Value 0 means ignore priority. 1 means the highest priority, 2 is the second highest priority.

AvailabilitySchedule.weekendRestitutionD.description: The time required to take the out-of-service equipment back into service in the weekend or during bank holidays. This includes the start-up time for generating units.

AvailablityPlan.description:
A consolidated plan established by a System Operator that groups the AvailabilitySchedules applicable to a defined period and operational scope.
Note: An AvailabilityPlan provides the system-level view of resource availability used for outage coordination and operational planning. It may be divided into subordinate AvailabilityPlans and may be subject to approval by an Outage Coordinator.

AvailablityPlan.AvailablityPlanApprover.description: The Outage Coordinator responsible for approving the AvailabilityPlan.

AvailablityPlan.PartOf.description: The parent AvailabilityPlan of which this AvailabilityPlan forms a part.

AvailablityPlan.SystemOperator.description: The System Operator responsible for establishing and maintaining the AvailabilityPlan.

AvailablityPlan.validFrom.description: The date and time the start of the availability plan.

AvailablityPlan.validTo.description: The date and time the end of the availability plan.

AvailablityPlanResponse.description:
A formal response provided by an affected Outage Coordinator to a specific AvailabilityPlanVersion.
Note: The response records the coordinator’s position on the proposed plan, such as acceptance, refusal, acceptance with conditions, an alternative proposal, acknowledgement, or absence of a response within the applicable time limit.

AvailablityPlanResponse.AffectedCoordina.description: The affected Outage Coordinator that provides the response to the AvailabilityPlanVersion.

AvailablityPlanResponse.AvailablityPlanV.description: The version of the AvailabilityPlan to which this response applies.

AvailablityPlanResponse.comment.description: Free-text explanation, justification or additional information provided with the response to the outage request version.

AvailablityPlanResponse.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

RequestResponseKind.accepted.description: Indicates that the responding agent agrees and accept the request version as submitted.

RequestResponseKind.acceptedWithConditio.description: Indicates that the responding agent can accept the request version only if specific conditions, modifications, or mitigations are met.

RequestResponseKind.acknowledged.description: Indicates that the responding agent has received and reviewed the request version, but has not yet provided an approval or objection.

RequestResponseKind.alternativeProposal.description: Indicates that the responding agent proposes alternative timing, duration, scope, or other adjustments to the request version.

RequestResponseKind.noResponseTimeout.description: Indicates that the responding agent did not provide a response within the required timeframe, and the coordination process proceeded using a timeout rule.

RequestResponseKind.refused.description: Indicates that the responding agent does not accept the request version due to operational, technical, or regulatory constraints.

AvailablityPlanResponse.status.description: Outcome of the response to the outage request version, indicating the decision or position of the responding party.

EventSchedule.description: Time series represent irregular event described by event points in time.

TimeSeriesInterpolationKind.previous.description: The value between two time points is set to previous value.

BaseTimeSeries.interpolationKind.description: Kind of interpolation done between time point.

BaseTimeSeriesKind.actual.description: Time series is actual data. The values represent measured or calculated values that represent the actual behaviour.

BaseTimeSeriesKind.schedule.description: Time series is schedule data. The values represent the result of a committed and plan forecast data that has been through a quality control and could incur penalty when not followed.

EventTimePoint.description: Event valid for a given point in time.

EventTimePoint.EventSchedule.description: Time series the time point values belongs to.

EventTimePoint.atTime.description: The time the data is valid for.

EventTimePoint.isActive.description: True, if the event is occurring (Active) at this time point. Otherwise false.

OutageAvailability.description:
Relationship between an OutageRequest and an AvailabilitySchedule, indicating that the outage request is one of the inputs or constraints used to establish that availability schedule.

Multiple outage requests may contribute to a single availability schedule, and a single outage request may be reflected in multiple availability schedules issued by the system operator.

OutageAvailability.AvailabilitySchedule.description: The availability schedule derived in part from this outage request.

OutageAvailability.OutageRequest.description: The outage request that contributes to or influences the resulting availability schedule.

OutageAvailability.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

OutageDependency.description:
A peer temporal dependency that defines temporal or operational constraints between two outage requests.
Note: The dependency constrains the start or end of the dependent outage relative to the start or end of the dependee outage. Lag constraints are evaluated using the latest applicable transition of the dependee. This supports sequencing and coordination of related outages without implying a hierarchical relationship between the outage requests.
Example:
- startToStartLag = 1H, startToStartLagKind = minimum: the dependent outage may start no earlier than one hour after the dependee outage starts.
- finishToStartLag = 20M, finishToStartLagKind = exact: the dependent outage starts exactly 20 minutes after the dependee outage ends, for example to allow a defined switching or restoration sequence between the outages.
- finishToFinishLag = 30M, finishToFinishLagKind = maximum: the dependent outage shall end no later than 30 minutes after the dependee outage ends.

OutageDependency.DependeeOutageRequest.description: The outage request upon which the dependent outage request depends.

OutageDependency.DependentOutageRequest.description: The outage request whose timing or execution is constrained by the dependee outage request.

DependencyConstraintKind.exclusive.description: The dependee and dependent shall not both be active or effective at the same time.

DependencyConstraintKind.inclusive.description: The dependent shall only be active or effective while the dependee is active or effective.

DependencyConstraintKind.restrictive.description:
The dependee constrains the dependent without requiring the dependent to become active or effective.
Note: A restrictive dependency defines temporal or operational constraints on the behaviour of the dependent while leaving its activation or operation optional.

PeerTemporalDependency.constraintKind.description:
The kind of temporal or operational constraint defined between the dependee and the dependent.
Note: Certain dependency constraint kinds may require or prohibit the use of temporal constraint attributes, depending on the semantics of the specialization.

PeerTemporalDependency.finishToFinishLag.description: The duration constraining the next finish or deactivation of the dependent relative to the latest applicable finish or deactivation of the dependee.

ReferenceValueKind.exact.description: The referenced value is to be met exactly.

ReferenceValueKind.maximum.description: The referenced value establishes a upper bound.

ReferenceValueKind.minimum.description: The referenced value establishes a lower bound.

PeerTemporalDependency.finishToFinishLag.description:
Specifies whether finishToFinishLag is an exact, minimum, or maximum temporal constraint.
Note: This attribute shall be specified when finishToFinishLag is provided.
Example: finishToFinishLag = 2D1H30M is interpreted together with finishToFinishLagKind:
- exact: the dependent finishes exactly 2 days, 1 hour and 30 minutes after the latest applicable finish of the dependee.
- minimum: the dependent may finish no earlier than 2 days, 1 hour and 30 minutes after the latest applicable finish of the dependee.
- maximum: the dependent shall finish no later than 2 days, 1 hour and 30 minutes after the latest applicable finish of the dependee.
In all cases, the dependee finish remains applicable only while the dependee remains in the state resulting from that finish. If the dependee subsequently changes state before the dependent finishes, the applicability of the previous finish is re-evaluated.

PeerTemporalDependency.finishToStartLag.description: The duration constraining the next start or activation of the dependent relative to the latest applicable finish or deactivation of the dependee.

PeerTemporalDependency.finishToStartLagK.description:
Specifies whether finishToStartLag is an exact, minimum, or maximum temporal constraint.
Note: This attribute shall be specified when finishToStartLag is provided.
Example: finishToStartLag = 20M is interpreted together with finishToStartLagKind:
- exact: the dependent starts exactly 20 minutes after the latest applicable finish of the dependee.
- minimum: the dependent may start no earlier than 20 minutes after the latest applicable finish of the dependee.
- maximum: the dependent shall start no later than 20 minutes after the latest applicable finish of the dependee.
In all cases, the dependee finish remains applicable only while the dependee remains in the state resulting from that finish. If the dependee subsequently changes state before the dependent starts, the constraint is evaluated from the next applicable finish of the dependee.

PeerTemporalDependency.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

PeerTemporalDependency.overlap.description: The duration constraining the period for which the dependee and dependent are simultaneously active or effective.

PeerTemporalDependency.overlapKind.description:
Specifies whether overlap is an exact, minimum, or maximum duration of simultaneous activity or effectiveness.
Note: This attribute shall be specified when overlap is provided.
Example: overlap = 1H28M45S is interpreted together with overlapKind:
- exact: the dependee and dependent are simultaneously active or effective for exactly 1 hour, 28 minutes, and 45 seconds.
- minimum: the dependee and dependent shall be simultaneously active or effective for at least 1 hour, 28 minutes, and 45 seconds.
- maximum: the dependee and dependent shall be simultaneously active or effective for no more than 1 hour, 28 minutes, and 45 seconds.
Unlike the lag attributes, overlap constrains the duration of a simultaneous state rather than the temporal separation between two state transitions.

PeerTemporalDependency.startToStartLag.description: The duration constraining the next start or activation of the dependent relative to the latest applicable start or activation of the dependee.

PeerTemporalDependency.startToStartLagKi.description:
Specifies whether startToStartLag is an exact, minimum, or maximum temporal constraint.
Note: This attribute shall be specified when startToStartLag is provided.
Example: startToStartLag = 2H is interpreted together with startToStartLagKind:
- exact: the dependent starts exactly 2 hours after the latest applicable start of the dependee.
- minimum: the dependent may start no earlier than 2 hours after the latest applicable start of the dependee.
- maximum: the dependent shall start no later than 2 hours after the latest applicable start of the dependee.
In all cases, the dependee start remains applicable only while the dependee remains in the state resulting from that start. If the dependee subsequently changes state before the dependent starts, the constraint is evaluated from the next applicable start of the dependee.

OutageRequest.description: Represents the initial business intent to take one or more resources out of service during a specified period, as submitted by an Outage Planning Agent.

OutageRequest.OutageRequestApprover.description: The coordinator responsible for approving the final version of the outage request.

OutageRequest.RequestedBy.description: The agent responsible for creating and submitting the outage request.

OutageRequest.causeDescription.description: A cause description for a cause kind. In case of CauseKind equals other, description or a reference of the cause of the (un)availability schedule.

OutageRequest.causeKind.description: Kind of cause for the availability schedule.

OutageRequest.daytimeReinstatement.description: True, when no work is planned for the weekend or public holidays and the equipment can be reinstated.

OutageRequest.daytimeReinstatementDurati.description: The time required to take the out-of-service equipment back into service during daytime. This includes the start-up time for generating units.

OutageRequest.earlyStart.description: Earliest possible start time/date of the work.

OutageRequest.eveningReinstatement.description: True, when no work is planned for the weekend or public holidays and the equipment can be reinstated.

OutageRequest.eveningReinstatementDurati.description: The time required to take the out-of-service equipment back into service after office hours. This includes the start-up time for generating units.

OutageRequest.lateStart.description: The latest time/date the work can start.

OutageRequest.maxReinstatementDuration.description: The maximum time required to take the out-of-service equipment back into service after office hours. This includes the start-up time for generating units.

OutageRequest.maxWorkDuration.description: The maximum work duration taken into account risk mitigation with less resources available. If like that assessment is done on this duration to avoid re-planning on a later stage.

OutageRequest.minWorkDuration.description: The minimum work duration that can be achieved when extra resources are allocated.

OutageRequest.priority.description: 0 means ignore priority. 1 means the highest priority, 2 is the second highest priority.

OutageRequest.weekendReinstatement.description: True, when no work is planned for the weekend or public holidays and the equipment can be reinstated.

OutageRequest.weekendReinstatementDurati.description: The time required to take the out-of-service equipment back into service in the weekend or during bank holidays. This includes the start-up time for generating units.

Time.description: Time as "hh:mm:ss.sss", which conforms with ISO 8601. UTC time zone is specified as "hh:mm:ss.sssZ". A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "hh:mm:ss.sss±hh:mm". The second component (shown here as "ss.sss") could have any number of digits in its fractional part to allow any kind of precision beyond seconds.

OutageRequest.workDayEndTime.description: The time in a normal work day that equipment can be reinstated.

OutageRequest.workDayStartTime.description: The time in a normal work day that equipment would be taken out of service in case of reinstatement later in the working day.

OutageRequestResource.description: Associates an OutageRequest with a PowerSystemResource affected by the requested outage.

OutageRequestResource.OutageRequest.description: The outage request that includes this specific affected resource.

OutageRequestResource.PowerSystemResourc.description: The specific power system resource that is affected by the outage request.

OutageRequestResource.kind.description: The requested operational availability function of the associated PowerSystemResource. This value is used as input when determining the resulting AvailabilitySchedule.

OutageRequestResource.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

OutageResponse.description: Represents the formal response provided by an affected agent or the outage coordinator to a specific OutageRequestVersion.

OutageResponse.AffectedAgent.description: The agent that issued the response.

OutageResponse.AffectedCoordinator.description: The system operator acting as outage coordinator who issued the response.

OutageResponse.OutageRequestVersion.description: The version of the outage request to which this response applies.

OutageResponse.comment.description: Free-text explanation, justification or additional information provided with the response to the outage request version.

OutageResponse.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

OutageResponse.status.description: Outcome of the response to the outage request version, indicating the decision or position of the responding party.

Dataset.description: A collection of data, published or curated by a single source, and available for access or download in one or more representations.

URI.description: Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) or URI Reference as defined by [RFC 3986], including amendments from [RFC 6874] for IPv6 zone identifiers. The value may be absolute or relative and can include an optional fragment identifier. This datatype is used to indicate that the value fulfills the role of a URI or URI Reference, providing a consistent format for referencing abstract or physical resources.

accessRights.description:
Information about who access the resource or an indication of its security status. Access Rights may include information regarding access or restrictions based on privacy, security, or other policies.
[CIM context:
Reference to the confidentiality level that shall be applied when handling this model.].

accrualPeriodicity.description:
The frequency with which items are added to a collection.
[CIM context:
Reference to the time frame.].

conformsTo.description:
An established standard to which the described resource conforms.
[CIM context:
An IRI describing the profile that governs this model. It uniquely identifies the profile and its version. Multiple instances of the property describe all standards or specifications to which the model and the document representing this model conform to.
A document would normally conform to profile definitions, the constraints that relate to the profile and/or the set of business specific constrains. A reference to a machine- readable constraints or specification indicates that the document was tested against these constraints and it conforms to them.].

LangString.description: Datatype that conforms to rdf:langString, representing a textual value with an associated language tag, following BCP 47 language conventions (e.g., en, fr-CA, no-NB).

description.description:
A free-text account of the resource.
Description may include but is not limited to: an abstract, a table of contents, a graphical representation, or a free-text account of the resource.

hasPart.description: The dataset which is part of another dataset.

UUID.description: Datatype representing a unique identifier in the form of a universally unique identifier (UUID). The value must conform to the UUID format as defined in RFC 4122, allowing for globally unique identification of entities.

identifier.description:
A unique identifier of the resource being described or cataloged.
The identifier might be used as part of the IRI of the resource, but still having it represented explicitly is useful.
The identifier is a text string which is assigned to the resource to provide an unambiguous reference within a particular context.
[CIM context:
A unique identifier of the model which is serialised in the document where the header is located. The identifier is persistent for a given version of the model and shall change when the model changes.
If a model is serialized as complete (full) model or as difference model exchange the identifier shall be the same. The identifier shall not be used as an identifier of the document which can be different for a given version of a model.].

issued.description:
Date of formal issuance of the resource.
Recommended practice is to describe the date, date/time, or period of time as recommended for the property Date, of which this is a subproperty.
[CIM context:
Reference to the date that the complete data set was made valid/available.].

license.description:
A legal document giving official permission to do something with the resource. Recommended practice is to identify the license document with a URI. If this is not possible or feasible, a literal value that identifies the license may be provided.
[CIM context:
Reference to the license under which the data is made available. If no license holder is defined, then the original data provider holds the license.].

publisher.description:
An entity responsible for making the resource available.
[CIM context: 
The agent that is publishing the dataset on the given platform.]

references.description:
A related resource that is referenced, cited, or otherwise pointed to by the described resource[.
[CIM context: 
The referenced resource that is being complemented in this dataset, e.g. SSH is referencing EQ.]

replaces.description:
A related resource that is supplanted, displaced, or superseded by the described resource
[CIM context: 
The referenced dataset is being replaced by this dataset.]

requires.description: A related resource that is required by the described resource to support its function, delivery, or coherence.

rights.description: A statement that concerns all rights not addressed with dct:license or dct:accessRights, such as copyright statements.

rightsHolder.description:
Information about rights held in and over the resource.
Typically, rights information includes a statement about various property rights associated with the resource, including intellectual property rights. Recommended practice is to refer to a rights statement with a URI. If this is not possible or feasible, a literal value (name, label, or short text) may be provided.

source.description:
A related resource from which the described resource is derived.
This property is intended to be used with non-literal values. The described resource may be derived from the related resource in whole or in part. Best practice is to identify the related resource by means of a URI or a string conforming to a formal identification system.

spatial.description:
The geographical area covered by the dataset.
[CIM context: 
The responsibility area that multiple model can describe, also referred to frame.].

title.description: A name given to the resource.

type.description: The nature or genre of the resource. Recommended practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as the DCMI Type Vocabulary [DCMI-TYPE]. To describe the file format, physical medium, or dimensions of the resource, use the property Format.

versionNotes.description: A description of changes between this version and the previous version of the resource.

DateTimeStamp.description: Position of an instant, expressed using xsd:dateTimeStamp, in which the time-zone field is mandatory.

endDate.description:
This property contains the end of the period.
[CIM context:
The end date and time of the validity period of the model that it is serialized in the document where the header is located. It is only used in relation to the startDate property which indicates the beginning of the validity period of the model.].

inSeries.description: A dataset series of which the dataset is part.

isVersionOf.description:
This resource has a more specific, versioned resource. This property is intended for relating a non-versioned or abstract resource to several versioned resources, e.g., snapshots.

The notion of version used by this property is limited to versions resulting from revisions occurring to a resource as part of its life-cycle. Therefore, its semantics is more specific than its super-property dcterms:hasVersion, which makes use of a broader notion of version, including editions and adaptations.

keyword.description:
A keyword or tag describing a resource.
[CIM context:
The intended content type of the model, usually the profile keyword. Used to identify what profiles and content is expected in the document, e.g., Equipment, Boundary, SSH, AE, etc. The same keyword is used for different versions of same profile. It can be also used to identify different content based on the same profile.
For instance, as the equipment profile can be used for both boundary data and equipment not related to boundary, the keyword is different to indicate that boundary data is exchanged. In order to avoid ambiguity the property is not exchanged in cases where the document contains multiple profiles referenced by dcterms:conformsTo.].

nextVersion.description: The next version for the resource.

previousVersion.description:
The previous version of a resource in a lineage.
This property is meant to be used to specify a version chain, consisting of snapshots of a resource.

The notion of version used by this property is limited to versions resulting from revisions occurring to a resource as part of its life-cycle. One of the typical cases here is representing the history of the versions of a dataset that have been released over time.

startDate.description:
This property contains the start of the period.
[CIM context:
The date and time that this model represents, i.e. for which the model is (or was) valid. It indicates the beginning of the validity period. It is indicating either an instant (in cases where the model is only valid for a point in time) or the start time of a period. If not provided the model is considered valid for any time stamp. The format is an extended format according to the ISO 8601-2005. European exchanges shall refer to UTC.].

temporalResolution.description:
Minimum time period resolvable in a dataset.
[CIM context: 
Describes the Market Time Unit (MTU), e.g. hourly, 15 min., etc.]

Version.description: Datatype representing a version identifier that follows Semantic Versioning (SemVer 2.0.0) principles: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+BUILD]. The version consists of a sequence of numbers and optional alphanumeric identifiers that indicate changes in a system, model, or software over time.

version.description: The version indicator (name or identifier) of a resource.

generatedAtTime.description:
Generation is the completion of production of a new entity by an activity. This entity did not exist before generation and becomes available for usage after this generation.
[CIM context:
The date and time when the model was serialized in the document where the header is located. The format is an extended format according to the ISO 8601-2005. European exchanges shall refer to UTC.].

wasGeneratedBy.description:
Generation is the completion of production of a new entity by an activity. This entity did not exist before generation and becomes available for usage after this generation.
[CIM context:
Reference to an activity or the exact business nature (process, configuration) which produced or uses the model.].

applicationSoftware.description:
Identifies the application software which generated this instance file. The application software term is defined in ISO/IEC/IEEE 24765:2017. The application software can be identified either:
- as a string which contains information on the software name and version, e.g. <tool_name>-<major_version>.<minor_version>.<patch>, or
- as a reference to a software identification tag as defined by ISO/IEC 19770-2:2015 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 24765:2017.

processType.description: The exact business nature. Reference to Business Process configurations.

usedSettings.description: Reference to a set of parameters describing used settings (e.g. power flow settings, process settings, etc.) applied to the model prior its serialisation.

alternativeVersionOf.description:
This resource is an alternative version of a non-versioned or abstract resource.
This property is intended for relating a versioned resource to a non-versioned or abstract resource at the same time express that multiple versions exist.
dcatcim:alternativeVersionOf is a specialisation of dcat:isVersionOf with the restriction that the resource shall have a preferred version (dcatcim:preferredVersion) so that the preferred dataset can be used when there is no need to access all alternative versions.

preferredVersion.description:
The preferred version of a resource in a lineage of alternative versions.
This property is used to specify a specific version to be the preference in a chain of alternatives, consisting of snapshots of a resource.

DifferenceSet.description: A dataset that is represented by statement that describe the difference previous version by using forwardDifference Statement for item that is added and reverseDifference Statement for items that are removed. Items that are updated is described in both the forwardDifference and reversalDifference statements.

Statements.description: One or more facts in the form of an RDF triples that forms a cohesive description of change to a dataset.

forwardDifference.description: Statement that describes facts that has been added from previous version of the dataset.

reverseDifference.description: Statement that describes facts that has been removed from previous version of the dataset.

Statement.description: rdf:Statement is an instance of rdfs:Class. It is intended to represent the class of RDF statements. An RDF statement is the statement made by a token of an RDF triple. The subject of an RDF statement is the instance of rdfs:Resource identified by the subject of the triple. The predicate of an RDF statement is the instance of rdf:Property identified by the predicate of the triple. The object of an RDF statement is the instance of rdfs:Resource identified by the object of the triple. rdf:Statement is in the domain of the properties rdf:predicate, rdf:subject and rdf:object. Different individual rdf:Statement instances may have the same values for their rdf:predicate, rdf:subject and rdf:object properties.

statement.description: A name given to the resource.

ProfileMetadata.creator: ENTSO-E CIM WG NC project
ProfileMetadata.description: This vocabulary is describing the impact assessment matrix profile.
ProfileMetadata.title: ImpactAssessmentMatrix-AP-Voc-RDFS2020.rdf
ProfileMetadata.comment: This package contains impact assessment matrix profile.
ProfileMetadata.label: ImpactAssessmentMatrixProfile

CalculationBasedImpactAssessmentMatrix.description: Calculation based impact assessment matrix. It relates to the remedial action schedule. Calculation-Based is the impact matrix determined by calculating the impact factors (eventually scaled by the intensity of the remedial action) and matching them against a threshold in a determined way described by the methodologies.

String.description: A string consisting of a sequence of characters. The character encoding is UTF-8. The string length is unspecified and unlimited.

IdentifiedObject.description.description: The description is a free human readable text describing or naming the object. It may be non unique and may not correlate to a naming hierarchy.

IdentifiedObject.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

IdentifiedObject.name.description: The name is any free human readable and possibly non unique text naming the object.

ConnectingImpactAssessmentMatrix.description: Connecting system operator matrix is the impact matrix indicating which system operators are connecting for that specific remedial action. The concept of connecting system operator for a remedial action is defined by CSAm Article 2.1(14).

ListBasedImpactAssessmentMatrix.description: List-Based is the impact matrix determined by agreement of the system operators involved. System operators jointly decide which Remedial Action (eventually scaled by the intensity of the remedial action) is impacting.

OwnerRemedialActionAssessment.description: Owner remedial action assessment of the impact of their remedial action on neighboring system operators.

OwnerRemedialActionAssessment.ImpactedSy.description: System operator that is evaluated to be impacted by the remedial action done by the remedial action owner.

OwnerRemedialActionAssessment.RemedialAc.description: Remedial action impact which is evaluated by the owner of the remedial action.

OwnerRemedialActionAssessment.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

QualitativeRemedialActionImpact.description: Defines the qualitative impact for a remedial action. Relevant remedial action is assumed to have impact when the impact quantity is applied.

RemedialActionImpact.AssessingSystemOper.description: The impacted System Operator that assigns a remedial action impact.

RemedialActionImpact.RemedialAction.description: The remedial action that has an impact.

RemedialActionImpact.RemedialActionGroup.description: The remedial action group that has an impact.

Float.description: A floating point number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

RemedialActionImpact.impactQuantity.description:
Delta, positive or negative, quantity that when it is applied to the remedial action,  it will cause impact on a conducting equipment monitored by the assessed system operator.
Example of relevant remedial action changes are redispatching, countertrading, change of set point on HVDC systems or change of taps on phase-shifting transformers.

ImpactAgreementKind.always.description: An agreement is reached that the remedial action is always impacting whichever the intensity.

ImpactAgreementKind.never.description: An agreement is reached that a remedial action is never impacting.

ImpactAgreementKind.noAgreement.description: No agreement is reached on the qualitative impact of a remedial action.

RemedialActionImpact.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

QuantitativeRemedialActionImpact.description: Defines the quantitative impact for a remedial action. The value if the impact quantity is derived through offline calculation that has coursed an impact of an element that is monitored by the assessed system operator higher than the relevant threshold for the conducting equipment.

QuantitativeRemedialActionImpact.Sensiti.description: Sensitivity area which should be monitored to evaluate the threshold given by the remedial action impact on relevant equipment.

RemedialActionOutcomeValue.description: Outcome of an impact assessment matrix for a remedial action.

OutcomeValue.ImpactAssessmentMatrix.description: the impact assessment matrix which has this value.

OutcomeValue.ImpactedSystemOperator.description: The impacted system operator that has an outcome value.

OutcomeValue.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

OutcomeImpactAssessmentKind.undecided.description: Undecided. Used only for list-based impact assessment matrix.

RemedialActionOutcomeValue.RemedialActio.description: The remedial action that has a remedial action outcome value.
The remedial action group that has a remedial action group outcome value.

RemedialActionOutcomeValue.impactQuantit.description:
Delta, positive or negative, quantity that when it is applied to the remedial action,  it will cause impact on a conducting equipment monitored by the assessed system operator.
Example of relevant remedial action changes are redispatching, countertrading, change of set point on HVDC systems or change of taps on phase-shifting transformers.

RemedialActionScheduleOutcomeValue.description: Outcome of an impact assessment matrix for a remedial action schedule.

RemedialActionScheduleOutcomeValue.Remed.description: The remedial action schedule that has a remedial action schedule outcome value.

Dataset.description: A collection of data, published or curated by a single source, and available for access or download in one or more representations.

URI.description: Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) or URI Reference as defined by [RFC 3986], including amendments from [RFC 6874] for IPv6 zone identifiers. The value may be absolute or relative and can include an optional fragment identifier. This datatype is used to indicate that the value fulfills the role of a URI or URI Reference, providing a consistent format for referencing abstract or physical resources.

accessRights.description:
Information about who access the resource or an indication of its security status. Access Rights may include information regarding access or restrictions based on privacy, security, or other policies.
[CIM context:
Reference to the confidentiality level that shall be applied when handling this model.].

accrualPeriodicity.description:
The frequency with which items are added to a collection.
[CIM context:
Reference to the time frame.].

conformsTo.description:
An established standard to which the described resource conforms.
[CIM context:
An IRI describing the profile that governs this model. It uniquely identifies the profile and its version. Multiple instances of the property describe all standards or specifications to which the model and the document representing this model conform to.
A document would normally conform to profile definitions, the constraints that relate to the profile and/or the set of business specific constrains. A reference to a machine- readable constraints or specification indicates that the document was tested against these constraints and it conforms to them.].

LangString.description: Datatype that conforms to rdf:langString, representing a textual value with an associated language tag, following BCP 47 language conventions (e.g., en, fr-CA, no-NB).

description.description:
A free-text account of the resource.
Description may include but is not limited to: an abstract, a table of contents, a graphical representation, or a free-text account of the resource.

hasPart.description: The dataset which is part of another dataset.

UUID.description: Datatype representing a unique identifier in the form of a universally unique identifier (UUID). The value must conform to the UUID format as defined in RFC 4122, allowing for globally unique identification of entities.

identifier.description:
A unique identifier of the resource being described or cataloged.
The identifier might be used as part of the IRI of the resource, but still having it represented explicitly is useful.
The identifier is a text string which is assigned to the resource to provide an unambiguous reference within a particular context.
[CIM context:
A unique identifier of the model which is serialised in the document where the header is located. The identifier is persistent for a given version of the model and shall change when the model changes.
If a model is serialized as complete (full) model or as difference model exchange the identifier shall be the same. The identifier shall not be used as an identifier of the document which can be different for a given version of a model.].

DateTime.description: Date and time as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss", which conforms with ISO 8601. UTC time zone is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sssZ". A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss-hh:mm". The second component (shown here as "ss.sss") could have any number of digits in its fractional part to allow any kind of precision beyond seconds.

issued.description:
Date of formal issuance of the resource.
Recommended practice is to describe the date, date/time, or period of time as recommended for the property Date, of which this is a subproperty.
[CIM context:
Reference to the date that the complete data set was made valid/available.].

license.description:
A legal document giving official permission to do something with the resource. Recommended practice is to identify the license document with a URI. If this is not possible or feasible, a literal value that identifies the license may be provided.
[CIM context:
Reference to the license under which the data is made available. If no license holder is defined, then the original data provider holds the license.].

publisher.description:
An entity responsible for making the resource available.
[CIM context: 
The agent that is publishing the dataset on the given platform.]

references.description:
A related resource that is referenced, cited, or otherwise pointed to by the described resource[.
[CIM context: 
The referenced resource that is being complemented in this dataset, e.g. SSH is referencing EQ.]

replaces.description:
A related resource that is supplanted, displaced, or superseded by the described resource
[CIM context: 
The referenced dataset is being replaced by this dataset.]

requires.description: A related resource that is required by the described resource to support its function, delivery, or coherence.

rights.description: A statement that concerns all rights not addressed with dct:license or dct:accessRights, such as copyright statements.

rightsHolder.description:
Information about rights held in and over the resource.
Typically, rights information includes a statement about various property rights associated with the resource, including intellectual property rights. Recommended practice is to refer to a rights statement with a URI. If this is not possible or feasible, a literal value (name, label, or short text) may be provided.

source.description:
A related resource from which the described resource is derived.
This property is intended to be used with non-literal values. The described resource may be derived from the related resource in whole or in part. Best practice is to identify the related resource by means of a URI or a string conforming to a formal identification system.

spatial.description:
The geographical area covered by the dataset.
[CIM context: 
The responsibility area that multiple model can describe, also referred to frame.].

title.description: A name given to the resource.

type.description: The nature or genre of the resource. Recommended practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as the DCMI Type Vocabulary [DCMI-TYPE]. To describe the file format, physical medium, or dimensions of the resource, use the property Format.

versionNotes.description: A description of changes between this version and the previous version of the resource.

DateTimeStamp.description: Position of an instant, expressed using xsd:dateTimeStamp, in which the time-zone field is mandatory.

endDate.description:
This property contains the end of the period.
[CIM context:
The end date and time of the validity period of the model that it is serialized in the document where the header is located. It is only used in relation to the startDate property which indicates the beginning of the validity period of the model.].

inSeries.description: A dataset series of which the dataset is part.

isVersionOf.description:
This resource has a more specific, versioned resource. This property is intended for relating a non-versioned or abstract resource to several versioned resources, e.g., snapshots.

The notion of version used by this property is limited to versions resulting from revisions occurring to a resource as part of its life-cycle. Therefore, its semantics is more specific than its super-property dcterms:hasVersion, which makes use of a broader notion of version, including editions and adaptations.

keyword.description:
A keyword or tag describing a resource.
[CIM context:
The intended content type of the model, usually the profile keyword. Used to identify what profiles and content is expected in the document, e.g., Equipment, Boundary, SSH, AE, etc. The same keyword is used for different versions of same profile. It can be also used to identify different content based on the same profile.
For instance, as the equipment profile can be used for both boundary data and equipment not related to boundary, the keyword is different to indicate that boundary data is exchanged. In order to avoid ambiguity the property is not exchanged in cases where the document contains multiple profiles referenced by dcterms:conformsTo.].

nextVersion.description: The next version for the resource.

previousVersion.description:
The previous version of a resource in a lineage.
This property is meant to be used to specify a version chain, consisting of snapshots of a resource.

The notion of version used by this property is limited to versions resulting from revisions occurring to a resource as part of its life-cycle. One of the typical cases here is representing the history of the versions of a dataset that have been released over time.

startDate.description:
This property contains the start of the period.
[CIM context:
The date and time that this model represents, i.e. for which the model is (or was) valid. It indicates the beginning of the validity period. It is indicating either an instant (in cases where the model is only valid for a point in time) or the start time of a period. If not provided the model is considered valid for any time stamp. The format is an extended format according to the ISO 8601-2005. European exchanges shall refer to UTC.].

Duration.description: Duration as "PnYnMnDTnHnMnS" which conforms to ISO 8601, where nY expresses a number of years, nM a number of months, nD a number of days. The letter T separates the date expression from the time expression and, after it, nH identifies a number of hours, nM a number of minutes and nS a number of seconds. The number of seconds could be expressed as a decimal number, but all other numbers are integers.

temporalResolution.description:
Minimum time period resolvable in a dataset.
[CIM context: 
Describes the Market Time Unit (MTU), e.g. hourly, 15 min., etc.]

Version.description: Datatype representing a version identifier that follows Semantic Versioning (SemVer 2.0.0) principles: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+BUILD]. The version consists of a sequence of numbers and optional alphanumeric identifiers that indicate changes in a system, model, or software over time.

version.description: The version indicator (name or identifier) of a resource.

generatedAtTime.description:
Generation is the completion of production of a new entity by an activity. This entity did not exist before generation and becomes available for usage after this generation.
[CIM context:
The date and time when the model was serialized in the document where the header is located. The format is an extended format according to the ISO 8601-2005. European exchanges shall refer to UTC.].

wasGeneratedBy.description:
Generation is the completion of production of a new entity by an activity. This entity did not exist before generation and becomes available for usage after this generation.
[CIM context:
Reference to an activity or the exact business nature (process, configuration) which produced or uses the model.].

applicationSoftware.description:
Identifies the application software which generated this instance file. The application software term is defined in ISO/IEC/IEEE 24765:2017. The application software can be identified either:
- as a string which contains information on the software name and version, e.g. <tool_name>-<major_version>.<minor_version>.<patch>, or
- as a reference to a software identification tag as defined by ISO/IEC 19770-2:2015 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 24765:2017.

processType.description: The exact business nature. Reference to Business Process configurations.

usedSettings.description: Reference to a set of parameters describing used settings (e.g. power flow settings, process settings, etc.) applied to the model prior its serialisation.

alternativeVersionOf.description:
This resource is an alternative version of a non-versioned or abstract resource.
This property is intended for relating a versioned resource to a non-versioned or abstract resource at the same time express that multiple versions exist.
dcatcim:alternativeVersionOf is a specialisation of dcat:isVersionOf with the restriction that the resource shall have a preferred version (dcatcim:preferredVersion) so that the preferred dataset can be used when there is no need to access all alternative versions.

preferredVersion.description:
The preferred version of a resource in a lineage of alternative versions.
This property is used to specify a specific version to be the preference in a chain of alternatives, consisting of snapshots of a resource.

DifferenceSet.description: A dataset that is represented by statement that describe the difference previous version by using forwardDifference Statement for item that is added and reverseDifference Statement for items that are removed. Items that are updated is described in both the forwardDifference and reversalDifference statements.

Statements.description: One or more facts in the form of an RDF triples that forms a cohesive description of change to a dataset.

forwardDifference.description: Statement that describes facts that has been added from previous version of the dataset.

reverseDifference.description: Statement that describes facts that has been removed from previous version of the dataset.

Statement.description: rdf:Statement is an instance of rdfs:Class. It is intended to represent the class of RDF statements. An RDF statement is the statement made by a token of an RDF triple. The subject of an RDF statement is the instance of rdfs:Resource identified by the subject of the triple. The predicate of an RDF statement is the instance of rdf:Property identified by the predicate of the triple. The object of an RDF statement is the instance of rdfs:Resource identified by the object of the triple. rdf:Statement is in the domain of the properties rdf:predicate, rdf:subject and rdf:object. Different individual rdf:Statement instances may have the same values for their rdf:predicate, rdf:subject and rdf:object properties.

statement.description: A name given to the resource.

ControllableQuantity.description: Controllable quantity is a set point quantity on a grid state alteration or on a remedial action.

ControllableQuantity.GridStateAlteration.description: The grid state alteration for this controllable quantity.

ControllableQuantity.RemedialAction.description: Remedial action which is associated with the controllable quantity.

Float.description: A floating point number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

ControllableQuantity.value.description: The value of the change applied to the grid state alteration or remedial action. In the case of multiple changes or non-quantifiable changes (e.g. Topology changes) the value needs to represent the suitable value that makes the derivable value given in the observable quantity for the purpose of the calculation of the sensitivity factor.  The value can be integer, float or boolean. In case of boolean 1 equals true and 0 equals false.

ObservableQuantity.description: Observable quantity is an electrical quantity on an assessed element or an assessed element with contingency.

ObservableQuantity.AssessedElement.description: The assessed element with contingency associated with this observable quantity.

ObservableQuantity.Contingency.description: The contingency associated with this observable quantity.

ObservableQuantityKind.activePower.description: The observable quantity is the active power.

ObservableQuantityKind.reactivePower.description: The observable quantity is the reactive power.

ObservableQuantityKind.voltageAngle.description: The observable quantity is the angle of terminal voltage.

ObservableQuantityKind.voltageMagnitude.description: The observable quantity is the magnitude of terminal voltage.

SensitivityFactor.description: The sensitivity factor which represents the sensitivity between observable and controllable elements.

SensitivityFactor.ControllableQuantity.description: The controllable quantity for this sensitivity factor.

SensitivityFactor.ObservableQuantity.description: The observable quantity for this sensitivity factor.

SensitivityFactor.SensitivityMatrix.description: The sensitivity matrix which contains this sensitivity factor.

SensitivityFactor.value.description: The value of the sensitivity factor.

SensitivityMatrix.description: The sensitivity matrix which represents the sensitivity factors between observable and controllable elements.

IdentifiedObject.name.description: The name is any free human readable and possibly non unique text naming the object.

IdentifiedObject.energyIdentCodeEic.description: The attribute is used for an exchange of the EIC code (Energy identification Code). The length of the string is 16 characters as defined by the EIC code. For details on EIC scheme please refer to ENTSO-E web site.

ACDCConverterController.ACDCConverter.description: ACDC converter controlled by the direct current controller.

ACDCConverterController.DirectCurrentPol.description: DC pole controller that controls this ACDC controller.

ACDCConverterControlStrategyKind.gridFol.description: Converter control strategy in which the converter synchronizes to an externally established AC voltage and frequency reference, typically using phase-locked synchronization and controlled current injection.

ACDCConverterControlStrategyKind.gridFor.description: Converter control strategy in which the converter establishes or contributes to the AC voltage magnitude and frequency reference, operating as a controllable AC voltage source.

ACDCConverterController.controlStrategy.description: High-level control strategy defining how the converter interacts with and regulates the connected AC system.

AutomationFunction.PartOf.description: Automation function is part of this automation function.

Boolean.description: A type with the value space "true" and "false".

AutomationFunction.normalEnabled.description: True, if the automation function is enabled (active). Otherwise false.

ACEmulationControlFunction.description:
The AC emulation control function is used when AC emulation model is activated for a DC system. It consists in computing the active power set point of the DC system as a function of the voltage angle difference between both points of common coupling with the AC network in order to mimic the behavior of an AC transmission line. This control mode enables the automatic adjustment of the active power reference following variations of the AC system operational point. 
The setpoint of the DC system is calculated by Psetpoint=Pref+Kdc*(angle1-angle2), where
- Pref is the existing active power setpoint; 
- Kdc is the control system gain and  
- angle1 and angle2 are the phase angle measurement (measured at points of common coupling with the AC network) respectively at the side 1 and 2 of the DC system.

ControlFunctionBlock.isDiscrete.description: True, if the control function is discrete. This applies to equipment with discrete controls, e.g. tap changers and shunt compensators.

PerCent.description: Percentage on a defined base.   For example, specify as 100 to indicate at the defined base.

ControlFunctionBlock.maxAllowedTargetVal.description:
Maximum allowed target value given by the percent of target value.
The allowed value range is [0,100].

ControlFunctionBlock.minAllowedTargetVal.description:
Minimum allowed target value given by the percent of target value.
The allowed value range is [0,100].

ControlFunctionBlock.targetValueDeadband.description:
The deadband related to the targetValue of the control function. It is used with discrete control to avoid excessive update of controls like tap changers and shunt compensator banks while regulating.  The attribute shall be a positive value or zero. If isDiscrete is set to "false", the targetDeadband is to be ignored.
Note that for instance, if the targetValue is 100 kV and the targetValueDeadband is 2 percent the range is from 99 to 101 kV.

FunctionBlock.AutomationBlockGroup.description: Automation block group which has function blocks.

FunctionBlock.AutomationFunction.description: Automation function describe automation that this function block is part of.

FunctionBlock.normalEnabled.description: True, if the function block is normally enabled (active). Otherwise false.

ACTieCorridor.description: A collection of one or more AC tie lines that connect two different control areas.

TieCorridor.delayRegulatingReserve.description: A positive number that is a multiple of Automatic Generation Control (AGC) run cycles that describes the delay in adapting imbalance of the tie corridor.

Float.description: A floating point number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

TieCorridor.maxRegulatingReserveRamp.description: Maximum authorized ramp for regulating reserve.

ActivePower.description: Product of RMS value of the voltage and the RMS value of the in-phase component of the current.

ActivePowerControlFunction.description: Active power control function is a function block that calculates operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target active power.

AmbientTemperatureDependencyCurve.description: A curve or functional relationship between the ambient temperature independent variable (X-axis) and relative temperature dependent (Y-axis) variables.

CurveStyle.constantYValue.description: The Y-axis values are assumed constant until the next curve point and prior to the first curve point.

CurveStyle.straightLineYValues.description: The Y-axis values are assumed to be a straight line between values.  Also known as linear interpolation.

Curve.curveStyle.description: The style or shape of the curve.

UnitMultiplier.none.description: No multiplier or equivalently multiply by 1.

UnitSymbol.Pa.description: Pressure in pascals (N/m²). Note: the absolute or relative measurement of pressure is implied with this entry. See below for more explicit forms.

UnitSymbol.VA.description: Apparent power in volt amperes. See also real power and reactive power.

UnitSymbol.VAr.description:
Reactive power in volt amperes reactive. The “reactive” or “imaginary” component of electrical power (VIsin(phi)). (See also real power and apparent power).
Note: Different meter designs use different methods to arrive at their results. Some meters may compute reactive power as an arithmetic value, while others compute the value vectorially. The data consumer should determine the method in use and the suitability of the measurement for the intended purpose.

UnitSymbol.VPerVAr.description: Power factor, PF, the ratio of the active power to the apparent power. Note: The sign convention used for power factor will differ between IEC meters and EEI (ANSI) meters. It is assumed that the data consumers understand the type of meter being used and agree on the sign convention in use at any given utility.

UnitSymbol.W.description: Real power in watts (J/s). Electrical power may have real and reactive components. The real portion of electrical power (I²R or VIcos(phi)), is expressed in Watts. See also apparent power and reactive power.

UnitSymbol.WPerm2.description: Heat flux density, irradiance, watts per square metre.

UnitSymbol.WPers.description: Ramp rate in watts per second.

UnitSymbol.degC.description:
Relative temperature in degrees Celsius.
In the SI unit system the symbol is °C. Electric charge is measured in coulomb that has the unit symbol C. To distinguish degree Celsius from coulomb the symbol used in the UML is degC. The reason for not using °C is that the special character ° is difficult to manage in software.

UnitSymbol.kgPerJ.description: Weight per energy in kilograms per joule (kg/J). Note: multiplier “k” is included in this unit symbol for compatibility with IEC 61850-7-3.

UnitSymbol.none.description: Dimension less quantity, e.g. count, per unit, etc.

AreaInterchangeController.description: Area interchange control is set to control active power of an area.

AreaInterchangeController.BiddingZone.description: Bidding zone which has an area interchange controller.

AreaInterchangeController.BiddingZoneBor.description: Bidding zone border that has an area interchange controller.

AreaInterchangeController.ControlArea.description: Control area that has a area interchange controller.

AreaInterchangeController.pTolerance.description: Active power net interchange tolerance. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero.

SystemControl.EquipmentController.description: Equipment controller controlles by this system control

AreaReserveResource.description:
A resource representation for a specific balancing reserve product, associated with either a scheduling area or a tie corridor, and used to represent reserve capability made available to a control area for market and operational purposes.
Note: An AreaReserveResource shall be associated with either a SchedulingArea or a TieCorridor, but not both.
When associated with a SchedulingArea, the resource represents reserve capability made available within that area context.
When associated with a TieCorridor, the resource represents reserve capability provided across an inter-area connection to support a control area other than the one in which the underlying resource is located.
A single physical or logical resource (for example a GeneratingUnit, HydroPump, PowerElectronicsUnit, or equivalent) may be represented by multiple AreaReserveResource instances, each corresponding to a different balancing reserve product (e.g. FCR, aFRR, mFRR).

AreaReserveResource.GeneratingUnit.description: Generating unit that provides the reserve capability represented by the area reserve resource.

AreaReserveResource.HydroPump.description: Hydro pump that provides the reserve capability represented by the area reserve resource.

AreaReserveResource.PowerElectronicsUnit.description: Power electronics unit that provides the reserve capability represented by the area reserve resource.

AreaReserveResource.ScheduleResource.description: Schedule resource representing an aggregation or grouping of resources that provides the reserve capability represented by the area reserve resource.

AreaReserveResource.SchedulingArea.description: Scheduling area within which the reserve resource is made available when the reserve support is provided in the area context of the underlying resource.

AreaReserveResource.TieCorridor.description: Tie corridor through which the reserve resource is made available to support a control area other than the one in which the underlying resource is located.

AreaReserveResource.normalEnabled.description: Identifies if the unit is normally enabled to accept a dispatch instruction. If true, the unit is enabled to accept a dispatch instruction. If false, the unit has the capability, but it is not enabled to receive a dispatch instruction.

AutomationBlockGroup.description: Grouping of function block that are operated with the same priority as settings.

AutomationBlockGroup.AutomationFunction.description: Automation function which has automation block group.

Integer.description: An integer number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

AutomationBlockGroup.priority.description: Value 0 means ignore priority. 1 means the highest priority, 2 is the second highest priority.

BaseOverloadLimitCurve.description:
A curve or functional relationship between 
- the relative loading - current loading over permanent loading (PATL) independent variable (X-axis), and 
- temporary overloading (TATL) limiting dependent (Y-axis) variables.

BatteryUnit.ratedE.description: Full energy storage capacity of the battery. The attribute shall be a positive value.

Equipment.AggregatedEquipment.description: An aggregated representation of the detailed equipment.

Equipment.Circuit.description: The circuit that containts its member equipment.

PowerElectronicsUnit.PowerElectronicsUni.description: Power electronics unit controller for this power electronics unit.

PowerElectronicsUnit.ScheduleResource.description: The schedule resource that has this power electronics unit.

PowerElectronicsUnit.maxEconomicP.description: Maximum high economic active power limit, that should not exceed the maximum operating active power limit.

PowerElectronicsUnit.minEconomicP.description: Low economic active power limit that shall be greater than or equal to the minimum operating active power limit.

PowerElectronicsUnit.normalParticipation.description:
Participation factor describing the entity part of the active power provided by a collection of entities (e.g. an active power forecast to a collection of entities is divided to each of the member entity according to the participation factor). Must be a positive value.
In the case of a sharing strategy, the distribution is following entities value (V) equals aggregated value (T) divided by sum of participation factors (PF), i.e. V=T/sum(PF). 
In the case of priority strategy, the item with the lowest number gets allocated energy first.

BiddingZone.description: A bidding zone is a market-based method for handling power transmission congestion. It consists of scheduling areas that include the relevant production (supply) and consumption (demand) to form an electrical area with the same market price without capacity allocation.

BiddingZone.CapacityCalculationRegion.description: The capacity calculation region related to this bidding zone.

BiddingZone.GridPowerCapacity.description: Grid Power capacity whidh is asocciated to the bidding zone.

BiddingZone.isTradeEnabled.description: Identifies the mechanism for determining the energy price for a given bidding zone. If true, the bid and the offer is expected to be provided for the bidding zone to create the market price. If false,  other mechanism determines the price of energy for a given bidding zone, e.g. virtual bidding zone.

BiddingZoneBorder.description: A unidirectional interface between two adjacent Bidding Zones, representing the available transmission capacity from the Bidding Zone defined by the association FromBiddingZone (source) to the Bidding Zone defined by the association ToBiddingZone (sink). It defines the capacity constraints and market-based allocation mechanisms for cross-zonal electricity exchange in the specified direction, considering potential transmission congestion and market price differences.

BiddingZoneBorder.CapacityCalculationReg.description: The capacity calculation region for which the capacity is derived from.

BiddingZoneBorder.FromBiddingZone.description: The bidding zone for the from side.

BiddingZoneBorder.TieCorridor.description: Tie corridor for a given bidding zone border.

BiddingZoneBorder.ToBiddingZone.description: The bidding zone for the to side.

BipolarDCSystem.description: Bipolar DC system (IEC 60633) consists of two poles of opposite polarity with respect to earth. The overhead lines, if any, of the two poles may be carried on common or separate towers.

BipolarDCSystem.isRigid.description: If true, the bipolar DC system is a rigid DC current bipolar system (IEC 60633). It is a bipolar DC system without neutral connection between both converter stations. Since only two (pole) conductors exist, no unbalance current between both poles is possible. In case of interruption of power transfer of one converter pole, the current of the other pole has to be interrupted as well (at least for a limited time to allow reconfiguration of the DC circuit).

DCSystemDirectionKind.bidirectional.description: Bidirectional DC system used for the transfer of energy in either direction. According to IEC 60633 a multiterminal DC system is bidirectional if one or more substations are bidirectional.

DCSystemDirectionKind.unidirectional.description: Unidirectional DC system used for the transfer of energy in only one direction. According to IEC 60633, most DC systems are inherently bidirectional. However, some systems may be optimized to transmit power in only one preferred direction. Such systems may still be considered as "bidirectional".

DCSystem.directionKind.description: Direction kind of the DC system.

DCSystemTransmissionKind.backToBack.description: DC back-to-back system (IEC 60633) is a DC system which transfers energy between AC buses at the same location.
