DCSystemTransmissionKind.multiTerminal.description: Multiterminal DC transmission system (IEC 60633) consisting of more than two separated DC substations and the interconnecting DC transmission lines.

DCSystemTransmissionKind.twoTerminal.description: Two-terminal DC transmission system (IEC 60633), consisting of two DC substations and the connecting DC transmission line(s).

DCSystem.transmissionKind.description: Transmission kind of the DC system.

BoundaryPoint.description: <<EU>> Designates a connection point at which one or more model authority sets shall connect to. The location of the connection point as well as other properties are agreed between organisations responsible for the interconnection, hence all attributes of the class represent this agreement. It is primarily used in a boundary model authority set which can contain one or many BoundaryPoint-s among other Equipment-s and their connections. New: A BoundaryPoint is a CommonResponsibilityPoint that identifies a location in the power system model where two or more parties establish a common agreement on modelling responsibility. It defines the point at which the representation of adjacent model responsibilities connect and where the agreed boundary between modelling domains is established. Note: A BoundaryPoint represents the agreed location where modelling responsibility changes between organisations such as transmission system operators, distribution system operators, or other authorised model authorities. The BoundaryPoint may be located on an interconnection between networks or at an internal location within a substation or facility where modelling responsibility is divided between parties.

BoundaryPoint.BoundaryPointBorder.description: The BoundaryPointBorder that identifies the bilateral border relationship between the two parties responsible for this BoundaryPoint.

BoundaryPoint.partyOneResourceName.description:
Name used by the first party to refer to the shared or connected resource associated with the BoundaryPoint.
Note: This attribute records the name used in the model maintained by the first party for the resource or connection associated with the BoundaryPoint.
It shall only be used when exactly two parties share modelling responsibility at the BoundaryPoint.

BoundaryPoint.partyTwoResourceName.description:
Name used by the second party to refer to the shared or connected resource associated with the BoundaryPoint.
Note: This attribute records the name used in the model maintained by the second party for the resource or connection associated with the BoundaryPoint.
It shall only be used when exactly two parties share modelling responsibility at the BoundaryPoint.

CommonResponsibilityPoint.ConnectivityNo.description: The ConnectivityNode that anchors this CommonResponsiblityPoint in the AC grid model.

CommonResponsibilityPoint.DCNode.description: The DCNode that anchors this CommonResponsibilityPoint in the DC grid model.

CommonResponsibilityPoint.isDirectCurren.description:
Indicates whether the CommonResponsibilityPoint is anchored to a DC grid node.
If isDirectCurrent is true, the CommonResponsibilityPoint shall be associated to a DCNode and shall not be associated to a ConnectivityNode.
If isDirectCurrent is false, the CommonResponsibilityPoint shall be associated to a ConnectivityNode and shall not be associated to a DCNode.

BoundaryPointBorder.description:
A BoundaryPointBorder identifies a specific border relationship between exactly two parties for one or more BoundaryPoints. It provides a bilateral context used to describe and reference the two parties that share responsibility for coordinating and exchanging boundary information across that border.
Note:
A BoundaryPointBorder always represents exactly two parties, even when one or more associated BoundaryPoints are shared among more than two parties (for example in multi-party interconnections). In such cases, separate BoundaryPointBorder instances are used to represent each bilateral border relationship.
partyOne* and partyTwo* attributes are role-neutral and do not imply direction, hierarchy, or electrical flow.

URI.description: URI is a string following the rules defined by the W3C/IETF URI Planning Interest Group in a set of RFCs of which one is RFC 3305.

BoundaryPointBorder.partyOneDesignatorRe.description:
Globally unique reference to the designator associated with the first party, expressed as a URI.
Note: The reference may be a web URL identifying the designator or another persistent identifier expressed in URI form. When resolvable, the URI may provide additional linked data describing the designator.
The designator typically represents a jurisdictional or organisational designation that has empowered the party with the authority to provide the normative power system reference model.
This may refer to a country or to a specific regulatory or governing organisation.
Example: "https://vocabulary.uncefact.org/unlocode-countries#NO", "https://www.nve.no/reguleringsmyndigheten/"

BoundaryPointBorder.partyOneName.description:
Human-readable name of the first party participating in the border relationship.
Note: This name shall be suitable for unambiguous identification of the party within the exchange context.
If partyOneRef is provided, partyOneName shall be aligned with the party identified by partyOneRef.
Example: "Statnett"

BoundaryPointBorder.partyOneRef.description:
Globally unique reference to the first party participating in the border relationship, expressed as a URI.
Note: The reference may be a web URL identifying the party or another persistent identifier expressed in URI form. When resolvable, the URI may provide additional linked data describing the party.
Example: "https://energy.referencedata.eu/party/statnett", "urn:uuid:6f3e3a4e-3d4e-4b1a-a1e4-2b2c3f1a9a8d", "https://virksomhet.brreg.no/nb/oppslag/enheter/962986633"

BoundaryPointBorder.partyTwoDesignatorRe.description:
Globally unique reference to the designator associated with the second party, expressed as a URI.
Note: The reference may be a web URL identifying the designator or another persistent identifier expressed in URI form. When resolvable, the URI may provide additional linked data describing the designator.
The designator typically represents a jurisdictional or organisational designation that has empowered the party with the authority to provide the normative power system reference model.
This may refer to a country or to a specific regulatory or governing organisation.
Example: "https://vocabulary.uncefact.org/unlocode-countries#SE", "https://ei.se/"

BoundaryPointBorder.partyTwoName.description:
Human-readable name of the second party participating in the border relationship.
Note: This name shall be suitable for unambiguous identification of the party within the exchange context.
If partyTwoRef is provided, partyTwoName shall be aligned with the party identified by partyTwoRef.
Example: "SvenskaKraftnet"

BoundaryPointBorder.partyTwoRef.description:
Globally unique reference to the second party participating in the border relationship, expressed as a URI.
Note: The reference may be a web URL identifying the party or another persistent identifier expressed in URI form. When resolvable, the URI may provide additional linked data describing the party.
Example: "https://energy.referencedata.eu/party/svk", "urn:uuid:0d4c7c30-cc7e-4f8f-bb6c-6d6b8c6f7f62", "https://www.allabolag.se/foretag/svenska-kraftn%C3%A4t/sundbyberg/energif%C3%B6rs%C3%B6rjning/XF94VWI5YE1K"

BoundaryPointBorderLink.description:
A BoundaryPointBorderLink identifies the relationship between a specific BoundaryPoint and a specific BoundaryPointBorder. It is used when a BoundaryPoint is shared by more than two parties and therefore needs to be related to multiple bilateral BoundaryPointBorder instances
Note: When exactly two parties share a BoundaryPoint, the BoundaryPoint shall be directly associated with a single BoundaryPointBorder and BoundaryPointBorderLink shall not be used.
BoundaryPointBorderLink does not imply direction or hierarchy between the two parties; it only establishes that the BoundaryPoint participates in the bilateral border context.

BoundaryPointBorderLink.BoundaryPoint.description: BoundaryPoint that is linked to multiple BoundaryPointBorder through the BoundaryPointBorderLink.

BoundaryPointBorderLink.BoundaryPointBor.description: The BoundaryPointBorder that is given by the BoundaryPointBorderLink.

BoundaryPointBorderLink.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

CapacityCalculationRegion.description: Capacity calculation region is a coherent part of the interconnected system that is used for calculating the transmission capacity for a bidding zone or between bidding zones.

CapacityCalculationRegion.CoordinatedCap.description: Coordinated capacity calculator responsible for the capacity calculation of the region.

CapacityCalculationRegion.SecurityCoordi.description: The security coordinator responsible for the capacity calculation region.

Region.OverlappingZone.description: The overlapping zone which is impacted by this  region.

CircuitShare.description: Defines the share of the circuit which is part of an associated power transfer corridor.

CircuitShare.Circuit.description: The circuit that has a share of the power system corridor.

CircuitShare.PowerTransferCorridor.description: The power transfer corridor that has this circuit share.

CircuitShare.normalContributionFactor.description:
Normal contribution factor for the circuit which is part of a power transfer corridor.
The allowed value range is [0,100].

ClimateZone.description:
A geographically defined area characterised according to a climate classification and used as a spatial reference for representative meteorological, hydrological and marine conditions relevant to energy production, consumption and resource availability.
Note: ClimateZone provides selected climatological normal values as structured information and may reference time series for detailed climate, weather, hydrological and marine data. A normal value represents a climatological reference condition for the area. Time series may represent observed, historical, modelled, forecast, scenario or climatological data. Reference period, scenario, source, calculation method and other provenance information are represented separately.
ClimateZone may be used to associate energy resources and energy-system studies with climate-dependent conditions such as temperature, wind, solar irradiance, precipitation, snow, hydro inflow, extreme weather, waves, sea ice and sea currents.
Example: Climate study zones defined in the Pan-European Climate Database (PECD) for European energy-system modelling.

ClimateZoneClassificationKind.koppenGeig.description:
The Köppen-Geiger climate classification.
Note: The Köppen-Geiger classification categorises climates principally from long-term temperature and precipitation conditions and their seasonal distribution. Climate categories are represented by codes such as Cfb, Dfb or ET.

ClimateZoneClassificationKind.national.description:
A climate classification established or adopted by a national authority.
Note: National classifications may be established for building regulation, infrastructure design, agriculture, environmental assessment, energy planning or another nationally defined purpose. The responsible authority and classification version should be identifiable when relevant.

ClimateZoneClassificationKind.other.description:
A climate classification scheme other than those explicitly represented by ClimateZoneClassificationKind.
Note: The classification scheme should be identified using ClimateZone.otherClassification. The issuing organisation and applicable version should be identifiable when relevant.

ClimateZoneClassificationKind.pecd.description:
The climate-zone classification defined by the Pan-European Climate Database (PECD) for climate and energy-system studies.
Note: PECD climate zones support the spatial aggregation of climate variables and renewable-energy data used in European power-system studies. The applicable PECD version should be identified separately when relevant.

ClimateZoneClassificationKind.regional.description:
A climate classification established or adopted for a geographical region.
Note: A regional classification may be established by a sub-national, multi-national or other regional authority or organisation and may cover an area that does not correspond to national boundaries.

ClimateZone.classificationKind.description:
The kind of climate classification scheme according to which the ClimateZone is defined.
Note: The attribute identifies the classification scheme and not the code or identifier of the ClimateZone within that scheme. When the classification scheme is not explicitly represented by ClimateZoneClassificationKind, classificationKind shall be set to other and otherClassification shall identify the scheme.

ClimateZone.code.description:
The code or identifier assigned to the ClimateZone by the selected climate classification scheme.
Note: The interpretation of the code depends on ClimateZone.classificationKind. The code should conform to the identification or naming convention defined by the corresponding classification scheme.
Example: "Dfb" or "Cfb" for Köppen-Geiger, or a zone code defined by PECD or a national classification.

Irradiation.description:
Energy carried by electromagnetic radiation incident on a surface per unit area over a time interval.

Note: Intended for accumulated solar energy such as annual global, direct or diffuse solar irradiation.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualDiffuseSolarIrra.description:
The climatological normal total diffuse solar energy received per unit area during an annual period.
Note: The orientation of the applicable reference surface is defined by the data specification or provenance information.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualDirectSolarIrrad.description:
The climatological normal total direct solar energy received per unit area during an annual period.
Note: The orientation of the applicable reference surface is defined by the data specification or provenance information.

Length.description: Unit of length. It shall be a positive value or zero.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualEvaporation.description: The climatological normal amount of water returned to the atmosphere through evaporation and evapotranspiration during an annual period, expressed as an equivalent depth of water.

Decimal.description: Decimal is the base-10 notational system for representing real numbers.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualExtremeFireDange.description:
The climatological normal number of days during an annual period classified as having extreme fire danger.
Note: The criterion for extreme fire danger is determined by the applicable wildfire index and classification identified through the data provenance. The CIM model does not prescribe a specific threshold.
Example: When the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) classification is applied, extreme fire danger corresponds to an Canadian Fire Weather Index (FWI) of 50 or greater. A value of "18.5" therefore indicates a climatological normal of 18.5 days per year with FWI greater than or equal to 50.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualFreezingPrecipit.description: The climatological normal number of days during an annual period with freezing precipitation.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualFrostDays.description:
The climatological normal number of frost days during an annual period.
Note: The threshold used to define a frost day is determined by the applicable meteorological specification, normally using minimum air temperature.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualGlobalSolarIrrad.description:
The climatological normal total global solar energy received per unit area during an annual period.
Note: Global solar irradiation includes direct and diffuse solar radiation incident on the applicable reference surface. For a horizontal reference surface it corresponds to global horizontal irradiation.
Example: A value may be expressed as annual solar energy per square metre, such as MJ/m2 or an equivalent unit.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualHailDays.description: The climatological normal number of days during an annual period on which hail occurs.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualHeatwaveDays.description:
The climatological normal number of days during an annual period occurring as part of a heatwave.
Note: A heatwave represents unusually high temperature persisting for a defined minimum duration. The temperature criteria and minimum duration are specified by the applicable climate dataset or scenario.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualHighAvalancheDan.description:
The climatological normal number of days during an annual period classified as having high avalanche danger.
Note: The criterion for high avalanche danger is determined by the applicable avalanche methodology and classification identified through data provenance. The CIM model does not prescribe a particular threshold.
Example: "8.5" when high avalanche danger is defined as EAWS danger level 4 or 5.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualHotDays.description:
The climatological normal number of hot days during an annual period.
Note: A hot day is defined using the threshold specified by the applicable climate dataset or scenario. The threshold may be an absolute temperature or a percentile relative to the local climatology.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualHydroInflow.description:
The climatological normal energy equivalent of natural hydro inflow associated with hydro resources in the ClimateZone during an annual period.
Note: The value represents the potential energy associated with natural inflow and not generated electrical energy. This representation is intended for aggregated power-system and adequacy studies where hydro inflow is expressed as an energy quantity.
Example: The value may represent the annual energy equivalent of natural inflow to reservoir hydropower resources within the ClimateZone.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualIcingDays.description:
The climatological normal number of days during an annual period with meteorological conditions producing significant icing.
Note: The criteria defining an icing day are provided by the applicable data specification or provenance information. The attribute may be used to characterise climate-related availability risk for overhead lines, wind turbines and other exposed equipment.

CountPerArea.description:
Number of discrete occurrences or events per unit area.

Note: Intended for spatial event densities such as lightning density. A new UnitSymbol countPerm2 is required if this quantity is represented as a CIMDatatype with an explicit unit.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualLightningDensity.description:
The climatological normal number of lightning events per unit area during an annual period.
Note: The definition of a lightning event, for example a flash or ground strike, is determined by the applicable data specification.
Example: 1.5 flashes/km2 indicates that an average of 1.5 lightning flashes per square kilometre occurs during a normal year.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualMaxDailyPrecipit.description:
The climatological normal of the maximum precipitation accumulated during a single day within an annual period.
Note: This value provides an indication of exposure to extreme precipitation that is not represented by normalAnnualPrecipitation alone.
Example: A value of 85 mm indicates that the normal annual maximum one-day precipitation is approximately 85 mm.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualMaxSignificantWa.description:
The climatological normal of the maximum significant wave height occurring during an annual period.
Note: This value characterises exposure to severe sea states relevant to accessibility, equipment loading and availability of offshore resources.

Temperature.description: Value of temperature in degrees Celsius.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualMaxTempAt2m.description:
The climatological normal of the maximum air temperature at 2 metres above ground level occurring during an annual period.
Note: This represents an annual extreme maximum rather than the normal mean of daily maximum temperatures.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualMaxWindGustAt10m.description:
The climatological normal of the maximum wind gust at 10 metres above ground level occurring during an annual period.
Note: This value characterises exposure to strong short-duration wind events rather than the normal wind resource.
Example: A value of 31 m/s indicates that the climatological normal annual maximum gust is approximately 31 m/s.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualMinTempAt2m.description:
The climatological normal of the minimum air temperature at 2 metres above ground level occurring during an annual period.
Note: This represents an annual extreme minimum rather than the normal mean of daily minimum temperatures.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualPotentialEvapora.description:
The climatological normal potential amount of water that could be returned to the atmosphere by evaporation during an annual period, expressed as an equivalent depth of water.
Note: Potential evaporation represents atmospheric evaporative demand and is not limited by actual water availability.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualPrecipitation.description:
The climatological normal total precipitation received during an annual period.
Note: Precipitation includes liquid and solid precipitation and is expressed as an equivalent depth of water over the area.
Example: 1100 mm represents an annual precipitation volume equivalent to 1100 litres of water per square metre.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualRainfall.description: The climatological normal amount of liquid precipitation received during an annual period.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualRunoff.description:
The climatological normal runoff during an annual period, expressed as an equivalent depth of water over the area.
Note: Runoff represents water leaving the land surface and subsurface drainage system after precipitation, snowmelt, evaporation, infiltration and storage effects.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualSeaIceDays.description:
The climatological normal number of days during an annual period for which sea ice is present within the ClimateZone.
Note: The minimum ice concentration or other criterion used to determine sea-ice presence is defined by the applicable data specification.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualSnowfall.description:
The climatological normal amount of solid precipitation received during an annual period, expressed as its equivalent amount of liquid water.
Note: The value represents water input from snowfall rather than physical snow depth.
Example: 500 mm means that the annual snowfall normally contains an amount of water equivalent to a 500 mm layer of liquid water.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualSnowmelt.description:
The climatological normal amount of water released by melting snow during an annual period.
Note: Snowmelt is expressed as the equivalent depth of liquid water produced from the snowpack.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualSunshineDuration.description:
The climatological normal total duration of sunshine during an annual period.
Example: 1650 h represents approximately 1650 hours of sunshine during a normal year.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualThunderDays.description: The climatological normal number of days during an annual period on which thunder is observed.

ClimateZone.normalAnnualTropicalNights.description:
The climatological normal number of tropical nights during an annual period.
Note: A tropical night is a night for which the minimum air temperature remains above the applicable threshold. A threshold of 20 degC is commonly used in European climate indicators, but the applicable threshold is defined by the dataset or scenario.

ClimateZone.normalCloudCover.description: The climatological normal proportion of the sky covered by cloud.

ClimateZone.normalDewPointTempAt2m.description:
The climatological normal dew-point temperature at 2 metres above ground level.
Note: Dew-point temperature indicates atmospheric moisture content and may be used together with air temperature to derive relative humidity and icing conditions.

ClimateZone.normalMaxSeaCurrentSpeed.description:
The climatological normal maximum sea-current speed within the ClimateZone.
Note: The value characterises strong current conditions relevant to marine-energy resource potential and equipment loading. The applicable depth and method for determining the maximum are defined by the source dataset or provenance information.

ClimateZone.normalMaxSeaIceThickness.description:
The climatological normal maximum sea-ice thickness during the seasonal cycle within a marine ClimateZone.
Note: This attribute is primarily relevant for high-latitude offshore areas and may be used when assessing accessibility and availability of offshore resources.
Example: 0.8 m indicates that the normal seasonal maximum sea-ice thickness is approximately 0.8 metres.

ClimateZone.normalMaxSnowWater.description:
The climatological normal of the maximum amount of water stored in the snowpack during the seasonal cycle.
Note: Snow water represents the water content of the snowpack expressed as an equivalent depth of liquid water. The value characterises seasonal snow storage and is more hydrologically meaningful than physical snow depth.
Example: 450 mm indicates that the normal seasonal maximum snowpack contains an amount of water equivalent to a 450 mm layer of liquid water.

ClimateZone.normalPopulationWeightedTemp.description:
The climatological normal population-weighted air temperature at 2 metres above ground level.
Note: Population-weighted temperature is a spatially aggregated temperature in which locations with a higher population are given greater weight. It provides a representative temperature for the conditions experienced by the population and is particularly relevant for energy-demand modelling. The population dataset, weighting method and other provenance information are represented separately.

ClimateZone.normalRelativeHumidityAt2m.description: The climatological normal relative humidity at 2 metres above ground level.

ClimateZone.normalSeaCurrentSpeed.description:
The climatological normal speed of the sea-water current within the ClimateZone.
Note: Sea-current speed depends on depth. The applicable depth or vertical reference is defined by the source dataset or provenance information.

ClimateZone.normalSeaSurfaceTemp.description: The climatological normal sea-surface temperature within a marine ClimateZone.

ClimateZone.normalSignificantWaveHeight.description:
The climatological normal significant wave height within a marine ClimateZone.
Note: Significant wave height is a statistical representation of sea state commonly approximated as the mean height of the highest one-third of waves.
Example: A value of 2.1 m represents a climate where the normal significant wave height is approximately 2.1 metres.

ClimateZone.normalSurfacePressure.description: The climatological normal atmospheric pressure at the surface.

ClimateZone.normalTempAt2m.description:
The climatological normal air temperature at 2 metres above ground level.
Note: Two metres above ground is the standard reference height for near-surface air temperature.

ClimateZone.normalWavePeriod.description:
The climatological normal representative wave period within a marine ClimateZone.
Note: The precise wave-period statistic, such as mean or peak period, is determined by the applicable data specification.

ClimateZone.normalWindSpeedAt100m.description:
The climatological normal wind speed at 100 metres above ground level.
Note: Wind speed at 100 metres is commonly available in meteorological and energy datasets and provides a useful indication of the wind resource for electricity generation.

ClimateZone.normalWindSpeedAt10m.description:
The climatological normal wind speed at 10 metres above ground level.
Note: Ten metres above ground is the conventional reference height for near-surface meteorological wind observations.

ClimateZone.otherClassification.description:
The name or identifier of the climate classification scheme when ClimateZone.classificationKind equals other.
Note: This attribute shall only be used when ClimateZone.classificationKind is set to other. It identifies the classification scheme that is not explicitly represented by ClimateZoneClassificationKind. The value should be sufficiently descriptive to identify the scheme.
Example: "Trewartha Climate Classification", "Holdridge Life Zones", "Thornthwaite Climate Classification", "Company Internal Climate Zones".

ClimateZone.ref.description:
A URI identifying the ClimateZone within the applicable climate classification scheme.
Note: The URI identifies the classified zone or concept rather than the classification scheme itself. It may be used as an alternative to code when the classification is published as linked data or another URI-based controlled vocabulary. Both code and ref may be provided when the classification defines both representations.
Example: "https://example.org/climate/pecd/zone-12" as an illustrative URI identifying a climate zone within a PECD classification.

ClosedDistributionSystemOperator.description: A system operator which distributes electricity (or gas) within a geographically confined industrial, commercial or shared services and does not supply household customers.

OrganisationRole.globalLocationNumber.description:
The Global Location Number (GLN) is part of the GS1 systems of standards. GLN is a 13-digit number structured that include GS1 Company Prefix, Location Reference (N1-N12) and Check Digit (N13).
GS1 is a neutral, not-for-profit, international organisation that develops and maintains standards for supply and demand chains across multiple sectors.

CogenerationPlant.description: A set of thermal generating units for the production of electrical energy and process steam (usually from the output of the steam turbines). The steam sendout is typically used for industrial purposes or for municipal heating and cooling. Update:

PowerPlant.deadbandMaxP.description: The  upper active-power boundaries of the range around zero in which continuous power-plant operation is not supported.

PowerPlant.deadbandMinP.description: The lower  active-power boundaries of the range around zero in which continuous power-plant operation is not supported.

PowerPlant.maxOperatingP.description: The maximum net active power at which the power plant is designed to operate.

PowerPlant.minOperatingP.description: The minimum signed net active power at which the power plant is designed to operate.

PowerPlant.nominalP.description: The reference active power capacity of the power plant.

CombinedCyclePlant.description:
A thermal power plant in which two or more thermal generating units are operated in combination so that heat from one thermodynamic cycle is used as an energy input to another thermodynamic cycle.
Note: A combined cycle plant normally includes at least one combustion-turbine generating unit and one steam-turbine generating unit. Dependencies between the thermal generating units may define their relative activation, deactivation and operation.

CombinedCyclePlant.kind.description: The configuration used to arrange and coordinate the thermal generating units of the combined cycle plant.

CompensatorController.description: Compensator controller is controlling the equipment to optimize the use of the compensators.

CompressedAirEnergyStoragePlant.description: An energy storage plant in which energy is stored by compressing air and is subsequently recovered by expanding the compressed air to support electrical generation. The plant may use stored thermal energy, external heat or fuel combustion during the energy recovery process.

EnergyStoragePlant.maxCapacity.description: The maximum amount of energy that may be stored by the energy storage plant within its defined operating limits.

EnergyStoragePlant.minCapacity.description: The minimum amount of stored energy within the normal operating range of the energy storage plant.

EnergyStoragePlant.nominalCapacity.description: The reference amount of stored energy that the energy storage plant is intended to operate with under normal conditions.

ConnectivityNode.description: Connectivity nodes are points where terminals of AC conducting equipment are connected together with zero impedance.

ControlArea.description:
A control area is a grouping of generating units and/or loads and a cutset of tie lines (as terminals) which may be used for a variety of purposes including automatic generation control, power flow solution area interchange control specification, and input to load forecasting. All generation and load within the area defined by the terminals on the border are considered in the area interchange control. Note that any number of overlapping control area specifications can be superimposed on the physical model. The following general principles apply to ControlArea:
1.  The control area orientation for net interchange is positive for an import, negative for an export.
2.  The control area net interchange is determined by summing flows in Terminals. The Terminals are identified by creating a set of TieFlow objects associated with a ControlArea object. Each TieFlow object identifies one Terminal.
3.  In a single network model, a tie between two control areas must be modelled in both control area specifications, such that the two representations of the tie flow sum to zero.
4.  The normal orientation of Terminal flow is positive for flow into the conducting equipment that owns the Terminal. (i.e. flow from a bus into a device is positive.) However, the orientation of each flow in the control area specification must align with the control area convention, i.e. import is positive. If the orientation of the Terminal flow referenced by a TieFlow is positive into the control area, then this is confirmed by setting TieFlow.positiveFlowIn flag TRUE. If not, the orientation must be reversed by setting the TieFlow.positiveFlowIn flag FALSE.

ControlArea.OutageCoordinationRegion.description: The outage coordination region that has this control area.

ControlArea.PartOf.description: The control area that is part of this control area.

ControlArea.SystemOperator.description: The system operator that operates this control area.

CoordinatedCapacityCalculator.description: A post that coordinates and executes the task of calculating transmission capacity.

CrossZonalDCPole.description: A CrossZonalNetworkElement represented by an HVDC pole participating in the transfer of electrical power between two bidding zones.

CrossZonalDCPole.DCPole.description: Direct current pole represented by the CrossZonalDCPole.

CrossZonalNetworkElement.BiddingZoneBord.description: The directional bidding zone borders associated with the cross-zonal network element. Exactly two borders shall be referenced, representing the same bidding zone pair in opposite directions.

CrossZonalNetworkElement.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

CrossZonalLine.description: A CrossZonalNetworkElement represented by an AC line participating in the transfer of electrical power between two bidding zones.

CrossZonalLine.Line.description: The AC line represented by the CrossZonalLine.

CrossZonalPowerTransformer.description: A CrossZonalNetworkElement represented by a power transformer participating in the transfer of electrical power between two bidding zones.

CrossZonalPowerTransformer.PowerTransfor.description: Power transformer represented by the CrossZonalPowerTransformer.

CurrentControlFunction.description: Current control function is a function block that calculates the operating point of the controlled equipment  to achieve the target current.

CurrentDroopControlFunction.description: Current droop control function is a function block that calculates the operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target current.

CurrentDroopControlFunction.droopCapacit.description: Droop in capacitive region. The unit is V/A.

CurrentDroopControlFunction.droopInducti.description: Droop in inductive region. The unit is V/A.

CurrentFlow.description: Electrical current with sign convention: positive flow is out of the conducting equipment into the connectivity node. Can be both AC and DC.

CurrentDroopOverride.description:
Current droop override uses the following logic:
- When the current exceeds a threshold the device executes the following transitions: 1) When injecting an inductive voltage or in monitoring mode the device tends to inject a voltage proportional to the difference between the line current and the aforementioned threshold. 2) When injecting a capacitive voltage the device transitions to monitoring mode. 
- If the aforementioned proportional voltage is lower than the initial one, the voltage injection remains unchanged. 
Current droop override is not applied when the device operates in currentDroop mode.

CurrentDroopOverride.SSSCController.description: The SSSC controller to which this CurrentDroopOverride applies to.

CurrentDroopOverride.droopCapacitive.description: Droop in capacitive region. The unit is V/A.

CurrentDroopOverride.droopInductive.description: Droop in inductive region. The unit is V/A.

CurrentDroopOverride.mRID.description:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

CurveData.description: Multi-purpose data points for defining a curve.  The use of this generic class is discouraged if a more specific class can be used to specify the X and Y axis values along with their specific data types.

CurveData.Curve.description: The curve of  this curve data point.

CurveData.xvalue.description: The data value of the X-axis variable,  depending on the X-axis units.

CurveData.y1value.description: The data value of the  first Y-axis variable, depending on the Y-axis units.

CurveData.y2value.description: The data value of the second Y-axis variable (if present), depending on the Y-axis units.

DCActivePowerControlFunction.description: Direct current active power control function is a function block that calculates operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target active power.

DCBiPole.description: DC system bipole (IEC 60633), which is part of an DC system consisting of two independently operable DC system poles, which during normal operation, exhibit opposite direct voltage polarities with respect to earth.

DCBiPole.BipolarDCSystem.description: Bipolar DC system that has this DC bipole.

DCBreaker.description: A breaker within a DC system.

Voltage.description: Electrical voltage, can be both AC and DC.

DCConductingEquipment.ratedUdc.description: Rated DC device voltage. The attribute shall be a positive value. It is configuration data used in power flow.

DCConductingEquipment.ratedCurrent.description:
The maximum continuous current carrying capacity in amps governed by the device material and construction.
The attribute shall be a positive value.

DCSwitch.normalOpen.description: The attribute is used in cases when no Measurement for the status value is present. If the DCSwitch has a status measurement the Discrete.normalValue is expected to match with the DCSwitch.normalOpen.

DCBusbar.description: A busbar within a DC system.

DCBypassSwitch.description: By-pass switch (IEC 60633) is a high-speed DC switch connected across each converter valve group in DC schemes using more than one independent converter per pole, designed to close rapidly to bypass a converter group that is being taken out of service and commutate the current back into a valve group that is being taken back in service. A by-pass switch may also be used for prolonged shunting of the bridge(s).

DCChopper.description: Low resistance equipment used in the internal DC circuit to balance voltages. It has typically positive and negative pole terminals and a ground.

DCConverterParallelingSwitch.description: Converter paralleling switch (IEC 60633) is a high-speed DC switch connected in series with each converter at the DC terminal in DC schemes where two or more converters are connected in parallel onto a common pole conductor, designed to allow additional converter(s) to be connected in parallel or disconnected without affecting the load current in the other converter.

DCConverterUnit.description: Indivisible operative unit comprising all equipment between the point of common coupling on the AC side and the point of common coupling – DC side, essentially one or more converters, together with one or more converter transformers, converter control equipment, essential protective and switching devices and auxiliaries, if any, used for conversion.

DCConverterUnit.Substation.description: The containing substation of the DC converter unit.

DCConverterUnit.DCPole.description: The DC pole that has this DC converter unit.

DCConverterUnit.DCSubstation.description: DC substation that has one or more DC converter units.

DCConverterUnit.PointOfCommonCoupling.description: The PointOfCommonCoupling that represents the electrical reference location where this DCConverterUnit interacts with the connected AC or DC grid.

DCCurrentControlFunction.description: DC current control function is a function block that calculates the operating point of the controlled equipment  to achieve the target current.

PU.description: Per Unit - a positive or negative value referred to a defined base. Values typically range from -10 to +10.

DCCurrentControlFunction.droop.description: Droop constant. The pu value is obtained as D [kV/MW] x Sb / Ubdc. The attribute shall be a positive value.

DCCurrentControlFunction.droopCompensati.description: Compensation constant. Used to compensate for voltage drop when controlling voltage at a distant bus. The attribute shall be a positive value.

DCDisconnector.description: A disconnector within a DC system.

DCEarthReturnTransferSwitch.description: Earth return transfer switch (IEC 60633) DC commutation switch used to transfer DC current from a metallic return path to an earth return path. In some applications, this function is performed by a by-pass switch. Although the term "earth return transfer breaker" has been widely used in the industry for many years, it is misleading since such switches have no ability to interrupt fault current.

DCEquivalentInjection.description: This class represents direct current equivalent injections (generation or load).

DCExtinctionAngleControlFunction.description: Direct current extinction angle control function is a function block that calculates operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target extinction angle.

DCFiringAngleControlFunction.description: Direct current firing angle control function is a function block that calculates operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target firing angle.

DCGround.description: A ground within a DC system.

DCHarmonicFilter.description: DC harmonic filter (IEC 60633) is a filter which, in conjunction with the DC reactor(s) and with the DC surge capacitor(s), if any, serves the primary function of reducing (current or voltage) ripple on the DC transmission line and/or earth electrode line.

DCLine.description: Overhead lines and/or cables connecting two or more HVDC substations.

DCLine.DCPole.description: The DC pole that has this DC line.

DCLineParallelingSwitch.description: Line paralleling switch (IEC 60633) DC commutation switch placed in series with one or more high-voltage pole conductors, allowing two or more lines to be connected in parallel or to revert to single-line operation while conducting load current.

DCLineSegment.description: A wire or combination of wires not insulated from one another, with consistent electrical characteristics, used to carry direct current between points in the DC region of the power system.

DCMetalicReturnSwitch.description: Metallic return transfer switch (IEC 60633) is a DC commutation switch used to transfer DC current from an earth return path to a metallic return path. Although the term "metallic return transfer breaker" has been widely used in the industry for many years, it is misleading since such switches have no ability to interrupt fault current.

DCNeutralBusGroundingSwitch.description: Neutral bus grounding switch (IEC 60633) or a neutral bus earthing switch is a DC commutation switch connected from the neutral bus to the station earth mat on a bipolar DC scheme, designed to provide a temporary earth connection in the event of an open circuit fault on the electrode line until the imbalance of current between the two poles can be reduced to a safe minimum level or the electrode line connection can be restored.

DCNeutralBusSwitch.description: Neutral bus switch (IEC 60633) is a DC commutation switch connected in series with the neutral bus on a bipolar DC scheme, designed to commutate current out of the pole conductor or neutral bus and into the electrode line or dedicated metallic return conductor or earth in response to a fault in a converter or neutral bus.

DCNode.description: DC nodes are points where terminals of DC conducting equipment are connected together with zero impedance.

DCPole.description:
The direct current (DC) system pole (IEC 60633) is part of a DC system consisting of all the equipment in the DC substations and the interconnecting transmission lines, if any, which during normal operation exhibit a common direct voltage polarity with respect to earth.
It includes active power, reactive power and participation factor to be able to schedule top down (using DCTieCorridor and participation factor to provide schedule on the DCPole) and bottom up (aggregation of DCPole to DCTieCorridor). Only one approach can be used at a time.

DCPole.AsymmetricMonopolarDCSystem.description: Asymmetric monopolar DC system that has this DC pole.

DCPole.DCBiPole.description: DC system bipole that has two independently operatable DC system poles.

DCPole.DCTieCorridor.description: The DCTieCorridor that has this DC pole.

DCPole.normalParticipationFactor.description:
Normal participation factor describing the entity part of the active power provided by a collection of entities (e.g. an active power forecast to a collection of entities is divided to each of the member entity according to the participation factor). Must be a positive value.
In the case of a sharing strategy, the distribution is following entities value (V) equals aggregated value (T) divided by sum of participation factors (PF), i.e. V=T/sum(PF). 
In the case of priority strategy, the item with the lowest number gets allocated energy first.

DCPulseWidthModulationControlFunction.description: Direct current pulse width modulation control function is a function block that calculates operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target pulse width modulation.

DCSeriesDevice.description: A series device within the DC system, typically a reactor used for filtering or smoothing.  Needed for transient and short circuit studies.

DCShunt.description: A shunt device within the DC system, typically used for filtering.  Needed for transient and short circuit studies.

DCSmoothingReactor.description: Reactor (IEC 60633) connected in series with a converter unit or converter units on the DC side for the primary purpose of smoothing the direct current and reducing current transients.

DCSmoothingReactorArrester.description: Arrester (IEC 60633) connected between the terminals of a smoothing reactor.

DCSubstation.description: DC substation or DC converter station (IEC 60633) is part of an DC system which consists of one or more converter units installed in a single location together with buildings, reactors, filters, reactive power supply, control, monitoring, protective, measuring and auxiliary equipment. A DC substation forming part of an DC transmission system may be referred to as an DC transmission substation.

DCSubstation.Substation.description: Substation that contains this DC susbstation.

DCSubstation.isTapping.description: DC tapping substation (IEC 60633) is a DC substation, mainly used for inversion, with a rating which is a small fraction of that of the rectifier(s) in the system.

DCSubstationBipole.description: Part of a bipolar DC system (IEC 60633) contained within a DC substation.

DCSubstationBipole.DCSubstation.description: DC substation that contains this DC substation bipole part.

DCSubstationPole.description: Part of an DC system pole (IEC 60633) which is contained within a DC substation.

DCSubstationPole.DCSubstation.description: DC substation that contains this DC substation pole part.

DCSwitch.description: A switch within the DC system.

DCTerminal.description: An electrical connection point to generic DC conducting equipment.

DCTerminal.ACDCConverter.description: The ACDCConverter that has this external DCTerminal.

DCTerminal.polarity.description: Represents the normal network polarity condition.

DCTieCorridor.description:
A collection of one or more direct current poles that connect two different control areas.
DCTieCorridor is linked to its own SchedulingArea. The active and reactive power is given by the SchedulingArea. The flow direction is provided by the link with the directional bidding zone.

DCTieCorridor.SchedulingArea.description: The scheduling area that has this DC tie corridor.

RampingPrincipleKind.continuous.description: Continuous ramping principle is applied between two scheduled time point. For instance, from 10 MW to 70 MW over one hour the change is 1 MW/min.

RampingPrincipleKind.fifteenMinutes.description: Fifteen minutes ramping principle. Ramping starts 15 minutes before the schedule time point and ends 15 minutes after. For instance, if the schedule time point is 19:30h it starts at 19:15h and ends at 19:45h.

RampingPrincipleKind.fiveMinutes.description: Five minutes ramping principle. Ramping starts five minutes before the schedule time point and ends five minutes after. For instance, if the schedule time point is 19:30h it starts at 19:25h and ends at 19:35h.

RampingPrincipleKind.maxContinuous.description: Maximum continuous ramping principle. The schedule is kept as long as possible and the maximum ramping rate is used to get from one point to another, symmetrically around the schedule time points. For example, there is 40 MW change in the schedule the maximum ramp rate is 20 MW/min the ramping starts 1 min before (e.g. 19:29h) and finishes 1 min after (e.g. 19:31h).

RampingPrincipleKind.tenMinutes.description: Ten minutes ramping principle. Ramping starts 10 minutes before the schedule time point and ends 10 minutes after. For instance, if the schedule time point is 19:30h it starts at 19:20h and ends at 19:40h.

DCTieCorridor.rampingKind.description: Ramping principle is used to define a transition from one scheduled value to next one.

DCVoltageControlFunction.description: DC voltage control function is a function block that calculate the operating point of the controlled equipment to achieve the target voltage.

DCVoltageSource.description: DC conducting equipment capable of establishing, maintaining, or controlling a DC voltage difference between connected DC terminals.

Inductance.description: Inductive part of reactance (imaginary part of impedance), at rated frequency.

DCVoltageSource.internalInductance.description: Equivalent internal inductance of the DC voltage source.

DCVoltageSource.internalResistance.description: Equivalent internal resistance of the DC voltage source.

DiodeValve.description: The diode is uncontrolled valve. It is always in a "ready" state and conducts automatically when the voltage at the anode is higher than the cathode. It cannot be turned off or on by an external signal.

DCValve.valveU0.description:
Represents the threshold or on-state voltage across the valve during conduction. The value is used in conduction loss calculations for converter valves. Approximate valve conduction losses may be calculated using: P_loss ˜ U0 × I
where:
U0 = valve forward voltage (valveU0)
I = valve current
Converter-level losses may be approximated from the combined contribution of associated valves, for example:
P_converter_loss ˜ N × U0 × I
where:
N = number of conducting valves
U0 = valve forward voltage
I = valve current.

DirectCurrentBipoleController.description: DC system bipole control that is the control system of a bipole in accordance with IEC 60633.

DirectCurrentBipoleController.DirectCurr.description: Direct current master controller which has direct current bipole controllers.

DirectCurrentCircuit.description: A direct current circuit is a circuit consists of direct current equipment.

Circuit.positiveFlowIn.description: True, if the positive value on the terminal shall be considered flow into the circuit. False, if the positive value on the terminal shall be considered flow out of the circuit.

DirectCurrentMasterController.description:
Direct current system control is a control system which governs the operation of an entire DC system consisting of more than one DC substation and performs those functions of controlling, monitoring and protection which require information from more than one substation. This can also be a multiterminal control which is a DC system control for more that two DC substations or a DC master control, which is a general concept for control coordination of a DC system. The DC master control may be implemented at the bipole and/or pole level as defined in IEC 60633. 
The DC system control/multiterminal control/master control is part of the hierarchical structure of an HVDC control system that has an integrated AC/DC system control as the highest level of control which governs the integrated operation of AC and DC systems of a power system. This control system is under the responsibility of the system operator.

DirectCurrentMasterController.DCTieCorri.description: DCTieCorridor controlled by this direct current master controller.

DirectCurrentPoleController.description: DC system pole control, which is the control system of a pole in accordance with IEC 60633.

DirectCurrentPoleController.DCPole.description: DC pole that is controlled by a DC pole controller.

DirectCurrentPoleController.DirectCurren.description: DC bipole controller that controls this DC pole controller.
DC master controller that has a DC pole controller.

DirectCurrentSubstationBipoleController.description: Control system of a substation bipole (IEC 60633).

DirectCurrentSubstationBipoleController..description: DC substation bipole that is controlled by a DC substation bipole controller.

DirectCurrentSubstationController.Multit.description: Multiterminal control that controls more than two DC substation controllers.

DirectCurrentSubstationPoleController.description: Control system of a substation pole (IEC 60633).

DirectCurrentSubstationPoleController.DC.description: DC substation pole that is controlled by a DC substation pole controller.

DirectCurrentSystemOperator.description: System operator of the direct current pole. There are typically one or two system operators that are operating either the control area at one side or the control areas at both sides of the direct current pole. In some cases it is operated by an operator from the connected control areas.

DistributionSystemOperator.description: A system operator that is responsible for operating of energy distribution network from transmission level down to low voltage levels including the connection to household.

DurationOverloadLimitCurve.description:
A curve or functional relationship between
- the overload duration independent variable (X-axis), and 
- temporary overloading (TATL) limiting dependent (Y-axis) variables.

EdgeControlArea.description: An EdgeControlArea representing the local, site-level (edge) operational domain that coordinates one or more Installations and their connections. It is typically operated by an edge operator (e.g., a person/company operating a campus, mall, microgrid, or prosumer cluster) and supports local monitoring, control, scheduling, and limits—both islanded and grid-connected.

EdgeSchedulingArea.description:
An EdgeSchedulingArea is a electrical area that is part of a SubSchedulingArea with one or more Installations connected.
It serves as the smallest energy level scheduling, forecasting and aggregated measurement used for coordinating energy production, consumption, and storage across its constituent connections.
An EdgeSchedulingArea may represent physical locations with multiple grid connection, such as a shopping mall, university campus, industrial facility, or private microgrid that are normally connected to the grid.

SchedulingArea.BiddingZone.description: The bidding zone related to this scheduling area.

SchedulingArea.ControlArea.description: The control area for this scheduling area.

SchedulingArea.EnergyCoordinationRegion.description: The energy coordination region that has this scheduling area.

SchedulingArea.GridPowerCapacity.description: Grid Power capacity of this shaduling area.

SchedulingArea.LoadFrequencyControlArea.description: The load frequency control area which has this scheduling area.

SchedulingArea.PartOf.description: The scheduling area is part of this scheduling area.

SchedulingArea.SynchronousArea.description: The synchronous are that has this scheduling area.

SchedulingArea.SystemOperator.description: The system operator for this scheduling area.

SchedulingArea.isIslandingEnabled.description: Identifies if the area can operate in island operation. If true, the area is enabled (capable) of operating as an electrical island. If false, the area does not have the capability or it is not enabled to operate as an electrical island.

SchedulingArea.isMeteringGridArea.description: Identifies if the area is settlement metered for all import and export to the area. If true, the area is metered area. If false, it is not.

SchedulingArea.normalParticipationFactor.description:
Normal participation factor describing the entity part of the active power provided by a collection of entities (e.g. an active power forecast to a collection of entities is divided to each of the member entity according to the participation factor). Must be a positive value.
In the case of a sharing strategy, the distribution is following entities value (V) equals aggregated value (T) divided by sum of participation factors (PF), i.e. V=T/sum(PF). 
In the case of priority strategy, the item with the lowest number gets allocated energy first.

ElectricalChargingUnit.description: A unit that supplies electrical power for charging electrical non-stationary entities, e.g. electrical vehicle, trucks, buses, ferries, boats and airplanes. The characteristic is that the energy consumption is highly schedule dependent.

EnergyAlignmentCoordinator.description: A post that is responsible for alignment of forecast and schedule energy to a given energy coordination region.

EnergyBlockComponent.description: Energy block component where the energy group is distributed according to the energy block order of each energy component in an energy group.

EnergyComponent.EnergyConsumer.description: The energy consumer that relates to this energy component.

EnergyComponent.EnergyResourceGroupCapac.description: The Energy Resource Group Capacity that has this energy component.

EnergyComponent.GeneratingUnit.description: The generating unit that is part of this energy component.

EnergyComponent.HydroPump.description: The hydro pump that relates to this energy component.

EnergyComponent.PowerElectronicsUnit.description: The power electronics unit that relates to this energy component.

EnergyBlockOrder.description: The energy block order is a block (an amount) of energy that forms the sequence of orders that are going to be distributed to an energy block component.

EnergyBlockOrder.EnergyBlockComponent.description: The energy block component that has this energy block order.

EnergyBlockOrder.normalSequence.description:
Normal sequence represents the local order of the power block order.

The sequence order for a given block dispatch instruction. The sequence number need to be unique for a given block dispatch instruction, e.g. two order in the same instruction cannot have the same sequence.

Duration.description: Duration as "PnYnMnDTnHnMnS" which conforms to ISO 8601, where nY expresses a number of years, nM a number of months, nD a number of days. The letter T separates the date expression from the time expression and, after it, nH identifies a number of hours, nM a number of minutes and nS a number of seconds. The number of seconds could be expressed as a decimal number, but all other numbers are integers.

EnergyConsumer.description:
Generic user of energy - a  point of consumption on the power system model.
EnergyConsumer.pfixed, .qfixed, .pfixedPct and .qfixedPct have meaning only if there is no LoadResponseCharacteristic associated with EnergyConsumer or if LoadResponseCharacteristic.exponentModel is set to False.

EnergyConsumer.maxEconomicP.description: Maximum high economic active power limit, that should not exceed the maximum operating active power limit.

EnergyConsumer.minEconomicP.description: Low economic active power limit that shall be greater than or equal to the minimum operating active power limit.

EnergyConsumer.normalParticipationFactor.description:
Participation factor describing the entity part of the active power provided by a collection of entities (e.g. an active power forecast to a collection of entities is divided to each of the member entity according to the participation factor). Must be a positive value.
In the case of a sharing strategy, the distribution is following entities value (V) equals aggregated value (T) divided by sum of participation factors (PF), i.e. V=T/sum(PF). 
In the case of priority strategy, the item with the lowest number gets allocated energy first.

EnergyCoordinationRegion.description: A region that has a common organisation or a service that is responsible for alignment of forecast and scheduling of energy.

EnergyCoordinationRegion.EnergyAlignment.description: The energy alignment coordinator that operates this energy coordination region.

EnergyExchangePoint.description:
An EnergyExchangePoint is a CommonResponsibilityPoint that identifies the point at which two or more adjacent grid providers establish shared responsibility for the measurement, accounting, and reconciliation of exchanged energy.
Note: The EnergyExchangePoint represents the inter-operator interface used for energy measurement and energy accounting (including settlement-relevant quantities where applicable). It is the reference point at which the participating grid providers define and apply their agreed responsibilities for metering data, data quality, validation, and exchange processes.
An EnergyExchangePoint may also be used as the reference for operational coordination requirements related to the exchange (for example observability/telemetry requirements, agreed transfer capability constraints, or coordination of switching and outage conditions), without changing its primary purpose as the responsibility point for energy measurement and accounting.

EnergyResourceGroupCapacity.description:
An aggregation of energy resources having common energy characteristics for which installed, available, or effective capacity is represented.

Note: EnergyResourceGroupCapacity groups energy resources for capacity modelling, forecasting, scenario analysis and aggregation. The group may be characterised by an energy kind, energy source, technology, location, scenario, weather condition or other modelling context.
The aggregated capacity may be represented by static values or by time-series values describing forecast, scheduled, actual or hindcast conditions. An EnergyComponent represents the part of an aggregated value associated with a particular underlying unit or resource. The aggregated value of the EnergyResourceGroupCapacity may therefore be distributed among its associated EnergyComponents, for example in proportion to the capability of the corresponding units or according to an ordered block-based allocation.
Weather or other environmental information may be referenced where it is relevant to the capacity or availability of the grouped resources/

EnergyResourceGroupCapacity.ClimateZone.description: The climate zone for the energy group.

EnergyResourceGroupCapacity.EnergyResour.description: The energy resource type represented by the aggregated capacity group.

EnergyResourceGroupCapacity.SchedulingAr.description: The scheduling area that has this energy group.

EnergyResourceGroupCapacity.normalAavail.description: The normal ratio (in percent) between the effective available capacity and the installed capacity over a defined time interval. For weather-dependent resources, the value reflects climate-driven availability as derived from meteorological or hydrological conditions.

EnergyResourceGroupCapacity.normalAvaila.description: The weather or condition-dependent active power capacity that is realistically available for operation at a given time. This value reflects normal reduction due to climatic, hydrological, or operational constraints.

EnergyResourceGroupCapacity.normalCapaci.description:
The normal relative weighting used to allocate an aggregate capacity requirement to this energy resource group.

Note: The value provides the default weighting for top-down capacity allocation when a more specific `capacityAllocationFactor` is not provided. The factor is relative to the factors of other applicable energy resource groups and is not required to represent a percentage or to sum to 1 across the groups. The allocation algorithm may normalize the applicable factors and take account of availability, existing capacity and other modelling constraints.

EnergyResourceGroupCapacity.normalInstal.description: The nominal installed active power capacity of the energy type, independent of weather or normal operating conditions. This is the maximum technical power rating under standard design assumptions and optimum operation condition.

EnergyResourceGroupCapacity.normalPartic.description: Normal participation factor for the power group in relation to scheduling area. Must be a positive value.

EnergyResourceGroupCapacity.scenarioCode.description: Code identifying the study, scenario, or modelling configuration from which the capacity or availability values are derived. Examples include TYNDP scenario identifiers, national estimates, or dataset versions.

EnergyResourceGroupCapacity.scenarioRef.description: Reference to the study, scenario, or modelling configuration from which the capacity or availability values are derived. Examples include TYNDP scenario identifiers, national estimates, or dataset versions.

EnergyResourceGroupCapacity.weatherDatas.description: Code identifying the external weather or climate dataset used to determine availability or effective capacity for weather-dependent resources. Examples include datasets from the Pan-European Climate Database (PECD) or similar climate data services.

Reference to the external weather or climate dataset used to determine availability or effective capacity for weather-dependent resources. Examples include datasets from the Pan-European Climate Database (PECD) or similar climate data services.

EnergyResourceType.description:
A reference classification of an energy resource based on its energy kind, primary energy source and conversion technology.
Note: An energy resource type provides a common classification for forecasting, capacity aggregation, scheduling and reporting. Codes and references may identify entries in external controlled vocabularies, such as the European Energy Certificate System (EECS) energy source and technology classifications. Technical and environmental attributes represent reference or default characteristics used for modelling and reporting and do not represent measurements of an individual resource.
Example: (1) Name = "Solar–Photovoltaic–Thin Film", kind = solar, technologyCode = T010102
(2) Name = "Renewable–Solid–Wood–Unspecified", kind = biomass, energySourceCode = F01010300.

Emission.description: Quantity of emission per fuel heat content.

EnergyResourceType.co2EmissionFactor.description:
The reference carbon dioxide emission factor of the energy resource type.
Note: The value represents a default factor used for modelling or reporting rather than measured emissions from an individual resource.

EnergyResourceType.electricalEfficiency.description:
The reference ratio of electrical energy output to energy input for the energy resource type.
Note: The value represents a default or reference efficiency used for modelling and reporting. It is not necessarily the measured efficiency of an individual resource.
Example: An energy resource type representing a combined-cycle gas turbine may have a reference electrical efficiency of 60 %.

EnergyResourceType.energySourceCode.description:
Code identifying the primary energy source.
Note: The code is assigned by a controlled vocabulary. The identified energy source need not be a combustible fuel; it may represent solar radiation, wind, hydro, ambient heat, biomass or another primary energy source.
Example: F01010300 identifies Renewable–Solid–Wood–Unspecified in the European Energy Certificate System (EECS) energy source classification.

EnergyResourceType.energySourceRef.description:
URI or URN identifying the same primary energy source classification as energySourceCode.
Note:URI or URN identifying the same primary energy source as energySourceCode. The URI may be resolvable (HTTP) or non-resolvable (URN). CIM does not mandate any identification scheme.
Example: https://www.aib-net.org/eecs/F01010300 to point to Renewable–Solid–Wood–Unspecified.

EnergyKind.battery.description: Energy storage based on batteries, capable of charging from and discharging to the electrical system.

EnergyKind.biomass.description: Generation based mainly on biomass fuels of biogenic origin, including solid, liquid and gaseous forms.

EnergyKind.buffer.description: Consumption associated with storage-like buffers where energy can be shifted in time while broadly preserving total energy use.

EnergyKind.chemicalElectrical.description: Conversion from chemical energy carriers to electrical energy, such as fuel cells or combustion of hydrogen-rich fuels.

EnergyKind.consumptionTimeShift.description: Demand that can be shifted in time without significantly changing total energy over a defined period.

EnergyKind.consumptionUnconstrained.description: Modelled demand assuming no explicit network or market constraints, used as an unconstrained reference load.

EnergyKind.consumptionUncontrollable.description: Demand that is not directly controlled and is primarily driven by weather, behaviour or unmanaged processes.

EnergyKind.electricalChemical.description: Conversion from electrical energy into chemical energy carriers, such as electrolysis or power-to-gas.

EnergyKind.fossil.description: Generation based mainly on fossil fuels such as coal, oil, gas or other non-renewable combustible fuels.

EnergyKind.geothermal.description: Generation based on geothermal heat from underground reservoirs.

EnergyKind.hydroPump.description: Pumped-storage hydropower operation where electrical energy is used to pump water to an elevated reservoir.

EnergyKind.hydroReservoir.description: Hydropower based on reservoirs with significant storage, enabling dispatchable generation.

EnergyKind.hydroRunOfRiver.description: Hydropower using natural river flow with little or no storage, where generation mainly follows river discharge.

EnergyKind.marine.description: Generation based on marine energy sources such as tidal or wave power.

EnergyKind.nuclear.description: Generation based on nuclear fission reactors of any type.

EnergyKind.solar.description: Generation or heat production based on solar energy, including photovoltaic and solar thermal technologies.

EnergyKind.waste.description: Generation based on energy recovery from renewable or non-renewable waste streams.

EnergyKind.wind.description: Generation based on wind energy using wind turbines on land or offshore.

EnergyResourceType.kind.description:
The general kind of energy resource.
Note: The value provides a broad functional classification suitable for aggregation and forecasting. More detailed classifications of the energy input and technology are provided by fuelCode, fuelRef, technologyCode and technologyRef.

EnergyResourceType.technologyCode.description:
Code identifying the production, conversion, storage or consumption technology.
Note: The code is assigned by an external controlled vocabulary. For electricity production, the code may identify a technology defined by the European Energy Certificate System (EECS) technology classification.
Example: T010102 identifies Solar–Photovoltaic–Thin Film in the European Energy Certificate System (EECS) technology classification.

EnergyResourceType.technologyRef.description:
URI or URN identifying the same technology classification as technologyCode.
Note: URI or URN identifying the same technology as technologyCode. The URI may be resolvable (HTTP) or non-resolvable (URN). CIM does not mandate any identification scheme.
Example: https://www.aib-net.org/eecs/T010102 to point to Solar–Photovoltaic–Thin Film.

EquivalentACDCConverter.description: An equivalent representation of an AC/DC converter used to model the electrical interaction between an AC network and a DC system, without explicitly modelling internal converter station equipment or DC connectivity. The EquivalentACDCConverter abstracts the behaviour of a DC converter by representing its active and reactive power exchange, control characteristics, and connectivity at the AC and/or DC interface. It is used where a detailed converter model is not exchanged or required. The converter has one AC Terminal and two DC Terminal objects.

ApparentPower.description: Product of the RMS value of the voltage and the RMS value of the current.

ACDCConverter.baseS.description: Base apparent power of the converter pole. The attribute shall be a positive value.

ACDCConverter.maxP.description: Maximum active power limit. The value is overwritten by values of VsCapabilityCurve, if present.

ACDCConverter.maxUdc.description: The maximum voltage on the DC side at which the converter should operate. It is converter’s configuration data used in power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

ACDCConverter.minP.description: Minimum active power limit. The value is overwritten by values of VsCapabilityCurve, if present.

ACDCConverter.minUdc.description: The minimum voltage on the DC side at which the converter should operate. It is converter’s configuration data used in power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

ACDCConverter.ratedUdc.description: Rated converter DC voltage, also called UdN. The attribute shall be a positive value. It is converter’s configuration data used in power flow. For instance a bipolar HVDC link with value  200 kV has a 400kV difference between the dc lines.

EquivalentGeneratingUnit.description: An indivisible set of installations which can generate electrical energy such that the frequency of the generated voltage, the generator speed and the frequency of network voltage are in a constant ratio and thus in synchronism. This is often referred as synchronous power-generating module.

ActivePowerChangeRate.description: Rate of change of active power per time.

GeneratingUnit.lowerRampRate.description: The normal maximum rate the generating unit active power output can be lowered by control actions.

GeneratingUnit.maxEconomicP.description: Maximum high economic active power limit, that should not exceed the maximum operating active power limit.

GeneratingUnit.minEconomicP.description: Low economic active power limit that shall be greater than or equal to the minimum operating active power limit.

GeneratingUnit.minimumOffTime.description: Minimum time interval between unit shutdown and startup.

GeneratingUnit.raiseRampRate.description: The normal maximum rate the generating unit active power output can be raised by control actions.

EquivalentGeneratingUnit.EquivalentPower.description: Equivalent power plant that has this equivalent generating unit.

GeneratingUnit.ScheduleResource.description: The schedule resource that has this generating unit.

GeneratingUnit.coolDownTime.description: Time it takes from a unit shutdown until it is considered cold.

Currency.BMD.description: Bermudian dollar (customarily known as Bermuda dollar).

GeneratingUnit.costCurrency.description: Currency the cost is given in.

GeneratingUnit.maxRampDownCountPerDay.description: Number of times the unit can do ramp down within a calendar day. One ramp down consists of a decrease of a power plant production level from a stable schedule to another regardless of how much time the power plant stays in such stable operating stage.

GeneratingUnit.maxStartupLoad.description: Maximum consumption by the generating unit as part of the startup process.

GeneratingUnit.minimumUpTime.description: The time that a generating unit has to stay running after it has been switched on by the Remedial Action Optimizer.

GeneratingUnit.normalMustRunP.description: Normal minimum active power injection that is needed to meet must-run requirement. This value can be higher or equal to minimum operational limit. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.

ReactivePower.description: Product of RMS value of the voltage and the RMS value of the quadrature component of the current.

GeneratingUnit.normalMustRunQ.description: Normal minimum reactive power injection that is needed to meet must-run requirement. This value can be higher or equal to minimum operational limit. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.

GeneratingUnit.normalParticipationFactor.description:
Participation factor describing the entity part of the active power provided by a collection of entities (e.g. an active power forecast to a collection of entities is divided to each of the member entity according to the participation factor). Must be a positive value.
In the case of a sharing strategy, the distribution is following entities value (V) equals aggregated value (T) divided by sum of participation factors (PF), i.e. V=T/sum(PF). 
In the case of priority strategy, the item with the lowest number gets allocated energy first.

GeneratingUnit.normalShutdownCost.description: The normal shutdown cost incurred for each shutdown of the GeneratingUnit.
